When the server refuses a call with 429, the error says how long to wait. `isRateLimitError` narrows it, and `retryAfter` is the wait in milliseconds, read from the `Retry-After` header:

```ts
import { api, isRateLimitError } from '#api';

let notice = '';

try {
    await api.notes.create({ title: 'Buy milk' });
} catch (error) {
    if (isRateLimitError(error)) {
        const seconds = Math.ceil((error.retryAfter ?? 60_000) / 1000);
        notice = `Too many requests. Try again in ${seconds} seconds.`;
    }
}
```

With retries on, the client waits and sends the call again by itself, once, when the wait is no longer than `maxDelay`, which is five seconds unless you change it. That also applies to writes: a call the rate limit refused never reached your route, so sending it again cannot do the work twice. A longer wait is not sat out, and the error reaches you at once.

The server side, `rateLimit { }` in `install(Svelte)`, is described under [Security](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/security#api-request-guards).

## Testing

### Fixtures for frontend tests

A frontend test should not need the backend running, and writing its answers by hand goes stale. Record them instead. In development, click through the part of the app you want to test, open the [dev panel](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow) and press **Save fixtures**. You get `api-fixtures.json` with every call the page made and what the server answered:

```json
{
    "recorded": "2026-11-16T12:00:00.000Z",
    "calls": [
        { "method": "GET", "path": "/api/notes?page=1", "status": 200, "response": { "items": [] } },
        { "method": "POST", "path": "/api/notes", "status": 201, "request": { "title": "New" }, "response": { "id": 7 } }
    ]
}
```

In a test, let the client answer from that file:

```ts
import { api, apiConfig, fixtureFetch, type ApiFixtures } from '#api';
import recorded from './api-fixtures.json';

apiConfig.fetch = fixtureFetch(recorded satisfies ApiFixtures);

const page = await api.notes.list({ page: 1 });
```

- The calls go through the real generated client, so the test sees typed results, `ApiError` for a recorded 404 and validation errors for a recorded 422, exactly as the app does.
- A call is matched by its method and its path with the query.
- When the same call was recorded more than once, such as a list before and after a create, the answers come back in that order, and the last one repeats.
- A call that was never recorded fails with a message that names it.

**Look before you commit**
Look through the file before you commit it. It holds the bodies as they were sent and received, which can include data you would not put in the repository. Fields marked [`@Sensitive`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/validation#sensitive-fields), such as a password, are saved as `***`. **Clear** in the panel starts a new recording.

## Full examples

### A notes page

A list of notes loaded before the page shows, with a clear error when the server is down, an edit form that creates and updates, and a delete that asks first. The root layout refreshes the page after every write, so the list is never stale.

::: code-group

```ts [+page.ts]
import { error } from '@sveltejs/kit';
import { apiWith, errorMessage } from '#api';
import type { PageLoad } from './$types';

export const prerender = false;
export const ssr = false;

export const load: PageLoad = async (event) => {
    const api = apiWith(event);
    try {
        const [notes, stats] = await Promise.all([api.notes.list(), api.stats.list()]);
        return { notes, stats };
    } catch (failure) {
        error(503, errorMessage(failure));
    }
};
```

```svelte [+page.svelte]
<script lang="ts">
    import { api, errorMessage, field, NoteInput, type Note } from '#api';
    import { formState } from '#lib/api/form-state.svelte.ts';
    import { confirmed } from '#lib/ktor-svelte/confirm.ts';
    import { routes } from '#routes';
    import type { PageProps } from './$types';

    let { data }: PageProps = $props();

    const form = formState<NoteInput>(NoteInput.empty(), { validate: NoteInput.validate });
    let editing = $state<Note | undefined>(undefined);
    let problem = $state('');

    function edit(note: Note) {
        editing = note;
        form.reset({ title: note.title, body: note.body, tags: note.tags });
    }

    function startOver() {
        editing = undefined;
        form.reset(NoteInput.empty());
    }

    async function save(event: SubmitEvent) {
        event.preventDefault();
        const target = editing;
        const saved = await form.submit((draft) => (target ? api.notes.update(target.id, draft) : api.notes.create(draft)));
        if (saved) startOver();
    }

    async function remove(note: Note) {
        problem = '';
        try {
            await confirmed(`Delete "${note.title}"?`, () => api.notes.delete(note.id), {
                details: 'It cannot be restored.',
                confirm: 'Delete',
                danger: true
            });
        } catch (error) {
            problem = errorMessage(error);
        }
    }
</script>

<h1>Notes ({data.stats.total})</h1>

{#if problem}<p role="alert">{problem}</p>{/if}

<ul>
    {#each data.notes as note (note.id)}
        <li>
            <a href={routes.notesId({ id: note.id })}>{note.title}</a>
            <button type="button" onclick={() => edit(note)}>Edit</button>
            <button type="button" onclick={() => remove(note)}>Delete</button>
        </li>
    {:else}
        <li>No notes yet.</li>
    {/each}
</ul>

<form onsubmit={save}>
    <h2>{editing ? 'Edit note' : 'New note'}</h2>
    <input aria-label="Title" bind:value={form.draft.title} use:field={{ bounds: NoteInput.bounds.title, errors: form.errors.title }} />
    <textarea aria-label="Body" bind:value={form.draft.body}></textarea>
    {#if form.message}<p role="alert">{form.message}</p>{/if}
    <button disabled={form.submitting}>{editing ? 'Save' : 'Create'}</button>
    {#if editing}<button type="button" onclick={startOver}>Cancel</button>{/if}
</form>
```

```svelte no-check [+layout.svelte]
<script lang="ts">
    import { refreshAll } from '$app/navigation';
    import { apiConfig } from '#api';

    let { children } = $props();

    apiConfig.onWrite = () => void refreshAll();
</script>

{@render children()}
```

```kotlin no-check [Routes.kt]
fun Route.noteRoutes(store: NoteStore) {
    resource<Note, Int>("/api/notes") {
        missing<Problem> { Problem("That note does not exist.") }
        list<NoteQuery> { query -> store.list(query.search, query.tag) }
        create<NoteInput> { input -> store.create(input) }
        get { id -> store.find(id) }
        update<NoteInput> { id, input -> store.update(id, input) }
        delete { id -> store.delete(id) }
    }
    get("/api/stats") {
        call.respond(store.stats())
    }
}
```

What each part does:

- The load uses `apiWith(event)`, so SvelteKit tracks the calls and `refreshAll` reruns them after a write.
- When the server cannot be reached, `error(503, ...)` shows your error page with a readable message instead of a broken list.
- `formState` runs `NoteInput.validate` before sending, puts a 422 from the server into `form.errors`, and anything else into `form.message`. With [toasts](#show-errors-automatically) on, the user also sees other failures without any markup.
- `confirmed` asks before the delete. With DaisyUI the modal shows a failure itself; without it the call rejects and the page shows `problem`.

### A search box

Results follow the input while the visitor types. `latest` drops answers to older terms, and the short pause keeps the server from a request per keystroke.

```svelte [SearchNotes.svelte]
<script lang="ts">
    import { api, errorMessage, isAbortError, latest, type Note } from '#api';

    const search = latest(api.notes.list);

    let term = $state('');
    let results = $state<Note[]>([]);
    let problem = $state('');
    let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;

    function onInput() {
        clearTimeout(timer);
        timer = setTimeout(run, 200);
    }

    async function run() {
        problem = '';
        try {
            results = await search({ search: term.trim() || undefined }, { silent: true });
        } catch (error) {
            if (!isAbortError(error)) problem = errorMessage(error);
        }
    }
</script>

<input type="search" placeholder="Search notes" aria-label="Search notes" bind:value={term} oninput={onInput} />

{#if problem}<p role="alert">{problem}</p>{/if}

<ul>
    {#each results as note (note.id)}
        <li>{note.title}</li>
    {:else}
        <li>Nothing found.</li>
    {/each}
</ul>
```

`silent: true` keeps failed searches out of the toasts, since the component shows its own message.

### A paged table

A table that loads 20 rows at a time behind a "Load more" button, on top of a paged route.

::: code-group

```kotlin [Routes.kt]
routing {
    getPage<Note>("/api/notes/feed", defaultLimit = 20) { request -> store.page(request.cursor, request.limit) }
}
```

```svelte [NoteTable.svelte]
<script lang="ts">
    import { onMount } from 'svelte';
    import { api, errorMessage, IsoDateTime, type Note } from '#api';

    let rows = $state<Note[]>([]);
    let cursor: string | undefined;
    let done = $state(false);
    let loading = $state(false);
    let problem = $state('');

    async function more() {
        loading = true;
        problem = '';
        try {
            const page = await api.notes.getFeed({ cursor, limit: '20' });
            rows = [...rows, ...page.items];
            cursor = page.next ?? undefined;
            done = cursor === undefined;
        } catch (error) {
            problem = errorMessage(error);
        } finally {
            loading = false;
        }
    }

    onMount(more);
</script>

<table>
    <thead>
        <tr><th>Title</th><th>Tags</th><th>Created</th></tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
        {#each rows as note (note.id)}
            <tr>
                <td>{note.title}</td>
                <td>{note.tags.join(', ')}</td>
                <td>{IsoDateTime.parse(note.createdAt).toLocaleDateString()}</td>
            </tr>
        {/each}
    </tbody>
</table>

{#if problem}<p role="alert">{problem}</p>{/if}
{#if !done}
    <button type="button" disabled={loading} onclick={more}>{loading ? 'Loading...' : 'Load more'}</button>
{/if}
```

For a ready-made table with sorting and paging, see [DataTable](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries#datatable) and [A table without the code](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/pagination#a-table-without-the-code).

## Use cases

- A page that needs data before it shows: [in load functions](#in-load-functions).
- A form: [typed errors](#typed-errors) with [validation](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/validation), or the [form helper](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/validation#form-state).
- Error handling for the common case without code: [show errors automatically](#show-errors-automatically).
- Deleting or other risky actions: [ask before a call](#ask-before-a-call).
- Mobile users and flaky networks: [timeouts](#timeouts), [retries](#retries) and [writes that are safe to send twice](#writes-that-are-safe-to-send-twice).
- Long lists: [paged lists](#paged-lists). Live data: [event streams](#event-streams).
- Support tickets: [request IDs](#request-ids).
- Frontend tests without a backend: [fixtures](#fixtures-for-frontend-tests).

## Good to know

- The client always speaks JSON. See [Transport](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/transport).
- Calls with their own `headers`, `fetch` or `signal` are never [shared](#share-identical-requests), and calls with their own `headers` or `signal` are never [prefetched](#prefetch-on-hover).
- `X-Request-Id`, `X-Time-Zone` and `Idempotency-Key` are only sent to your own origin, never to a `baseUrl` on another host.
- A 401 goes to `apiConfig.onUnauthorized` when you set it. Otherwise a 401 from your own origin sends the visitor to the [login page](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/auth#the-login-page), when one is set.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/validation

# Validation

One set of rules for the server and the browser, with errors per field. You write the rules once in Kotlin; the server enforces them on every request, and the generated client checks the same rules in the browser with the same messages.

<Badge type="tip" text="Ktor plugin" /> <Badge type="warning" text="Generated client" />

## Quick start

Put simple bounds on the properties with Ktor's `JsonSchema` annotations, and any other rule on the class itself by implementing `Validated`:

```kotlin
import io.ktor.openapi.JsonSchema

@Serializable
data class NoteInput(
    @JsonSchema.MaxLength(80)
    val title: String,
    val body: String = "",
) : Validated {
    override fun Validator.rules() {
        check(::title, title.isNotBlank()) { "A note needs a title." }
    }
}

post("/api/notes") {
    val input = call.receive<NoteInput>()
    call.respond(HttpStatusCode.Created, store.create(input))
}
```

When something fails, the route never runs, and the client gets a 422 with an error list per field, in one standard shape that `isValidationError` understands:

```json
{ "message": "Validation failed", "fields": { "title": ["A note needs a title."] } }
```

## Where the rules run

Both kinds of rule run on every `call.receive` of that class, in every route:

- for nested classes, lists, map values and sealed subtypes too
- for every item when you receive a `List` or `Map` of such classes
- for a [query class](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#query-parameters-as-a-class) read with `call.query<T>()`
- for the result of a [`Patch<T>`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#changing-some-fields)

| Rule | Server | Browser (`validate()`) |
|---|---|---|
| `JsonSchema` annotations | Yes | Yes, same messages |
| `@Trim`, `@Lowercase`, `@EmptyAsNull` | Yes | No, the text is checked as typed |
| `Validated.rules()` | Yes | No, the errors arrive with the 422 |
| `validate { }` in a route | Yes | No, the errors arrive with the 422 |
| `fieldCheck` routes | Yes | Asked while typing, through [`formState`](#checks-only-the-server-can-make) |

## Rules on properties

| Annotation | Checks | Message |
|---|---|---|
| `@JsonSchema.MinLength(n)`, `@JsonSchema.MaxLength(n)` | Length of a string | `Must be at most 80 characters.` |
| `@JsonSchema.Minimum(x)`, `@JsonSchema.Maximum(x)` | A number, `exclusive = true` for a strict bound | `Must be at least 1.` |
| `@JsonSchema.Pattern(regex)` | A string contains a match | `Must match ^[a-z]+$.` |

```kotlin
@Serializable
data class Product(
    @JsonSchema.Pattern("^[A-Z]{3}-[0-9]{4}$")
    val sku: String,
    @JsonSchema.Minimum(0.0, exclusive = true)
    val price: Double,
    @JsonSchema.Minimum(1.0) @JsonSchema.Maximum(99.0)
    val quantity: Int,
)
```

The messages for these bounds are English and are the same in the browser and on the server. For another language, or friendlier wording than `Must match ^[a-z]+$.`, write the rule yourself with `check` and your own text.

## Ready-made rules

For the values every app checks, use a preset instead of writing a pattern. Each one has a friendly message, and the server and the browser use the same pattern and the same text:

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.Rule

@Serializable
data class AccountInput(
    @Rule.Email val email: String,
    @Rule.StrongPassword val password: String,
    @Rule.WebAddress val homepage: String? = null,
    @Rule.Phone val phone: String? = null,
    @Rule.Slug val handle: String,
)
```

| Annotation | Accepts | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@Rule.Email` | `name@example.com`: something, `@`, a domain with a dot, no spaces | `Must be an email address, such as name@example.com.` |
| `@Rule.WebAddress` | `http://` or `https://`, a host with a dot, no spaces | `Must be a web address that starts with http:// or https://.` |
| `@Rule.Phone` | 6 to 20 digits, spaces and `+ ( ) . / -`, such as `+49 30 1234567` or `(030) 123-45` | `Must be a phone number, such as +49 30 1234567.` |
| `@Rule.Slug` | lowercase letters and digits with single dashes, such as `hello-world-2` | `Must be lowercase letters and digits, with single dashes between words.` |
| `@Rule.StrongPassword` | at least 10 characters with a lowercase letter, an uppercase letter and a digit | `Must have at least 10 characters, a lowercase letter, an uppercase letter and a digit.` |

- A preset checks a value that is there. Combine it with `@JsonSchema.MinLength(1)` to also refuse an empty text, and make the property nullable to allow leaving it out.
- In the OpenAPI document each preset is the property's `format` (`email`, `uri`, `phone`, `slug`, `strong-password`); that is how the generated `validate()` knows which check to run.
- The patterns are deliberately loose. An email that passes can still bounce; confirm addresses by sending a mail.
- For your own wording or another language, write the rule with `check` in [`Validated.rules()`](#rules-on-the-class) instead.

## Rules on the class

Anything the annotations cannot say, such as a rule over two fields, goes into `Validated.rules()`:

```kotlin
@Serializable
data class Booking(
    val from: String,
    val until: String,
    val guests: Int,
) : Validated {
    override fun Validator.rules() {
        check(::until, until >= from) { "The stay has to end after it starts." }
        check(::guests, guests in 1..8) { "Between 1 and 8 guests." }
    }
}
```

- `check(::title, condition) { message }` adds the message when the condition is false.
- It names the field from the property, so renaming it in the IDE keeps the error in sync. If the property has a different `@SerialName`, pass the name as a string instead: `check("api_key", ...)`.
- Every failed check is collected, so the user sees all problems at once.

### Error paths

Errors use the JSON name, with paths for nested values:

| Where | Path |
|---|---|
| A field | `title` |
| A field of an item in a list | `lines[1].sku` |
| A field of a map value | `prices[eur].amount` |
| A field of an item of a received list | `[0].sku` |

## Rules inside a route

For a rule that depends on the route, such as comparing against a database, call `validate { check(...) { ... } }` inside the route. It answers the same way, with a 422 and the errors per field:

```kotlin
@Serializable
data class CouponInput(val code: String)

post("/api/coupons/redeem") {
    val input = call.receive<CouponInput>()
    validate {
        check("code", input.code.startsWith("WELCOME")) { "That code does not exist." }
    }
    call.respond(HttpStatusCode.NoContent)
}
```

**StatusPages**
`validate` and the other rules throw a `ValidationException`, which ktor-svelte turns into the 422. If you use Ktor's `StatusPages` with a handler for all exceptions, it runs first, so let `ValidationException` through.

## Cleaning up input

People paste text with spaces around it and type their email address with capitals. Say once, on the field, how it should arrive, and no route cleans up strings by hand:

```kotlin
@Serializable
data class SignUp(
    @Trim @Lowercase
    val email: String,
    @Trim
    @JsonSchema.MinLength(1)
    val name: String,
    @Trim @EmptyAsNull
    val company: String? = null,
)
```

| Annotation | What arrives in the route |
|---|---|
| `@Trim` | The text without whitespace at both ends |
| `@Lowercase` | The text in lowercase, independent of the server's locale |
| `@EmptyAsNull` | `null` when the text is empty, which is what a form sends for a field left blank. The property has to be nullable |

- They are applied in that order, so `@Trim @EmptyAsNull` turns a field of only spaces into `null`.
- This happens when the JSON body is received, before the bounds and your `Validated` rules run, so `@Trim @JsonSchema.MinLength(1)` refuses a name of only spaces without a rule of your own.
- On a `List<String>` or a `Map<String, String>` they apply to every item or value.
- They are found in nested classes, in lists of classes, in sealed subtypes with the default `type` discriminator, and on the property of a value class, so `value class Email(@Trim @Lowercase val value: String)` is clean wherever it is used.

**Server only**
Only JSON request bodies are cleaned up, not query parameters, and the browser does not apply them: `validate()` in the generated TypeScript checks the text as typed. That only matters for a value that is valid after trimming but not before, which the server then accepts.

## Sensitive fields

The development tools show a lot of what travels between browser and server, and some of it should not be shown: a password, a token, an API key. Mark such a field once:

```kotlin
@Serializable
data class Login(
    val email: String,
    @Sensitive
    val password: String,
)
```

From then on the field's value is replaced by `***` wherever ktor-svelte itself displays or stores it:

- in the `curl` command the [dev panel](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow) copies
- in the [fixtures](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#fixtures-for-frontend-tests) it saves, for request and response bodies
- in browser console output that is forwarded to the dev log
- in the request list and the slow call log, for a query parameter of that name

It works for requests and for responses, in nested classes too, and by the JSON name of the field, so `@SerialName("api_key")` masks `api_key`.

**Two things to know**
- Masking goes by name: once `password` is marked in one class, every field and query parameter called `password` is masked in those places, in any class. So give a sensitive field a telling name, not `value` or `next`.
- It changes nothing about your API: the field is received and returned as before. Keeping a value out of a response is still done by not putting it into the response class.

## In the browser

With `generateTs`, the same annotations end up in OpenAPI and in the generated TypeScript, so a form gets the bounds without asking the server, and `validate()` checks a value in the browser with the same messages the server sends:

```ts
import { NoteInput } from '#api';

const problems = NoteInput.validate(draft);
const titleBounds = NoteInput.bounds.title;
```

How `bounds` and `validate()` are generated, and which bounds get `required`, is in [Generated TypeScript](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/typescript#types-and-forms).

### Errors next to inputs

`use:field` puts the bounds on an input and shows its errors right after it, with `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` set for screen readers. Pass the same errors whether they come from `validate()` or from a 422:

```svelte
<input bind:value={draft.title} use:field={{ bounds: NoteInput.bounds.title, errors: errors.title, errorClass: 'text-error' }} />
```

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `bounds` | The HTML attributes from `bounds`, such as `maxlength` |
| `errors` | The messages for this field. The message disappears when they are empty |
| `errorClass` | The class of the message. Defaults to `field-error` |
| `describedBy` | The id of the input's own hint, which stays in `aria-describedby` next to the error |

The message is a `<p role="alert">`.

With `libraries { components() }`, the generated [`<Field>`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries#field) wraps this action together with the label and a hint.

## Form state

Every form needs the same few variables: the values being edited, whether they changed, whether a submit is running, and the errors that came back. `formState` holds them, so a form is its inputs and one function:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { api, field, NoteInput } from '#api';
    import { formState } from '#lib/api/form-state.svelte.ts';

    const form = formState<NoteInput>(NoteInput.empty(), { validate: NoteInput.validate, resetOnSuccess: true });

    async function create() {
        const note = await form.submit((draft) => api.notes.create(draft));
        if (note) console.log('created', note.id);
    }
</script>

<form onsubmit={(event) => { event.preventDefault(); void create(); }}>
    <input bind:value={form.draft.title} use:field={{ bounds: NoteInput.bounds.title, errors: form.errors.title }} />
    <p role="alert">{form.message}</p>
    <button disabled={form.submitting}>Create</button>
    <button type="button" disabled={!form.dirty} onclick={() => form.reset()}>Discard</button>
</form>
```

| | |
|---|---|
| `form.draft` | The values being edited, deeply reactive, so `bind:value={form.draft.title}` works |
| `form.dirty` | `true` while the draft differs from the last saved values |
| `form.submitting` | `true` while `submit` waits for the server. A second `submit` in that time does nothing |
| `form.errors` | Errors per field, from `validate`, from a 422 answer and from [checks](#checks-only-the-server-can-make). Hand them to `use:field` |
| `form.error`, `form.message` | Any other failure of the last submit, and its text for the user. `message` is empty when there is none |
| `form.checking` | `true` while a [check](#checks-only-the-server-can-make) waits for its answer |
| `form.reset()` | Back to the last saved values, with the errors cleared. `form.reset(values)` makes `values` the saved ones, such as after loading a record |
| `form.submitChanges(send)` | Like `submit`, but `send` gets only the changed fields as a `Patch<T>`, and is not called when nothing changed |
| `form.submit(send)` | Runs `validate` first and stops on errors without calling the server. Otherwise calls `send` with a plain copy of the draft and returns its result, or `undefined` when it failed |
| `form.conflict`, `form.takeTheirs()`, `form.keepMine()` | After a [version conflict](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#two-people-one-record): the other person's record, reset to it, or take over its version so the next submit goes through |

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `validate` | none | Checks the draft before sending, such as `NoteInput.validate` |
| `resetOnSuccess` | `false` | Empties the form after a successful submit |
| `checks` | none | [Check routes](#checks-only-the-server-can-make) per field |
| `checkDelay` | `300` | Milliseconds of quiet typing before a check is asked |
| `focusErrors` | `true` | After a submit that fails validation, in the browser or with a 422, moves focus to the first invalid field |

- After a successful submit the sent values are the saved ones, so the form is no longer dirty. That suits an edit form. For a form that creates something, `resetOnSuccess: true` empties it again.
- `submit` never throws: a failed call ends up in `errors` or `error`. The failure still reaches `apiConfig.onError`, so with [toasts](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#show-errors-automatically) on, the user sees it without any markup of yours.
- The helper uses runes, so it is a module of its own and not part of `#api`.
- The draft should be plain data, the kind that goes into a JSON body. `dirty` compares it as JSON.

### What changed

Each field knows whether it differs from the saved value. Use it for a marker beside the field, and for a summary of the changes before saving:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import Field from '#components/Field.svelte';
</script>

<Field label="Title" bind:value={form.draft.title} changed={form.changed('title')} />

{#if form.dirty}
    <ul>
        {#each form.changes as change (change.field)}
            <li>{change.field}: {String(change.from)} -> {String(change.to)}</li>
        {/each}
    </ul>
{/if}
```

| Name | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `form.changed('title')` | `true` while the field differs from the saved value; reactive |
| `form.changes` | every changed field as `{ field, from, to }`, in the order of the draft's fields |

- Fields are compared as JSON, so a list or a nested object counts as changed when anything inside it changed, and changing a value back removes it from the list.
- After a successful submit the sent values are the saved ones, so `changes` is empty again.
- `<Field changed>` shows a small dot after the label, announced as "Changed"; pass a text instead of `true` for another language, such as `changed={form.changed('title') && m.fieldChanged()}`.

### Send only what changed

For a big record where only one field was edited, send just the changed fields. `submitChanges` validates the whole draft like `submit`, then calls your function with a [`Patch<T>`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#changing-some-fields) of the changed fields only:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { api, NoteInput } from '#api';
    import { formState } from '#lib/api/form-state.svelte.ts';

    const form = formState<NoteInput>({ title: note.title, body: note.body, tags: note.tags }, { validate: NoteInput.validate });

    async function save(event: SubmitEvent) {
        event.preventDefault();
        await form.submitChanges((changes) => api.notes.patch(note.id, changes));
    }
</script>
```

- When only the title changed, the body is `{"title": "Oat milk"}`.
- When nothing changed, your function is not called and the result is `undefined`, so a double click on "Save" sends nothing.
- Fields are compared as JSON against the saved values, the same way as [`form.changes`](#what-changed). A field set to `undefined` is sent as `null`, which the server's `Patch<T>` reads as "clear it".
- Errors, conflicts and the saved state work exactly as with `submit`.

### Forms in several steps

`formWizard` splits one form into steps. Each step is checked against the same `validate()` before you can move on, the progress survives a reload, and the whole object is sent once at the end:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { api, Signup } from '#api';
    import Field from '#components/Field.svelte';
    import { formWizard } from '#lib/api/form-state.svelte.ts';

    const wizard = formWizard<Signup>(Signup.empty(), {
        validate: Signup.validate,
        steps: [['name', 'email'], ['company', 'role'], ['password']],
        keep: 'signup'
    });

    async function finish(event: SubmitEvent) {
        event.preventDefault();
        if (!wizard.last) return void wizard.next();
        await wizard.submit((draft) => api.signups.create(draft));
    }
</script>

<p>Step {wizard.step + 1} of {wizard.count}</p>
<form novalidate onsubmit={finish}>
    {#if wizard.step === 0}
        <Field id="name" label="Name" bind:value={wizard.draft.name} errors={wizard.errors.name} />
        <Field id="email" label="Email" bind:value={wizard.draft.email} errors={wizard.errors.email} />
    {:else if wizard.step === 1}
        <Field id="company" label="Company" bind:value={wizard.draft.company} errors={wizard.errors.company} />
        <Field id="role" label="Role" bind:value={wizard.draft.role} errors={wizard.errors.role} />
    {:else}
        <Field id="password" label="Password" type="password" bind:value={wizard.draft.password} errors={wizard.errors.password} />
    {/if}
    {#if !wizard.first}<button type="button" onclick={wizard.back}>Back</button>{/if}
    <button disabled={wizard.submitting}>{wizard.last ? 'Create account' : 'Next'}</button>
</form>
```

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `steps` | The fields of each step, in order. Errors of a nested path such as `address.city` or `lines[2].sku` belong to the step of `address` or `lines` |
| `keep` | A `sessionStorage` key. The step and the draft are kept there, so a reload or a back button does not lose the progress; it is cleared after a successful submit or a `reset()` |
| `validate`, `checks`, `focusErrors`, ... | As for [`formState`](#form-state) |

| Name | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `wizard.step`, `count`, `first`, `last` | Where you are |
| `wizard.reached` | The furthest step reached; `goTo` cannot jump past it |
| `wizard.fields` | The fields of the current step |
| `wizard.next()` | Checks the current step's fields only; shows and focuses their errors and returns `false`, or moves on and returns `true` |
| `wizard.back()`, `wizard.goTo(n)` | Move back, or to any step already reached |
| `wizard.submit(send)` | Checks everything and sends once. When an earlier step is invalid, or the server answers 422 for one of its fields, it jumps back to the first step with an error |

Everything else of a `formState` (`draft`, `errors`, `dirty`, `changes`, `submitChanges`, `reset`, ...) works on the wizard too. `form.setErrors(errors)` sets the shown errors by hand, on any form.

### Focus the first error

When a submit fails validation, `formState` waits for the error messages to appear and then moves focus to the first field marked invalid, scrolled to the middle of the screen. Keyboard and screen reader users land right on the problem, and on a long form nobody has to scroll to find it.

- It works with every field that uses `use:field` or the generated [components](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components), since they mark invalid fields with `aria-invalid="true"`.
- It happens for the browser's own `validate()` and for a 422 from the server alike.
- Turn it off with `focusErrors: false`, and call `form.focusFirstError()` yourself when you want it at another moment.
- For long forms, add an [ErrorSummary](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#errorsummary) above the button: a list of every problem, each a link that jumps to its field.

### An edit form

For a record that already exists, start with its values and save with `update`:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { api, field, NoteInput } from '#api';
    import { formState } from '#lib/api/form-state.svelte.ts';

    const form = formState<NoteInput>({ title: note.title, body: note.body, tags: note.tags }, { validate: NoteInput.validate });
</script>

<form onsubmit={(event) => { event.preventDefault(); void form.submit((draft) => api.notes.update(note.id, draft)); }}>
    <input bind:value={form.draft.title} use:field={{ bounds: NoteInput.bounds.title, errors: form.errors.title }} />
    <button disabled={!form.dirty || form.submitting}>Save</button>
</form>
```

## Checks only the server can make

Whether an email address is taken, or a coupon code exists, cannot be decided in the browser. Without help, the visitor learns it after sending the whole form. A check route answers the question for one value:

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.fieldCheck

routing {
    fieldCheck("/api/checks/email") { email ->
        if (email == "ada@example.com") "That email address already has an account." else null
    }
}
```

- The block gets the value and returns what is wrong with it, or null when it is fine.
- It runs inside the route, so `call` is there for the current user or the language.
- The route is a `GET` with the value in the `value` query parameter, never cached, and part of the generated client like any other, such as `api.checks.getEmail({ value })`.
- An empty value is never passed to the block, and a value longer than 1000 characters is refused with a 400.

`formState` asks it while the visitor types:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { api, field, Registration } from '#api';
    import { formState } from '#lib/api/form-state.svelte.ts';

    const form = formState<Registration>(Registration.empty(), {
        validate: Registration.validate,
        checks: { email: api.checks.getEmail }
    });
</script>

<input type="email" bind:value={form.draft.email} use:field={{ errors: form.errors.email }} />
```

- The call waits until typing has paused for 300 ms (`checkDelay`), and an answer that arrives for an older value is dropped.
- The answer is part of `form.errors.email`, next to the errors from `validate` and from a 422, so it shows up the same way with no extra markup.
- While a check says no, `form.submit` does not send. `form.checking` is true while an answer is awaited.
- An empty value and the value the form started with are not checked. A profile form does not tell its owner that their own email is taken.
- A check that fails, because the server is unreachable or answers with an error, says nothing. The real answer comes when the form is sent.

**Keep the rule in the route**
A check does not replace the rule in the route that saves: two people can pass the check at the same moment. Keep the rule there and treat the check as the earlier, friendlier message.

A check route also tells anyone who asks whether a value exists. For email addresses that reveals who has an account, so put the route under a [rate limit](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#rate-limits), as you would the sign-in route.

## Full example

A registration form: the email is cleaned up and checked while typing, the password is masked in the dev tools, two passwords must match, and the route checks the email once more when the form is sent.

::: code-group

```kotlin no-check [Registration.kt]
@Serializable
data class Registration(
    @Trim @Lowercase
    @JsonSchema.Pattern("^[^@ ]+@[^@ ]+$")
    val email: String,
    @Trim
    @JsonSchema.MinLength(1)
    @JsonSchema.MaxLength(60)
    val name: String,
    @Sensitive
    @JsonSchema.MinLength(12)
    val password: String,
    @Sensitive
    val repeatPassword: String,
    @Trim @EmptyAsNull
    val company: String? = null,
) : Validated {
    override fun Validator.rules() {
        check(::repeatPassword, repeatPassword == password) { "The passwords do not match." }
    }
}

fun Route.registrationRoutes(accounts: Accounts) {
    fieldCheck("/api/checks/email") { email ->
        if (accounts.isTaken(email)) "That email address already has an account." else null
    }

    post("/api/register") {
        val input = call.receive<Registration>()
        validate {
            check(input::email, !accounts.isTaken(input.email)) { "That email address already has an account." }
        }
        val account = accounts.create(input)
        call.toast("Welcome, ${account.name}!", ToastKind.Success)
        call.respond(HttpStatusCode.Created, account)
    }
}
```

```svelte no-check [+page.svelte]
<script lang="ts">
    import { goto } from '$app/navigation';
    import { api, field, Registration } from '#api';
    import { formState } from '#lib/api/form-state.svelte.ts';

    const form = formState<Registration>(Registration.empty(), {
        validate: Registration.validate,
        checks: { email: api.checks.getEmail }
    });

    async function register(event: SubmitEvent) {
        event.preventDefault();
        const account = await form.submit((draft) => api.register.create(draft));
        if (account) await goto('/welcome');
    }
</script>

<form onsubmit={register}>
    <label>
        Email
        <input type="email" bind:value={form.draft.email} use:field={{ bounds: Registration.bounds.email, errors: form.errors.email }} />
    </label>
    <label>
        Name
        <input bind:value={form.draft.name} use:field={{ bounds: Registration.bounds.name, errors: form.errors.name }} />
    </label>
    <label>
        Password
        <input type="password" bind:value={form.draft.password} use:field={{ bounds: Registration.bounds.password, errors: form.errors.password }} />
    </label>
    <label>
        Repeat password
        <input type="password" bind:value={form.draft.repeatPassword} use:field={{ errors: form.errors.repeatPassword }} />
    </label>
    <label>
        Company (optional)
        <input bind:value={form.draft.company} />
    </label>

    {#if form.message}<p role="alert">{form.message}</p>{/if}
    <button disabled={form.submitting || form.checking}>Create account</button>
</form>
```

What happens where:

- In the browser, `Registration.validate` checks the pattern and the lengths on every submit, and `api.checks.getEmail` asks about the email while the visitor types.
- On the server, `@Trim @Lowercase` clean up the email before anything else, the annotations and `rules()` run on `call.receive`, and `validate { }` checks the email once more, because two people can pass the check at the same moment.
- Every error lands in `form.errors`, whichever side found it, and `use:field` shows it next to the input.
- The passwords show as `***` in the dev panel, the fixtures and the logs.

## Use cases

- Any form that sends a body: annotations plus [`formState`](#form-state).
- Rules over two fields, such as dates or passwords: [`Validated.rules()`](#rules-on-the-class).
- Rules that need the database: [`validate { }` in the route](#rules-inside-a-route), with a [check route](#checks-only-the-server-can-make) for early feedback.
- Email addresses, names and optional text from forms: [cleaning up input](#cleaning-up-input).
- Passwords, tokens and keys: [sensitive fields](#sensitive-fields).
- Two people editing one record: [version conflicts](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#two-people-one-record).

## Good to know

- The 422 has one shape everywhere: `{ "message": "Validation failed", "fields": { ... } }`. `isValidationError` in the client recognises it.
- Annotation messages are English. Write a `check` with your own text for other languages.
- Write patterns with `^` and `$`: the browser matches the whole value, the server looks for a match inside it.
- Classes without annotations or rules are not checked, and get no `validate()` in TypeScript.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/routes

# Typed routes

Every page in `src/routes` becomes a typed constant in TypeScript and in Kotlin, so a link or a redirect to a page that does not exist fails to compile. On top of that come menus, titles, breadcrumbs, link previews, checks for string links and dead links, and tasks that create, rename and scaffold pages.

<Badge type="info" text="Gradle" /> <Badge type="warning" text="Generated client" />

## Quick start

Turn it on in `build.gradle.kts` and run `./gradlew svelteSync`:

```kotlin
svelte {
    libraries {
        routes()
    }
}
```

Then link to pages by name:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { routes } from '#routes';

    let { note } = $props();
</script>

<a href={routes.home()}>Home</a>
<a href={routes.notesId({ id: note.id })}>{note.title}</a>
```

## What counts as a page

- A folder is a page when it holds a `+page.svelte`, `+page.ts`, `+page.js` or `+page.server.ts`.
- Route groups such as `(app)` are left out of the path.
- Layouts alone are not pages.

| Setting in `routes { }` | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `dir` | `src/routes` in your frontend | Where your routes live |

```kotlin
svelte {
    libraries {
        routes { dir = layout.projectDirectory.dir("frontend/src/pages") }
    }
}
```

## Overview

| You want to | Use |
|---|---|
| Link to a page in Svelte | [`routes.notesId({ id })`](#in-svelte) |
| Highlight the open page in a menu | [`isActive`, `ariaCurrent`](#marking-the-open-page-in-a-menu) |
| Redirect to a page from Kotlin | [`FrontendRoutes.notesId(id)`](#in-kotlin) |
| Build a menu, titles and breadcrumbs | [`_nav`, `nav`, `pageTitle`, `breadcrumbs`](#menu-titles-and-breadcrumbs) |
| Nice previews when a link is shared | [`description` and `image` in `_nav`](#link-previews) |
| Rename a page and every link to it | [`svelteRename`](#renaming-a-page) |
| Find links that are still strings | [`svelteVerifyRoutes`](#finding-links-that-are-still-strings) |
| Find links that lead nowhere | [`svelteVerifyLinks`](#finding-links-that-lead-nowhere) |
| Create a page | [`svelteAdd --page`](#a-new-page) |
| Create list, detail and form pages for a class | [`svelteAdd --crud`](#pages-for-a-class) |

## In Svelte

`#routes` exports `routes`, an object with one function per page. Each one returns the page's URL through SvelteKit's `resolve()` from `$app/paths`:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { goto } from '$app/navigation';
    import { routes } from '#routes';

    let { note } = $props();
</script>

<a href={routes.notes()}>All notes</a>
<button onclick={() => goto(routes.notesId({ id: note.id }))}>Open</button>
```

- The parameters come from SvelteKit's own route types, so a missing or misspelled parameter is a type error.
- Numbers are accepted too, so an ID needs no `String()`.
- Since every call goes through `resolve()`, a base path and relative prerender links work as usual, and the same functions work with `goto`.

`routeIds` holds the raw SvelteKit route IDs under the same names, such as `routeIds.notesId` for `/notes/[id]`. Use it to call `resolve()` yourself.

### Marking the open page in a menu

Every route can tell whether it is the page that is open, so a menu does not compare path strings:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { page } from '$app/state';
    import { routes } from '#routes';
</script>

<a href={routes.home()} aria-current={routes.home.ariaCurrent(page)}>Home</a>
<a href={routes.notes()} aria-current={routes.notes.ariaCurrent(page, { below: true })}>Notes</a>
<a href={routes.about()} class:font-bold={routes.about.isActive(page)}>About</a>
```

| Function | Returns |
|---|---|
| `isActive(page)` | `true` on that page. For a page with parameters, such as `routes.notesId`, that is every note |
| `isActive(page, { below: true })` | Also `true` on every page below it |
| `ariaCurrent(page)` | The value for `aria-current`: `page` on the page itself, `true` on a page below it when `below` is set, and nothing otherwise, so the attribute is left out |
| `routes.notes.id` | The route ID itself |

- With `{ below: true }`, `routes.notes` is active on `/notes`, `/notes/4` and `/notes/4/edit`, but not on `/notebooks`. The home page has everything below it, so for `routes.home` the option changes nothing.
- Style the open link through `aria-current`, such as `[aria-current]` in CSS or `aria-[current]:font-bold` in Tailwind.
- They compare SvelteKit's route ID, not the URL, so a base path, a language prefix, a trailing slash or a query string cannot get in the way, and route groups such as `(app)` are ignored.

### With i18n

With [i18n](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries#i18n) and `strategy = LocaleStrategy.UrlPrefix`, every route also puts the current language in front, such as `/de/notes/1`, so every language gets prerendered without calling `localizeHref` by hand. With the `Cookie` strategy, or without i18n, it is plain `resolve()`.

## In Kotlin

The same pages become `FrontendRoutes` in the generated package. Pages without parameters are constants, and pages with parameters are functions that encode their arguments:

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.FrontendRoutes
import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.localizeHref

post("/api/notes") {
    val note = store.create(call.receive<Note>())
    call.respondRedirect(call.localizeHref(FrontendRoutes.notesId(note.id.toString())))
}

get("/old-about") {
    call.respondRedirect(FrontendRoutes.about, permanent = true)
}
```

- Optional parameters such as `[[lang]]` become nullable arguments.
- Rest parameters such as `[...path]` keep their slashes.
- With i18n, `call.localizeHref` adds the visitor's language for `UrlPrefix` and returns the path unchanged for `Cookie`.
- The same names work with [`call.navigateTo`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#navigation-from-the-server), which opens a page in the browser after an API call.

## Names

A route's name is its path in camel case, without groups:

| Page | Name |
|---|---|
| `/` | `home` |
| `/about` | `about` |
| `/notes/[id]` | `notesId` |
| `/[[lang]]/docs/[...path]` | `langDocsPath` |
| `/404` | `route404` |

A name that would start with a digit gets a `route` prefix. When two pages would get the same name, such as `/blog-post` and `/blog/post`, sync fails and names both, so rename one of the folders.

## Keeping it current

`routes.ts` is a generated file like the others: commit it, and a production build fails if it is out of date.

- While `svelteDev` or `svelteDevAll` runs, adding, moving or deleting a page updates `routes.ts` at once.
- Under `svelteDevAll` `FrontendRoutes` follows and the app restarts. Otherwise it updates the next time Kotlin compiles.

## Renaming a page

Moving a page folder changes its route name, so every typed call to it stops compiling. `svelteRename` moves the folder and fixes those calls in one step:

```bash
./gradlew svelteRename --page=notes/[id] --to=memos/[id]
```

It moves `src/routes/notes/[id]` and every page below it, rewrites `routes.notesId` and `routeIds.notesId` in the frontend and `FrontendRoutes.notesId` in Kotlin to the new names, and then runs `svelteSync`, so `routes.ts` matches again. Both paths are relative to the routes folder, and route groups such as `(app)` are written as they are on disk.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--page=<path>` | The page to move, relative to the routes folder |
| `--to=<path>` | Where it goes |
| `--force` | Renames even when a file it would rewrite has uncommitted changes |

- The task stops before it changes anything when a file it would rewrite has uncommitted changes, so the rename stays one clean diff. Add `--force` to rename anyway.
- When the page's parameters change, such as `[id]` to `[noteId]`, the calls are renamed but their arguments are yours to update, and the compiler names each one.
- Nothing answers at the old address afterwards, so add a redirect if it was linked from outside the app.

## Finding links that are still strings

An app that turns typed routes on later still has links such as `href="/notes/{note.id}"`. `svelteVerifyRoutes` reads every `.svelte`, `.ts` and `.js` file under `src` and lists each `href`, `goto` and `redirect` whose path is one of your pages, with the call to write instead. It reads the Kotlin files in `src/main/kotlin` too, and lists each `respondRedirect` to a page with its `FrontendRoutes` replacement:

```bash
./gradlew svelteVerifyRoutes
```

```text
src/routes/+page.svelte:12  href="/notes/{note.id}"  ->  routes.notesId({ id: note.id })
src/lib/NoteForm.svelte:31  goto("/notes/" + created.id)  ->  routes.notesId({ id: created.id })
src/main/kotlin/notes/Routes.kt:48  respondRedirect("/notes/${note.id}")  ->  FrontendRoutes.notesId(note.id)
```

- It fails while it finds any.
- It only looks at paths that match a page, so links to your API, to files and to other sites are left alone.
- When a path is too dynamic to read, the suggestion shows `...` where the value goes.
- In Kotlin, string templates such as `$id` and `${note.id}` become the arguments, and a value that is not a `String` still needs its `toString()`.

Add `--fix` and the task rewrites the links for you and adds the `#routes` import to each file it changes:

```bash
./gradlew svelteVerifyRoutes --fix
```

It only rewrites a link when nothing is lost. A link with a query string or a fragment, a path that is too dynamic to read, and a Kotlin redirect with parameters are still listed for you to change by hand, and a file that already has something else called `routes` is left alone. Look at the diff before you commit, and run your formatter afterwards.

The check is not part of `check`. To keep new string links out, add it yourself:

```kotlin
tasks.check {
    dependsOn("svelteVerifyRoutes")
}
```

## Finding links that lead nowhere

`svelteVerifyLinks` is the opposite check. It reads the same files, and lists every internal link whose path is not one of your pages, not under your API and not a file in `static`, so a typo in an `href` shows up before a visitor finds it:

```bash
./gradlew svelteVerifyLinks
```

```text
src/routes/+page.svelte:14  href="/abuot"  ->  nothing is served at /abuot
src/main/kotlin/notes/Routes.kt:52  respondRedirect("/notes/${id}/edit")  ->  nothing is served at /notes/{}/edit
```

It only lists what it finds. Add `--strict` to fail the build instead, for example in CI.

- The check works with or without typed routes.
- Paths under your API are never reported, because the generated client already makes a call to a missing route a compile error. The API roots come from the generated `openapi.json`, or `/api` when there is none.
- A link that starts with a value, such as `href="/{section}/overview"`, cannot be judged and is skipped.
- With `LocaleStrategy.UrlPrefix` a leading language such as `/de` is accepted.

## Menu, titles and breadcrumbs

A menu is a list of pages with a title and an icon each, kept by hand somewhere far from the pages. Let each page say it about itself instead, in its `+page.ts`:

```ts
export const _nav = { title: 'Board', icon: 'LayoutDashboard', order: 1 };
```

| Field | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `title` | The page's title. With `i18n` on, write the key of a message, such as `'nav-board'`, and the title is translated |
| `icon` | Optional. With `lucide()` on, the name of an icon |
| `order` | Optional. Where the page stands in the menu. Pages without it come last, in the order of their paths |
| `menu` | Optional. `false` keeps the page out of the menu, with its title still known |
| `description`, `image` | Optional. For [link previews](#link-previews) |

The name starts with an underscore because SvelteKit refuses other exports from a page file. Keep the values plain: text, numbers, `true` and `false`. The plugin reads the file without running it, so a function call or a variable there fails `svelteSync` with the name of the file.

`routes.ts` then has three more things:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { page } from '$app/state';
    import { breadcrumbs, nav, pageTitle } from '#routes';
</script>

<svelte:head>
    <title>{pageTitle(page) ?? 'My app'}</title>
</svelte:head>

<nav>
    {#each nav as item (item.name)}
        <a href={item.to()} aria-current={item.to.ariaCurrent(page)}>{item.title()}</a>
    {/each}
</nav>

<ol>
    {#each breadcrumbs(page) as crumb (crumb.href)}
        <li><a href={crumb.href} aria-current={crumb.current ? 'page' : undefined}>{crumb.title}</a></li>
    {/each}
</ol>
```

| Export | What it is |
|---|---|
| `nav` | The pages without parameters, in order. Each item has the typed route as `to`, the `title` as a function so that it follows the language, the `icon`, and the route's `name` |
| `pageTitle(page)` | The title of the open page, or `undefined` for a page that declared none. It works for pages with parameters too |
| `breadcrumbs(page)` | The way from the start page to the open one: every page above it that has a title, with a link that carries the open page's parameters. Each crumb has `href`, `title` and `current` |

A menu that depends on who is signed in is a filter over `nav`. With [page guards](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/auth#page-guards) the rule is already written:

```ts
const links = $derived(
    nav.filter((item) => {
        const guard = matchGuard(pageGuards, item.to());
        if (!guard) return true;
        return currentUser.signedIn && (!guard.permission || can(guard.permission));
    })
);
```

## Link previews

When someone pastes a link to your site into a chat, the preview comes from tags in the page's HTML. Add what the preview should say to the same `_nav`:

```ts
export const _nav = {
    title: 'home-title',
    description: 'home-lead',
    image: 'https://example.com/share/home.png'
};
```

| Field | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `description` | One or two sentences. Like `title`, the key of a message when `i18n` is on |
| `image` | The preview image. Give its full address: most services do not follow a path. A path that starts with `/` is accepted and written as it is |

Every prerendered page that has a `description` or an `image` then gets these tags in its `<head>`, at build time:

```html
<meta property="og:type" content="website">
<meta property="og:title" content="A team board in one JAR">
<meta name="description" content="This example uses every ktor-svelte feature.">
<meta property="og:description" content="This example uses every ktor-svelte feature.">
<meta property="og:image" content="https://example.com/share/home.png">
<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image">
```

- They are written by the generated server hooks, so there is nothing to add to a layout.
- With `LocaleStrategy.UrlPrefix` each language's pages get the tags in that language. With the cookie strategy a page is prerendered once, so its tags are in the default language.

**Prerendered pages only**
This is for pages that are prerendered. A page with a parameter, such as `/notes/[id]`, is not: the server never renders pages, so such a page sets its own title when it runs, and a link to it previews without these tags.

## A new page

A new page is a folder, two files with the right names, the load's types, and for a page with a parameter two settings that are easy to forget. `svelteAdd` writes them:

```bash
./gradlew svelteAdd --page=notes/[id]
```

```text
ktor-svelte added /notes/[id]:
  frontend/src/routes/notes/[id]/+page.svelte
  frontend/src/routes/notes/[id]/+page.ts
Its load calls api.notes.get, the route that answers at the same path.
Add paramRoutes("/notes/[id]") to install(Svelte), so the app serves the page for every value.
The files are yours from here on.
```

Write the folder as it is under `src/routes`, with groups such as `(app)/settings` if you use them.

The `+page.ts` has a typed load. When the generated client already has a `GET` route at the same path below your API prefix, the load calls it, with the page's parameters in the type the route wants:

```ts
import { apiWith } from '#api';
import type { PageLoad } from './$types';

export const prerender = false;
export const ssr = false;

export const load: PageLoad = async (event) => {
    return { note: await apiWith(event).notes.get(Number(event.params.id)) };
};
```

- Without such a route the load returns the page's parameters, and you fill in the rest.
- The `+page.svelte` shows a title and the loaded data, so the page works before you have designed it.
- With `routes()` on, `routes.ts` is updated in the same run.

Add `--route` and the task also writes a Kotlin file with a route to start from, at the API path of the page:

```bash
./gradlew svelteAdd --page=orders/[id] --route
```

```kotlin
fun Route.ordersIdRoutes() {
    get("/api/orders/{id}") {
        val id = call.parameters["id"].orEmpty()
        call.respondText("Orders $id")
    }
}
```

The file goes into the package of your main class. Call the function inside `routing { }`, and after the next `svelteGenerateTs` the client has the route.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--page=<path>` | The page folder under `src/routes`. With `--crud`, the folder for the pages |
| `--route` | Also writes a Kotlin route at the page's API path |
| `--crud=<Class>` | Writes list, detail and form pages for a class. See [Pages for a class](#pages-for-a-class) |

The task only creates. It refuses when one of its files is already there, it never edits a file of yours, and what it wrote has no generated header: the files are yours.

## Pages for a class

Once the API can list, read, create, change and delete something, the first version of its pages is the same every time: a table, a form, a detail page. `svelteAdd --crud` writes that first version from the generated client:

```bash
./gradlew svelteAdd --crud=Note
```

```text
ktor-svelte added pages for Note, wired to api.notes:
  frontend/src/routes/notes/+page.ts
  frontend/src/routes/notes/+page.svelte
  frontend/src/routes/notes/new/+page.svelte
  frontend/src/routes/notes/[id]/+page.ts
  frontend/src/routes/notes/[id]/+page.svelte
Their texts are in de.json, en.json, in English. Translate them.
The form leaves out tags, icon: add inputs for them, they are not plain text, numbers or switches.
Add paramRoutes("/notes/[id]") to install(Svelte), so the app serves the detail page for every id.
The files are yours from here on.
```

The task looks for the route that lists the class, such as the `list` of a [resource](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/typescript#resource-routes), and for the other four routes next to it. What it finds decides what it writes:

| Route in the client | Page |
| --- | --- |
| `list` | A table of the class's plain fields, loaded in `+page.ts` |
| `create` | `new/+page.svelte` with a form, and a link to it from the list |
| `get` | `[id]/+page.ts` and a detail page, and a link to it from each row |
| `update` | The form again on the detail page, filled with the item |
| `delete` | A delete button in each row and on the detail page |

The pages use what the project has:

- The form is a [`formState`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/validation#form-state) of the input class, with its `validate` and, per field, its `bounds`, so the browser shows the same rules as the server.
- With `routes()` on, every link and `goto` is a typed route.
- With `i18n` on, every text is a message. The keys are added to each locale file in English, and keys that are already there are left alone.

Text, numbers and booleans get an input. Other fields, such as lists and enums, are left out of the form and named in the output, and the draft keeps their default.

`--page=(app)/memos` puts the pages in another folder than the one named after the API path.

As with a single page, the task only creates: it refuses when a file is already there, and what it wrote has no generated header. These are your pages from the first minute, a starting point to redesign and not a layer to configure.

## Full example

An app shell with a menu built from the pages themselves, the title in the browser tab, breadcrumbs, and a Kotlin route that sends old links to the right page.

::: code-group

```ts no-check [notes/+page.ts]
export const _nav = {
    title: 'Notes',
    icon: 'NotebookPen',
    order: 1,
    description: 'All your notes in one place.',
    image: 'https://example.com/share/notes.png'
};
```

```ts no-check [notes/[id]/+page.ts]
import { apiWith } from '#api';
import type { PageLoad } from './$types';

export const _nav = { title: 'Note', menu: false };

export const prerender = false;
export const ssr = false;

export const load: PageLoad = async (event) => {
    return { note: await apiWith(event).notes.get(Number(event.params.id)) };
};
```

```svelte no-check [+layout.svelte]
<script lang="ts">
    import { page } from '$app/state';
    import Icon from '#icon';
    import { breadcrumbs, nav, pageTitle, routes } from '#routes';

    let { children } = $props();
</script>

<svelte:head>
    <title>{pageTitle(page) ?? 'Notes app'}</title>
</svelte:head>

<header>
    <a href={routes.home()}>Notes app</a>
    <nav>
        {#each nav as item (item.name)}
            <a href={item.to()} aria-current={item.to.ariaCurrent(page, { below: true })}>
                {#if item.icon}<Icon name={item.icon} size={16} />{/if}
                {item.title()}
            </a>
        {/each}
    </nav>
</header>

<ol aria-label="Breadcrumbs">
    {#each breadcrumbs(page) as crumb (crumb.href)}
        <li><a href={crumb.href} aria-current={crumb.current ? 'page' : undefined}>{crumb.title}</a></li>
    {/each}
</ol>

<main>{@render children()}</main>
```

```kotlin no-check [Redirects.kt]
import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.FrontendRoutes

fun Route.oldLinks() {
    get("/memo/{id}") {
        val id = call.pathParameter<Int>("id")
        call.respondRedirect(FrontendRoutes.notesId(id.toString()), permanent = true)
    }
    get("/memos") {
        call.respondRedirect(FrontendRoutes.notes, permanent = true)
    }
}
```

Move `notes` to `memos` with `svelteRename`, and the menu, the breadcrumbs, the redirects and every `routes.notesId` call follow in one diff.

## Use cases

- Any app with more than a handful of pages: typed links, and [`svelteVerifyLinks`](#finding-links-that-lead-nowhere) in CI.
- Turning typed routes on in an existing app: [`svelteVerifyRoutes --fix`](#finding-links-that-are-still-strings).
- A menu, the tab title and breadcrumbs from one place: [`_nav`](#menu-titles-and-breadcrumbs).
- Pages shared on social media and in chats: [link previews](#link-previews).
- Redirects after a form post or from old addresses: [`FrontendRoutes`](#in-kotlin).
- Starting a new feature: [`svelteAdd`](#a-new-page), or [`svelteAdd --crud`](#pages-for-a-class) for a whole resource.

## Good to know

- A page with a parameter needs `paramRoutes("/notes/[id]")` in `install(Svelte)`, so the app serves it for every value. `svelteAdd` reminds you.
- `routes.ts` is generated: commit it, and do not edit it.
- `svelteVerifyRoutes` and `svelteVerifyLinks` are not part of `check`. Add them to `check` or to CI yourself.
- See also [Routes](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries#routes) among the frontend libraries.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/runtime-config

# Runtime config

Pass values to the frontend at startup, so one JAR works in every environment, and declare every environment variable the app reads in one place. The frontend gets the config typed, without a request, and the build fails when a secret ends up in the frontend files.

<Badge type="tip" text="Ktor plugin" /> <Badge type="info" text="Gradle" /> <Badge type="warning" text="Generated client" />

## Quick start

Hand a `@Serializable` object to `publicConfig`. The type comes along with `generateTs`:

```kotlin
@Serializable
data class AppConfig(val sentryDsn: String?)

install(Svelte) {
    publicConfig(AppConfig(sentryDsn = System.getenv("SENTRY_DSN")))
}
```

```ts
import { loadPublicConfig } from '#api';

const config = await loadPublicConfig();
```

In TypeScript the type is always called `PublicConfig`, whatever the Kotlin class is named.

## Reading the config

The config is also inlined into every page as `<script type="application/json" id="ktor-svelte-config">`, so it is there before your code runs, without a request. Read it synchronously, for example in a store or a component's script:

```ts
import { readPublicConfig } from '#api';

const config = readPublicConfig();
```

| Function | Returns | Use it |
|---|---|---|
| `readPublicConfig()` | The inlined config, or `undefined` when there is none, such as during development with Vite or on the server | In a store or a component's script, when you can handle `undefined` |
| `loadPublicConfig()` | A promise of the config. It uses the inlined copy when it is there and only asks the server otherwise, once | When you need the value for sure |

- The config is served as JSON from `/_ktor-svelte/config.json`. During development with Vite, `loadPublicConfig()` asks there.
- The JSON is escaped, so a value cannot close the script tag.
- Pages with the config are prepared once and cached, with their own ETag and a gzip copy.

| Setting in `install(Svelte)` | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `publicConfig(value)` | none | The config, fixed at startup |
| `publicConfig { ... }` | none | A function that gives the config, see [below](#changing-values-without-a-restart) |
| `inlinePublicConfig` | `true` | `false` keeps the config out of pages, so only `loadPublicConfig()` finds it |

## Changing values without a restart

Pass a function instead of a value when the config comes from somewhere you edit while the app runs, such as a file:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    publicConfig { Json.decodeFromString<AppConfig>(Path("config/public.json").readText()) }
}
```

- In development the function runs on every request for the config and for every page, so a saved change shows up on the next page load.
- Inlined pages get a new ETag when the config changes, so the browser does not keep a stale copy.
- In production the function runs once at startup and the result is kept, so a broken file fails the start instead of a request.

## Keep secrets out

It is served as JSON from `/_ktor-svelte/config.json` to anyone who asks, so **never put secrets in it**.

In SvelteKit, call `loadPublicConfig` only in the browser, because prerendering has no server to ask.

## Trying other values in development

To see the frontend with another value, you do not have to change the config: the [dev panel](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow) can override `publicConfig` values for your browser only.

## Environment variables

An app that reads `System.getenv` here and there finds out one variable at a time what is missing, in production, and nobody knows the full list. Declare them in one place instead:

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.EnvironmentScope
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.environment

class AppEnvironment(env: EnvironmentScope) {
    val databaseUrl = env.string("DATABASE_URL", "JDBC URL of the database", example = "jdbc:postgresql://localhost/app")
    val port = env.int("PORT", "Port the server listens on", default = 8080)
    val signKey = env.secret("SESSION_SIGN_KEY", "Signs the session cookie")
    val siteUrl = env.optional("SITE_URL", "Public address, for links in emails")
    val signUps = env.oneOf<SignUps>("SIGN_UPS", "Whether new people can register", default = SignUps.Open)
}

fun main() {
    val env = environment(declare = ::AppEnvironment)
    embeddedServer(Netty, port = env.port) { module(env) }.start(wait = true)
}
```

`environment` reads every variable, converts it, and returns your class with typed values. When something is missing or does not fit, the app stops before it does anything else, with all of it in one table:

```text
The app cannot start: 2 environment variables are missing or wrong.

  DATABASE_URL  missing                         JDBC URL of the database, such as jdbc:postgresql://localhost/app
  PORT          "eighty" is not a whole number  Port the server listens on

Set them in the environment. .env.example lists every variable the app reads.
```

| Function | Value |
|---|---|
| `string(name, description, default?, example?)` | Text. Required unless it has a default. |
| `optional(name, description, example?)` | Text or null. |
| `secret(name, description)`, `optionalSecret(...)` | Text that must not be shown. Its value never appears in the example file or in messages. |
| `int(name, description, default?, example?)` | A whole number. |
| `boolean(name, description, default?)` | `true` or `false`. |
| `oneOf<E>(name, description, default?)` | One of the values of an enum, in any letter case. |

- An empty variable counts as not set.
- A name has to be written in capital letters, digits and `_`, such as `DATABASE_URL`.
- The failure is an `EnvironmentException`, whose `variables` lists the names that are missing or wrong.
- `environment(source = { name -> ... }, declare = ...)` reads from somewhere else than `System.getenv`, such as a map in a test.

### .env.example

`svelteGenerateTs` writes `.env.example` next to `build.gradle.kts` from the same declaration, and dev mode keeps it current. Each variable is there with its description, whether it is required, and its default or example. Secrets are listed without a value.

`svelteVerifyTs`, and so `check`, fails when the file is out of date, so a new variable cannot be added without it showing up in a pull request.

**The generating run**
The generating run starts the app without your environment. It therefore does not stop for missing variables: a required one reads as its example, or as empty text. Code that runs at startup, such as connecting to the database, should already be skipped in that run or tolerate that, as it must today for `svelteGenerateTs` to work on a build server.

## Secrets in the frontend build

Everything in the frontend build is sent to browsers. A secret gets in there easily: a server-only variable imported in a component, a key pasted into a config file, a `.env` value Vite was told to expose. Nothing fails, and the key is public from the next deploy on.

`svelteVerifyLeaks` runs after `svelteBuild`, before the build is packed into the JAR, and looks for secret values in the built files. When it finds one, the build fails:

```text
ktor-svelte found secret values in the frontend build. Everything in that folder is sent to browsers.

  SESSION_SIGN_KEY (declared as a secret)  _app/immutable/chunks/B3kq9.js
  STRIPE_KEY (.env)                        _app/immutable/nodes/2.Dx1.js

Read such values on the server only. A value that is meant to be public belongs in svelte { buildEnv }, or gets a name that starts with PUBLIC_.
```

It names the variable and the file, never the value. The values it looks for are:

- the [declared environment variables](#environment-variables) marked as `secret`, with the value they have in the environment of the build
- every value in `.env`, `.env.local`, `.env.production` and `.env.production.local`, next to `build.gradle.kts` and in the frontend folder

Left out are:

- variables listed in `buildEnv`
- names that start with `PUBLIC_` or `VITE_`
- values shorter than eight characters
- values that are one plain word, such as `production`

Those would be found in almost any build.

The check can only find a secret whose value it knows. On a build server that does not have the production secrets, it has nothing to compare, which is one more reason to build with the real environment or not at all. To turn it off:

```kotlin
svelte {
    verifyLeaks = false
}
```

## Full example

An app that reads its settings from the environment, hands the public part to the frontend, and shows a banner and a sign-up link depending on it.

::: code-group

```kotlin no-check [Environment.kt]
enum class SignUps { Open, InviteOnly, Closed }

class AppEnvironment(env: EnvironmentScope) {
    val port = env.int("PORT", "Port the server listens on", default = 8080)
    val databaseUrl = env.string("DATABASE_URL", "JDBC URL of the database", example = "jdbc:postgresql://localhost/app")
    val signKey = env.secret("SESSION_SIGN_KEY", "Signs the session cookie")
    val sentryDsn = env.optional("SENTRY_DSN", "Where the frontend reports errors")
    val banner = env.optional("BANNER", "A short notice shown on every page, such as planned maintenance")
    val signUps = env.oneOf<SignUps>("SIGN_UPS", "Whether new people can register", default = SignUps.Open)
}

@Serializable
data class AppConfig(
    val sentryDsn: String?,
    val banner: String?,
    val registrationOpen: Boolean,
)

fun main() {
    val env = environment(declare = ::AppEnvironment)
    embeddedServer(Netty, port = env.port) { module(env) }.start(wait = true)
}

fun Application.module(env: AppEnvironment) {
    install(Svelte) {
        generateTs = true
        publicConfig(
            AppConfig(
                sentryDsn = env.sentryDsn,
                banner = env.banner,
                registrationOpen = env.signUps == SignUps.Open,
            ),
        )
    }
}
```

```svelte no-check [+layout.svelte]
<script lang="ts">
    import { loadPublicConfig, type PublicConfig } from '#api';

    let { children } = $props();

    let config = $state<PublicConfig | undefined>(undefined);

    $effect(() => {
        loadPublicConfig().then((loaded) => (config = loaded));
    });
</script>

{#if config?.banner}
    <p role="status" class="banner">{config.banner}</p>
{/if}

<header>
    <a href="/">Notes</a>
    {#if config?.registrationOpen}<a href="/register">Sign up</a>{/if}
</header>

{@render children()}
```

```text [.env.example]
# Generated by ktor-svelte from the environment variables the app declares. Do not edit.

# Port the server listens on. A whole number. Default: 8080.
# PORT=8080

# JDBC URL of the database. Required.
DATABASE_URL=jdbc:postgresql://localhost/app

# Signs the session cookie. Required. Secret.
SESSION_SIGN_KEY=

# Where the frontend reports errors. Optional.
# SENTRY_DSN=

# A short notice shown on every page, such as planned maintenance. Optional.
# BANNER=

# Whether new people can register. One of Open, InviteOnly, Closed. Default: Open.
# SIGN_UPS=Open
```

- The same JAR runs in staging and production; only the environment differs.
- A missing `DATABASE_URL` or `SESSION_SIGN_KEY` stops the start with one table of everything that is wrong.
- `SESSION_SIGN_KEY` never reaches the frontend. If it did, `svelteVerifyLeaks` would fail the build.
- `.env.example` is written by `svelteGenerateTs` and dev mode. Required variables are written as they are, optional ones commented out, and secrets without a value.

## Use cases

- Values that differ between environments, such as an error reporting DSN, a support email or a feature switch: [`publicConfig`](#quick-start).
- Notices you change without a deploy: [a function](#changing-values-without-a-restart) that reads a file.
- Knowing every variable the app needs, and failing early when one is missing: [environment variables](#environment-variables).
- Making sure a key never ships to browsers: [`svelteVerifyLeaks`](#secrets-in-the-frontend-build).

## Good to know

- The config is public. Anything in it can be read by anyone.
- In SvelteKit, call `loadPublicConfig` only in the browser.
- `readPublicConfig()` is `undefined` during development with Vite, because Vite serves the pages. Use `loadPublicConfig()` when you need the value.
- The generator playground leaves `readPublicConfig()` out, because it has no `publicConfig`. See [Generator playground](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/playground).

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/playground

# Generator playground

Paste an OpenAPI document and see the TypeScript that `generateTs` writes for it. The playground runs the same generator as the Ktor plugin, compiled to JavaScript, so nothing leaves your browser.

## How to use it

1. Get the OpenAPI document of your API. In an app with `generateTs` it is the committed `frontend/src/lib/api/openapi.json`.
2. Paste it above.
3. Read the generated `types.ts` and `services.ts`, and compare them with what [Generated TypeScript](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/typescript) describes.

## What is different in a real project

- Only paths under the API prefix are kept, as in your app.
- The document must be JSON, which is what Ktor produces.
- In a real project the generator also adds the `LucideIcon` type when `lucide` is enabled and `readPublicConfig()` when you set [`publicConfig`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/runtime-config), so those are missing here.

See [Generated TypeScript](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/typescript) for what each file contains and how to use it, and [Calling the API](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api) for how to call the result.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries

# Frontend libraries

Tailwind, DaisyUI, fonts, charts, Lucide icons, optimized images, an installable app, toasts, typed routes, ready-made components and i18n, all turned on in Gradle, with typed helpers on both sides.

<Badge type="info" text="Gradle" /> <Badge type="warning" text="Generated files" />

You list what you want in `build.gradle.kts`. ktor-svelte installs the packages, configures them, and generates the glue, so everything works together, including across Kotlin and TypeScript. This page is the map: what each library does, how they are applied, and what ktor-svelte owns in your frontend. Each library has its own page with every option and longer examples.

## Quick start

```kotlin
svelte {
    libraries {
```
