```kotlin
        daisyUi()
        lucide()
        toasts()
    }
}
```

```bash
./gradlew svelteSync
```

That is a styled app with themes, typed icons and error toasts. Add the rest one line at a time.

## All libraries

| Library | In `libraries { }` | What you get | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tailwind | `tailwind()` | Tailwind 4 wired into Vite and the CSS, with the typography and forms plugins on request | [Styling](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/styling#tailwind) |
| DaisyUI | `daisyUi { }` | Components and themes, typed in TypeScript and Kotlin, with no flash of the wrong theme | [Styling](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/styling#daisyui) |
| Fonts | `fonts("Inter")` | A font served from your own app, preloaded, as the default font | [Styling](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/styling#fonts) |
| Charts | `charts()` | LayerChart in your theme colors, with typed series | [Charts](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/charts) |
| Lucide | `lucide()` | A typed `LucideIcon` enum and an `<Icon>` component, with only the icons you use in the build | [Icons and images](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/icons-and-images#lucide-icons) |
| Images | `images()` | `<enhanced:img>`: AVIF and WebP in several widths, at build time | [Icons and images](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/icons-and-images#images) |
| Installable app | `installable { }` | A web manifest, icons in every size and a service worker with an offline page | [Installable app](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/installable-app) |
| Toasts | `toasts()` | Failed API calls shown as toasts, a `toast()` helper and an optional reload prompt | [Calling the API](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#show-errors-automatically), [Components](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#toasts) |
| Routes | `routes()` | Every page as a typed constant in TypeScript and Kotlin | [Typed routes](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/routes) |
| Components | `components()` | Form fields, date inputs, a data table, file drop, error page, theme and language switches | [Components](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components) |
| i18n | `i18n { }` | Typed messages, plurals, and number, money and date formats that match on both sides | [i18n](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/i18n) |

Every project with generated files also gets a [modal helper](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#modals), a [confirm helper](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#confirm-before-a-call), a [guide for coding assistants](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#guide-for-coding-assistants) and [lint rules](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#lint-rules).

## The libraries block

Everything at once, as a full example:

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.gradle.DaisyTheme
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.gradle.LocaleStrategy

svelte {
    libraries {
        tailwind {
            typography()
            forms()
        }
        daisyUi {
            themes(DaisyTheme.ShadcnLight, DaisyTheme.ShadcnDark, DaisyTheme.Cupcake)
            customTheme("brand") {
                primary = "#7f52ff"
                base100 = "#fdfcff"
            }
            defaultTheme(DaisyTheme.ShadcnLight)
            prefersDark(DaisyTheme.ShadcnDark)
        }
        fonts("Inter")
        charts()
        lucide()
        images()
        toasts()
        routes()
        components()
        i18n {
            locales("en", "de")
            defaultLocale = "en"
            strategy = LocaleStrategy.Cookie
        }
    }
}
```

Some libraries build on others:

- `daisyUi()` turns on `tailwind()` as well.
- `fonts(...)` needs `tailwind()` or `daisyUi()`, which bring the stylesheet.
- `charts()` needs `daisyUi()`, whose theme colors the charts take.
- `components()` imports from `#api`, so it needs `generateTs = true` on the server.
- `ThemeToggle` is generated with `daisyUi`, and `LocaleSwitch` and `TimeAgo` with `i18n`.

A setting the plugin does not know, such as a typo inside `daisyUi { }`, fails the build with the name of the block.

## Apply changes with svelteSync

```bash
./gradlew svelteSync
```

`svelteSync` adds the packages, updates your lockfile and writes the generated files. Commit the result.

- The generated folder `src/lib/ktor-svelte` carries its own `.gitattributes`, which marks the files as generated and keeps their line endings the same on every machine.
- `svelteDev` and `svelteDevAll` sync automatically.
- A production build never changes anything: it fails and asks you to run `svelteSync` if something is out of date.

## What ktor-svelte owns

Once any library is on, some files belong to the plugin. You change them through Gradle, not by hand.

| File | Who writes it | How you add your own |
|---|---|---|
| `vite.config.ts` | ktor-svelte | Put your settings in `vite.user.ts`. They are merged in |
| `src/hooks.server.ts` | ktor-svelte | Combine your `handle` with `ktorSvelteHandle`, see below |
| `src/hooks.ts` | ktor-svelte, for URL prefixes | |
| `src/lib/ktor-svelte/` | ktor-svelte, rewritten by every sync | Write your own files next to it, such as a component on the same helper |
| `src/routes/+layout.svelte` | Created only when you have none | Add the stylesheet import to yours |
| Generated Kotlin | ktor-svelte, in `io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte` | Change the package with `generatedPackage` |

Your own Vite settings go in `vite.user.ts`:

```ts
export default {
    server: { port: 3000 }
};
```

If you already have your own versions of the hook files, sync stops rather than overwriting them, and tells you to move your settings and delete the file. To combine your own `handle` with ours, use `sequence` from `@sveltejs/kit/hooks` with `ktorSvelteHandle` from `#lib/ktor-svelte/server-hooks.js`, after removing the generated hook file and any use of a library that needs it.

If you already have `src/routes/+layout.svelte`, add this line once. Without a layout, one is created for you.

```ts
import '#lib/ktor-svelte/app.css';
```

Generated Kotlin lands in the `io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte` package. Change it in the libraries block:

```kotlin
svelte {
    libraries {
        generatedPackage = "com.example.ui"
    }
}
```

## Tailwind

`tailwind()` installs Tailwind 4 and wires Vite and the CSS. `typography()` and `forms()` add the official plugins. See [Styling: Tailwind](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/styling#tailwind).

## DaisyUI

`daisyUi()` adds DaisyUI and turns on Tailwind as well. With no themes listed, you get `Light` and `Dark`. Themes are typed on both sides, and the saved choice is applied before the first paint, so there is no flash of the wrong theme. Use the theme selector in the top bar of this site to see every theme ktor-svelte ships, the shadcn themes included.

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.gradle.DaisyTheme

svelte {
    libraries {
        daisyUi {
            themes(DaisyTheme.ShadcnLight, DaisyTheme.ShadcnDark)
            defaultTheme(DaisyTheme.ShadcnLight)
            prefersDark(DaisyTheme.ShadcnDark)
        }
    }
}
```

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { setTheme, themes } from '#theme';
</script>

{#each themes as theme}
    <button class="btn" onclick={() => setTheme(theme)}>{theme}</button>
{/each}
```

The build stops when `daisyUi` has no theme, when `defaultTheme` or `prefersDark` names a theme that is not in the list, or when a custom theme name is not lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Custom themes, the dev panel color picker, the server side and the full list of themes are on [Styling: DaisyUI](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/styling#daisyui).

### shadcn themes

`DaisyTheme.ShadcnLight` and `DaisyTheme.ShadcnDark` bring the look of shadcn/ui to every DaisyUI component. See [Styling: shadcn themes](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/styling#shadcn-themes).

## Fonts

`fonts("Inter")` serves a font from your own app instead of a font CDN. See [Styling: Fonts](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/styling#fonts).

## Charts

`charts()` sets up LayerChart in your theme colors. See [Charts](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/charts).

## Lucide

`lucide()` generates a typed `LucideIcon` enum and builds only the icons you use. See [Icons and images: Lucide icons](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/icons-and-images#lucide-icons).

## Images

`images()` adds `<enhanced:img>`, which turns pictures into AVIF and WebP in several widths at build time. See [Icons and images: Images](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/icons-and-images#images).

## Installable app

`installable { }` makes the app installable on phones and desktops, with a manifest, icons and an offline page. See [Installable app](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/installable-app).

## Toasts

`toasts()` shows failed API calls as toasts, without any error handling in your components. See [Show errors automatically](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#show-errors-automatically), and [Components: Toasts](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#toasts) for your own toasts.

`toasts { reloadPrompt() }` also offers a reload when the server runs a newer build than the page. See [Reload after a deploy](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#reload-after-a-deploy).

## Routes

`routes()` turns every page into a typed constant in TypeScript and Kotlin, for links and redirects that always point to a real page. See [Typed routes](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/routes).

## i18n

`i18n { }` gives both sides typed functions from one set of JSON message files, and a missing key or a mismatched parameter in any language fails the build.

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.gradle.LocaleStrategy

svelte {
    libraries {
        i18n {
            locales("en", "de")
            defaultLocale = "en"
            strategy = LocaleStrategy.Cookie
        }
    }
}
```

The build stops when `i18n` has no locale, when `defaultLocale` is not one of the locales, or when a locale is not a tag such as `en` or `pt-BR`. Messages, strategies, plurals and formats are on the [i18n page](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/i18n).

### Plurals

Moved to [i18n: Plurals](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/i18n#plurals).

### Numbers, money and dates

Moved to [i18n: Numbers, money and dates](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/i18n#numbers-money-and-dates).

### Messages nobody translated yet

Moved to [i18n: Messages nobody translated yet](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/i18n#messages-nobody-translated-yet).

### Messages nothing uses

Moved to [i18n: Messages nothing uses](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/i18n#messages-nothing-uses).

## Components

`components()` generates Svelte components over the helpers ktor-svelte already writes. See [Components](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components).

### Field

Moved to [Components: Field](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#field).

### DateInput and DateTimeInput

Moved to [Components: DateInput and DateTimeInput](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#dateinput-and-datetimeinput).

### EnumSelect

Moved to [Components: EnumSelect](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#enumselect).

### DataTable

Moved to [Components: DataTable](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#datatable).

### FileDrop

Moved to [Components: FileDrop](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#filedrop).

### ErrorPage

Moved to [Components: ErrorPage](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#errorpage).

### ThemeToggle and LocaleSwitch

Moved to [Components: ThemeToggle and LocaleSwitch](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#themetoggle-and-localeswitch).

### NavigationProgress

Moved to [Components: NavigationProgress](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#navigationprogress).

## Modals

`modal()` opens a `<dialog>` and returns a promise with its result. See [Components: Modals](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#modals).

## Guide for coding assistants

`svelteSync` writes an `AGENTS.md` that tells coding assistants how your project works. See [Components: Guide for coding assistants](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#guide-for-coding-assistants).

## Lint rules

`svelteSync` writes a small ESLint plugin for common ktor-svelte mistakes. See [Components: Lint rules](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#lint-rules).

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/styling

# Styling

Tailwind, DaisyUI themes and self-hosted fonts, set up from Gradle. Themes are typed in TypeScript and Kotlin, and the visitor's choice is applied before the first paint.

<Badge type="info" text="Gradle" /> <Badge type="warning" text="Generated files" />

This page is part of [Frontend libraries](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries). Run `./gradlew svelteSync` after every change to the `libraries { }` block.

## Quick start

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.gradle.DaisyTheme

svelte {
    libraries {
        daisyUi {
            themes(DaisyTheme.ShadcnLight, DaisyTheme.ShadcnDark)
        }
        fonts("Inter")
    }
}
```

```svelte
<button class="btn btn-primary">Save</button>
```

That is Tailwind, DaisyUI with the shadcn look in light and dark, and Inter as the font of the whole page.

## Tailwind

`tailwind()` installs Tailwind 4 and wires Vite and the CSS. Everything else is normal Tailwind CSS.

```kotlin
svelte {
    libraries {
        tailwind()
    }
}
```

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `typography()` | off | Adds the official typography plugin, for the `prose` classes on long text |
| `forms()` | off | Adds the official forms plugin, which gives form controls a plain base style that is easy to change with utilities |

```kotlin
svelte {
    libraries {
        tailwind {
            typography()
            forms()
        }
    }
}
```

The stylesheet is generated as `src/lib/ktor-svelte/app.css`. If you already had a root layout, import it there once:

```ts
import '#lib/ktor-svelte/app.css';
```

`daisyUi()` turns on Tailwind as well, so you do not need both lines.

## DaisyUI

`daisyUi()` adds [DaisyUI](https://daisyui.com) on top of Tailwind. Themes are typed on both sides, and the saved choice is applied before the first paint, so there is no flash of the wrong theme. Use the theme selector in the top bar of this site to see every theme ktor-svelte ships, the shadcn themes included, applied to these pages.

```kotlin
svelte {
    libraries {
        daisyUi()
    }
}
```

With no themes and no custom theme, you get `Light` and `Dark`.

### Choosing themes

`themes(...)` takes the themes as `DaisyTheme` constants, so a typo is a compile error. Themes appear in `themes` in the frontend in the order you list them.

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.gradle.DaisyTheme

svelte {
    libraries {
        daisyUi {
            themes(DaisyTheme.Light, DaisyTheme.Dark, DaisyTheme.Nord, DaisyTheme.Dracula)
        }
    }
}
```

**Every DaisyTheme constant**
`Light`, `Dark`, `Cupcake`, `Bumblebee`, `Emerald`, `Corporate`, `Synthwave`, `Retro`, `Cyberpunk`, `Valentine`, `Halloween`, `Garden`, `Forest`, `Aqua`, `Lofi`, `Pastel`, `Fantasy`, `Wireframe`, `Black`, `Luxury`, `Dracula`, `Cmyk`, `Autumn`, `Business`, `Acid`, `Lemonade`, `Night`, `Coffee`, `Winter`, `Dim`, `Nord`, `Sunset`, `Caramellatte`, `Abyss`, `Silk`, `ShadcnLight` and `ShadcnDark`.

In the frontend each theme is its DaisyUI name in lowercase, such as `'cupcake'`, and the shadcn ones are `'shadcn-light'` and `'shadcn-dark'`.

### Default theme and dark mode

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `themes(...)` | `Light` and `Dark`, when there is no custom theme either | The DaisyUI themes to ship |
| `defaultTheme(...)` | The first theme | The theme for a visitor who has not chosen one |
| `prefersDark(...)` | `Dark` or `ShadcnDark`, when one of them is in the list | The theme for a visitor whose system is set to dark mode |
| `customTheme(name) { }` | none | A theme of your own, see [Custom themes](#custom-themes) |

`defaultTheme` and `prefersDark` take a `DaisyTheme` or the name of a custom theme as text:

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.gradle.DaisyTheme

svelte {
    libraries {
        daisyUi {
            themes(DaisyTheme.Corporate, DaisyTheme.Business)
            customTheme("brand") {
                primary = "#7f52ff"
            }
            defaultTheme("brand")
            prefersDark(DaisyTheme.Business)
        }
    }
}
```

A visitor's own choice always wins over both.

### shadcn themes

`DaisyTheme.ShadcnLight` and `DaisyTheme.ShadcnDark` bring the look of [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com) to every DaisyUI component: its neutral palette, `0.625rem` corners, thin borders and flat surfaces without shadows or noise. Use them like any other theme. Projects created by the setup script start with them:

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.gradle.DaisyTheme

svelte {
    libraries {
        daisyUi {
            themes(DaisyTheme.ShadcnLight, DaisyTheme.ShadcnDark)
            defaultTheme(DaisyTheme.ShadcnLight)
            prefersDark(DaisyTheme.ShadcnDark)
        }
    }
}
```

On the server they are `AppTheme.ShadcnLight` and `AppTheme.ShadcnDark`, and in the frontend `'shadcn-light'` and `'shadcn-dark'`. When you only pick these two, the dark one is used for visitors who prefer dark mode.

### Custom themes

`customTheme` defines a theme of your own. Set the colors you want, and DaisyUI fills in the rest:

```kotlin
svelte {
    libraries {
        daisyUi {
            customTheme("brand") {
                primary = "#7f52ff"
                secondary = "#ff3e00"
                base100 = "#fdfcff"
                baseContent = "#1f1b3a"
            }
        }
    }
}
```

| Setting | DaisyUI variable |
|---|---|
| `primary`, `secondary`, `accent`, `neutral` | `--color-primary` and so on |
| `base100`, `base200`, `base300`, `baseContent` | `--color-base-100`, `--color-base-200`, `--color-base-300`, `--color-base-content` |
| `info`, `success`, `warning`, `error` | `--color-info` and so on |
| `variable("radius-box", "1rem")` | Any other variable DaisyUI supports, by its name without `--` |
| `colorScheme = "dark"` | Marks a dark theme. The default is `"light"` |

`colorScheme` is a parameter of `customTheme`:

```kotlin
svelte {
    libraries {
        daisyUi {
            customTheme("midnight", colorScheme = "dark") {
                primary = "#a78bfa"
                base100 = "#0f0d1a"
                variable("radius-box", "1rem")
            }
        }
    }
}
```

- The name must be lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter.
- Custom themes join the list after the ones you pass to `themes(...)`.
- In Kotlin the theme becomes an `AppTheme` constant in PascalCase: `"brand"` is `AppTheme.Brand`, `"my-brand"` is `AppTheme.MyBrand`.

### Tune colors in the dev panel

You do not have to guess those colors in the build file. With DaisyUI on, the [dev panel](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow) has a **Theme colors** section with a color picker for each of the twelve. Changing one recolors the open page at once, so you tune the theme on your real screens. **Copy for Gradle** puts the result on the clipboard as a finished block, named as you typed it:

```kotlin
customTheme("sunset") {
    primary = "#ff0044"
    secondary = "#f5f5f5"
    base100 = "#fff8e7"
}
```

The real block lists all twelve colors, and says `colorScheme = "dark"` when you started from a dark theme. Paste it into `daisyUi { }`, and `svelteSync` makes it a theme like any other. The changes on the page are a preview only: **Reset**, or a reload, brings the theme back.

### Switch themes in the frontend

`#theme` holds the helpers, generated from your list:

| Export | What it is |
|---|---|
| `themes` | Every theme name, in order, as a readonly tuple |
| `ThemeName` | The union of those names, such as `'shadcn-light' \| 'shadcn-dark'` |
| `defaultTheme` | The default theme |
| `getTheme()` | The visitor's saved theme, or the default. On the server it is always the default |
| `setTheme(theme)` | Applies the theme at once and saves it in a cookie for a year |

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { onMount } from 'svelte';
    import { getTheme, setTheme, themes, type ThemeName } from '#theme';

    let current = $state<ThemeName>(themes[0]);

    onMount(() => {
        current = getTheme();
    });

    function pick(theme: ThemeName) {
        current = theme;
        setTheme(theme);
    }
</script>

<div class="join">
    {#each themes as theme (theme)}
        <button class="btn join-item" class:btn-active={theme === current} onclick={() => pick(theme)}>{theme}</button>
    {/each}
</div>
```

For a switch you do not have to write, `components()` generates [`ThemeToggle`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#themetoggle-and-localeswitch): a button with two themes, a select with more.

### The theme on the server

The theme cookie is readable in Ktor too, typed through the generated `AppTheme` enum:

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.AppTheme
import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.theme

get("/api/report") {
    val isDark = call.theme == AppTheme.Dark
}
```

- `call.theme` is the visitor's theme, or `AppTheme.default` when there is none.
- Each constant has its `cssName`, such as `"shadcn-dark"`.
- `AppTheme.fromCssName(name)` turns a name back into a constant, or `null`.

Use it for anything rendered on the server that should match the page, such as a PDF or a chart image.

### Content-Security-Policy

The saved theme is applied by a small inline script. The automatic [Content-Security-Policy](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/security#security-headers) allows it by its hash. If you set your own `contentSecurityPolicy`, allow it with SvelteKit's `csp` option in `hash` mode.

## Fonts

A font from a font CDN is a request to another company on every first visit, a line in the privacy policy, and an exception in the Content-Security-Policy. `fonts` serves the font from your own app instead:

```kotlin
svelte {
    libraries {
        tailwind()
        fonts("Inter")
    }
}
```

`svelteSync` then does three things:

- It installs the font from [Fontsource](https://fontsource.org), an npm package per font, so the lockfile pins the files like any other dependency.
- It imports the font into the generated stylesheet and makes it the default: `font-sans` in Tailwind, and so the font of the whole page.
- It preloads the Latin file on every page, through the generated server hooks, so text does not first appear in a fallback font.

The files end up in the frontend build under hashed names and are served by your app, with the long cache lifetime of every other asset.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `fonts("Inter")` | none | The font of the page, `font-sans` |
| `mono` | none | The font for code, `font-mono` |
| `variable` | `true` | Uses the variable version, one file for all weights. Set `false` for a font that has none, and the regular and bold files are used |

### A font for code

```kotlin
fonts("Inter") {
    mono = "JetBrains Mono"
}
```

Write the names as the fonts are called, with spaces.

### Fonts without a variable version

```kotlin
fonts("Roboto") {
    variable = false
}
```

Whether a font exists, and whether it has a variable version, shows on its Fontsource page.

## Full example

A settings page where the visitor picks a theme from cards that each show the theme itself. The build file ships four themes and one of your own, like the showcase example:

::: code-group

```kotlin [build.gradle.kts]
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.gradle.DaisyTheme

svelte {
    libraries {
        tailwind {
            typography()
            forms()
        }
        daisyUi {
            themes(DaisyTheme.ShadcnLight, DaisyTheme.ShadcnDark, DaisyTheme.Nord, DaisyTheme.Dracula)
            customTheme("ktor") {
                primary = "#7f52ff"
                secondary = "#ff3e00"
                accent = "#c711e1"
                base100 = "#fdfcff"
                baseContent = "#1f1b3a"
            }
            defaultTheme(DaisyTheme.ShadcnLight)
            prefersDark(DaisyTheme.ShadcnDark)
        }
        fonts("Inter") {
            mono = "JetBrains Mono"
        }
    }
}
```

```svelte no-check [settings/appearance/+page.svelte]
<script lang="ts">
    import { onMount } from 'svelte';
    import { getTheme, setTheme, themes, type ThemeName } from '#theme';

    const names: Partial<Record<ThemeName, string>> = {
        'shadcn-light': 'Light',
        'shadcn-dark': 'Dark',
        nord: 'Nord',
        dracula: 'Dracula',
        ktor: 'Ktor purple'
    };

    let current = $state<ThemeName>(themes[0]);

    onMount(() => {
        current = getTheme();
    });

    function pick(theme: ThemeName) {
        current = theme;
        setTheme(theme);
    }
</script>

<h1 class="mb-6 text-3xl font-bold">Appearance</h1>

<fieldset class="grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-3">
    <legend class="mb-2 font-semibold">Theme</legend>
    {#each themes as theme (theme)}
        <label
            data-theme={theme}
            class="card bg-base-100 text-base-content cursor-pointer border-2 p-4"
            class:border-primary={theme === current}
            class:border-base-300={theme !== current}
        >
            <input class="sr-only" type="radio" name="theme" value={theme} checked={theme === current} onchange={() => pick(theme)} />
            <span class="font-semibold">{names[theme] ?? theme}</span>
            <span class="mt-3 flex gap-1">
                <span class="badge badge-primary">Aa</span>
                <span class="badge badge-secondary">Aa</span>
                <span class="badge badge-accent">Aa</span>
            </span>
            <code class="mt-3 font-mono text-xs">{theme}</code>
        </label>
    {/each}
</fieldset>

<article class="prose mt-10">
    <h2>Preview</h2>
    <p>Long text gets the typography plugin's styles, in your theme and in Inter.</p>
</article>
```

```kotlin no-check [ReportRoutes.kt]
import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.AppTheme
import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.theme

get("/api/report.pdf") {
    val dark = call.theme in setOf(AppTheme.ShadcnDark, AppTheme.Dracula)
    call.respondBytes(renderReport(dark = dark), ContentType.Application.Pdf)
}
```

Each card sets `data-theme` on itself, so it shows that theme's colors whatever the page uses.

## Use cases

- A product with a brand color: one `customTheme`, tuned in the dev panel.
- An internal tool that should look calm and neutral: the [shadcn themes](#shadcn-themes).
- A public site with a privacy policy to keep short: [fonts](#fonts) from your own app instead of a CDN.
- Server-rendered files, such as PDFs or emails, that match the visitor's theme: [`call.theme`](#the-theme-on-the-server).
- A theme switch without writing one: [ThemeToggle](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#themetoggle-and-localeswitch).

## Good to know

**The theme is applied before the first paint**
The saved theme is in a cookie (`ktor_svelte_theme`), and a small inline script sets it on `<html>` before the page shows, so there is no flash of the wrong theme.

**The build checks your themes**
The build stops when `daisyUi` has no theme, when `defaultTheme` or `prefersDark` names a theme that is not in the list, and when a custom theme name is not lowercase letters, digits and dashes. The error message links to [DaisyUI](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries#daisyui) on the Frontend libraries page.

**Changing fonts**
`fonts` needs `tailwind()` or `daisyUi()`, which bring the stylesheet. A name that does not exist fails at `svelteSync`, when the package cannot be installed. When you drop or change a font, remove its old `@fontsource` package from `package.json` yourself: the plugin does not know which of them are yours.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/icons-and-images

# Icons and images

Typed Lucide icons that you can use in Kotlin DTOs and Svelte alike, and pictures that are resized and converted at build time.

<Badge type="info" text="Gradle" /> <Badge type="warning" text="Generated files" />

This page is part of [Frontend libraries](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries). Run `./gradlew svelteSync` after every change to the `libraries { }` block.

## Quick start

```kotlin
svelte {
    libraries {
        lucide()
        images()
    }
}
```

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import Icon from '#icon';
</script>

<Icon name="ArrowRight" size={20} />
<enhanced:img src="#lib/assets/hero.png" alt="Our team" />
```

## Lucide icons

`lucide()` installs [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) for Svelte and generates a `LucideIcon` enum from the installed version, so a misspelled icon is a compile error, in Kotlin and in TypeScript.

### In Svelte

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import Icon from '#icon';
</script>

<Icon name="ArrowRight" size={20} />
<Icon name={note.icon} class="text-primary" />
```

| Prop | What it does |
|---|---|
| `name` | The icon, typed as `LucideIconName`. A typo fails `svelteCheck` |
| `size` | Width and height, as a number of pixels or any CSS length |
| `color` | The stroke color. Without it the icon takes the text color |
| `strokeWidth` | The width of the lines |
| `class` | Classes for the `<svg>`, such as `text-primary` or `inline` |

Each icon loads on demand, so you only download the ones a page uses.

### In Kotlin

The enum is generated in the [generated package](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries#what-ktor-svelte-owns). Use it in your DTOs, and it reaches the frontend as the same type:

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.LucideIcon

@Serializable
data class Note(val title: String, val icon: LucideIcon)
```

A misspelled icon name from a client gets a 400 from Ktor, like any other invalid enum value.

### Icon names

An icon's enum name is its Lucide name in PascalCase:

| Lucide name | Enum name |
|---|---|
| `arrow-right` | `ArrowRight` |
| `square-check` | `SquareCheck` |
| `layout-dashboard` | `LayoutDashboard` |
| `a-arrow-down` | `AArrowDown` |

Names starting with a digit get an `Icon` prefix.

### Only the icons you use

Only the icons your app uses are built into the frontend. `svelteSync` finds them in your Kotlin code (`LucideIcon.Flame`) and in your frontend (`name="ArrowRight"`, `Icon.Tags`, or a string such as `'Search'`), and writes just those into `src/lib/ktor-svelte/icons.ts`.

Lucide has almost 2,000 icons, and each would otherwise become its own file in your JAR. In the notes example, this takes the frontend build from 6,180 files and 11 MB down to 120 files and 1.8 MB. The `LucideIcon` enum and the TypeScript type still list every icon, so anything stored or sent stays valid.

A list of icons in your own code is found the same way, since each name is a string:

```ts
import type { LucideIcon } from '#api';

const choices: LucideIcon[] = ['SquareCheck', 'Bug', 'Lightbulb', 'Rocket'];
```

### In development

In development, an icon that isn't in the list yet still shows, with a console hint to run `svelteSync`. A production build checks the list and fails with "Run svelteSync" when an icon is missing, so nothing silently disappears. `svelteDevAll` syncs on every Kotlin change.

### Keep every icon

If icon names come from somewhere the scan can't see, such as a database your users fill or an icon picker, keep all icons:

```kotlin
svelte {
    libraries {
        lucide {
            allIcons()
        }
    }
}
```

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `allIcons()` | off | Builds every Lucide icon into the frontend, not only the ones the scan finds |

## Images

`images()` adds SvelteKit's [`@sveltejs/enhanced-img`](https://svelte.dev/docs/kit/images#sveltejs-enhanced-img). Keep pictures next to your code, for example in `frontend/src/lib/assets`, and use `enhanced:img` instead of `img`:

```svelte
<enhanced:img src="#lib/assets/hero.png" alt="Our team" sizes="(min-width: 768px) 65ch, 100vw" />
```

### What the build makes of it

At build time, every image becomes AVIF and WebP in several widths, plus a fallback in the original format, inside a `<picture>` with `srcset`, `width` and `height`.

- Browsers download only the size and format they need.
- The layout doesn't jump while the image loads, because the size is known.
- In the notes example, a 339 KB PNG becomes an 8 KB AVIF for a laptop screen.
- The files land in `_app/immutable/`, so browsers cache them for a year like any other hashed asset.

`sizes` is the standard HTML attribute that tells the browser how wide the image is shown, so it can pick the right file.

### Images in static

Files in `frontend/static/` are copied as they are, because nothing in the build knows where they are used. Move images there to `src/lib/assets` to have them optimized.

## Full example

A task form with an icon picker, where the icon is a typed field of the DTO, and a start page with a hero image. This is how the showcase example does it.

::: code-group

```kotlin no-check [Model.kt]
import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.LucideIcon

@Serializable
data class TaskInput(
    val title: String,
    val icon: LucideIcon = LucideIcon.SquareCheck,
)

@Serializable
data class Task(
    val id: Long,
    val title: String,
    val icon: LucideIcon,
)
```

```svelte no-check [TaskForm.svelte]
<script lang="ts">
    import type { LucideIcon, TaskInput } from '#api';
    import Icon from '#icon';

    let { draft = $bindable() }: { draft: TaskInput } = $props();

    const icons: LucideIcon[] = ['SquareCheck', 'Bug', 'Lightbulb', 'Rocket', 'Flame', 'Package', 'Star'];
</script>

<fieldset>
    <legend class="mb-1">Icon</legend>
    <div class="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
        {#each icons as icon (icon)}
            <label class="btn btn-sm" class:btn-primary={draft.icon === icon}>
                <input class="sr-only" type="radio" name="task-icon" value={icon} bind:group={draft.icon} />
                <Icon name={icon} size={16} />
                <span class="sr-only">{icon}</span>
            </label>
        {/each}
    </div>
</fieldset>
```

```svelte no-check [TaskCard.svelte]
<script lang="ts">
    import type { Task } from '#api';
    import Icon from '#icon';

    let { task }: { task: Task } = $props();
</script>

<a class="link flex items-center gap-2 font-semibold" href="/tasks/{task.id}">
    <Icon name={task.icon} size={18} />
    {task.title}
</a>
```

```svelte no-check [+page.svelte]
<script lang="ts">
    import Icon from '#icon';
</script>

<section class="grid items-center gap-8 md:grid-cols-2">
    <div>
        <h1 class="text-4xl font-bold">A team board in one JAR</h1>
        <a class="btn btn-primary mt-6" href="/board"><Icon name="LayoutDashboard" size={18} /> Open the board</a>
    </div>
    <enhanced:img
        class="rounded-box h-auto w-full"
        src="#lib/assets/hero.png"
        alt="Ktor and SvelteKit working together"
        sizes="(min-width: 768px) 28rem, 100vw"
    />
</section>
```

The seven icons of the picker, `LayoutDashboard`, and every `LucideIcon.X` in your Kotlin code are found by the scan, so they are in the build. A task stored with any other icon still loads in development, and a production build tells you to run `svelteSync`.

## Use cases

- Users pick an icon for a project, a label or a category: store it as a `LucideIcon`, and it is validated on the way in.
- Navigation items with icons, defined once next to [typed routes](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/routes).
- A marketing or start page with large pictures: `enhanced:img`.
- Icons chosen from data you do not control, such as a user-filled table: [`allIcons()`](#keep-every-icon).

## Good to know

**Smaller JARs**
Without the used-icon scan, every Lucide icon would be a file in your JAR. With it, only the icons you use are built. Turn on `allIcons()` only when names come from data.

**Image processing**
Processing uses `sharp`, which comes with prebuilt binaries for Windows, macOS and Linux. The first build with many large images takes longer, and later builds reuse Vite's cache.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/charts

# Charts

`charts()` sets up [LayerChart](https://layerchart.com), a chart library for Svelte 5, so that its charts take the colors of your DaisyUI themes, light and dark, without any setup of your own. A small typed helper makes sure every series points at a real number field.

<Badge type="info" text="Gradle" /> <Badge type="warning" text="Generated files" />

This page is part of [Frontend libraries](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries).

## Quick start

```kotlin
svelte {
    libraries {
        daisyUi()
        charts()
    }
}
```

```bash
./gradlew svelteSync
```

`svelteSync` installs the package, adds LayerChart's DaisyUI preset to the generated stylesheet, and writes `src/lib/ktor-svelte/charts.ts`, imported as `#charts`. A chart is then a component in an element with a height:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { LineChart } from 'layerchart';
    import { chartSeries } from '#charts';

    interface Day {
        day: string;
        opened: number;
        closed: number;
    }

    let { days }: { days: Day[] } = $props();

    const series = chartSeries<Day>({ opened: 'Opened', closed: { label: 'Closed', color: 'success' } });
</script>

<div class="h-64">
    <LineChart data={days} x="day" {series} />
</div>
```

## Typed series with chartSeries

`chartSeries<T>` is the typed part. Its keys must be number properties of `T`, so a renamed field fails `svelteCheck` instead of drawing an empty chart.

Each entry is one of:

| Entry | Example | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A label | `opened: 'Opened'` | That label, and the color for its position |
| A label and a color | `closed: { label: 'Closed', color: 'success' }` | That label and that theme color |
| Only a color | `closed: { color: 'error' }` | The key as the label, and that color |

```ts
interface Month {
    month: string;
    revenue: number;
    costs: number;
    customers: number | null;
}

const money = chartSeries<Month>({
    revenue: { label: 'Revenue', color: 'primary' },
    costs: { label: 'Costs', color: 'error' }
});

// Fails svelteCheck: 'month' is text, not a number.
const wrong = chartSeries<Month>({ month: 'Month' });
```

A property that may be `null` or missing, such as `customers` above, still counts as a number property.

The result is an array of `{ key, label, color }`, typed as `ChartSeries<T>[]`, which is the shape LayerChart's `series` prop takes.

## Theme colors

The colors are the theme's own, as CSS variables, so a chart follows the theme when the visitor switches it. A series without a color gets the one for its position in `chartSeries`: the first series `primary`, the second `secondary`, and so on:

| Name | CSS variable |
|---|---|
| `primary` | `var(--color-primary)` |
| `secondary` | `var(--color-secondary)` |
| `accent` | `var(--color-accent)` |
| `neutral` | `var(--color-neutral)` |
| `info` | `var(--color-info)` |
| `success` | `var(--color-success)` |
| `warning` | `var(--color-warning)` |
| `error` | `var(--color-error)` |

After the eighth series the list starts again.

## chartColors for anything else

`chartColors` holds the same colors, for anything else you draw, and `ChartColor` is the union of their names:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { chartColors } from '#charts';
</script>

<svg viewBox="0 0 100 10" class="h-3 w-full">
    <rect width="70" height="10" fill={chartColors.success} />
    <rect x="70" width="30" height="10" fill={chartColors.error} />
</svg>
```

## Exports of #charts

| Export | What it is |
|---|---|
| `chartSeries<T>(lines)` | Turns labels and colors into typed series |
| `chartColors` | The eight theme colors as CSS variables |
| `ChartColor` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| ... \| 'error'` |
| `ChartSeries<T>` | One series: `key`, `label` and `color` |
| `ChartLine` | One entry of `chartSeries`: a label, or `{ label?, color? }` |
| `NumberKeys<T>` | The keys of `T` whose values are numbers |

## Full example

A dashboard with tasks per status as bars, and opened and closed tasks per day as lines. The server sends the numbers, the page draws them. It follows the board page of the showcase example.

::: code-group

```kotlin no-check [StatsRoutes.kt]
@Serializable
data class BoardStats(val todo: Int, val doing: Int, val done: Int)

@Serializable
data class DayStats(val day: String, val opened: Int, val closed: Int)

fun Route.statsRoutes() {
    get("/api/stats") {
        call.respond(BoardStats(todo = tasks.count(Status.TODO), doing = tasks.count(Status.DOING), done = tasks.count(Status.DONE)))
    }
    get("/api/stats/days") {
        call.respond(tasks.perDay(days = 14))
    }
}
```

```ts no-check [+page.ts]
import { apiWith } from '#api';
import type { PageLoad } from './$types';

export const load: PageLoad = async (event) => {
    const api = apiWith(event);
    const [stats, days] = await Promise.all([api.stats.list(), api.stats.days()]);
    return { stats, days };
};
```

```svelte no-check [+page.svelte]
<script lang="ts">
    import type { DayStats } from '#api';
    import { chartSeries } from '#charts';
    import { m } from '#i18n';
    import { BarChart, LineChart } from 'layerchart';
    import type { PageProps } from './$types';

    let { data }: PageProps = $props();

    interface StatusCount {
        status: string;
        tasks: number;
    }

    const counts = $derived<StatusCount[]>([
        { status: m.statusTodo(), tasks: data.stats.todo },
        { status: m.statusDoing(), tasks: data.stats.doing },
        { status: m.statusDone(), tasks: data.stats.done }
    ]);

    const countSeries = chartSeries<StatusCount>({ tasks: { label: m.navBoard(), color: 'primary' } });
    const daySeries = chartSeries<DayStats>({
        opened: 'Opened',
        closed: { label: 'Closed', color: 'success' }
    });
</script>

<h1 class="mb-6 text-3xl font-bold">Dashboard</h1>

<dl class="stats bg-base-200 mb-6 w-full">
    <div class="stat"><dt class="stat-title">{m.statusTodo()}</dt><dd class="stat-value text-2xl">{data.stats.todo}</dd></div>
    <div class="stat"><dt class="stat-title">{m.statusDoing()}</dt><dd class="stat-value text-2xl">{data.stats.doing}</dd></div>
    <div class="stat"><dt class="stat-title">{m.statusDone()}</dt><dd class="stat-value text-2xl">{data.stats.done}</dd></div>
</dl>

<div class="grid gap-6 md:grid-cols-2">
    <section class="card bg-base-100 border-base-300 border p-4">
        <h2 class="mb-2 font-semibold">Tasks by status</h2>
        <div class="h-48">
            <BarChart data={counts} x="status" series={countSeries} />
        </div>
    </section>
    <section class="card bg-base-100 border-base-300 border p-4">
        <h2 class="mb-2 font-semibold">Last two weeks</h2>
        <div class="h-48">
            <LineChart data={data.days} x="day" series={daySeries} />
        </div>
    </section>
</div>
```

Switch the theme, and both charts change color with the rest of the page.

## Use cases

- A dashboard or admin page with a few numbers over time.
- Counts per status or per category next to a list, as on the showcase board.
- A small bar or meter in your own SVG, in theme colors: [`chartColors`](#chartcolors-for-anything-else).

## Good to know

**charts needs daisyUi**
`charts()` needs `daisyUi()`, whose theme colors the charts take. Without it the build stops with "charts needs daisyUi()".

**Give the chart a height**
LayerChart fills its parent. Put the chart in an element with a height, such as `class="h-64"`, or it has none.

- For what the components can do, such as axes, tooltips, legends and other chart types, see LayerChart's own documentation. ktor-svelte adds the colors and the typed series, nothing else.
- The preset is LayerChart's own `layerchart/daisyui-5.css`, imported into the generated stylesheet.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/i18n

# i18n

Translations for the frontend and the server from one set of JSON files, with typed functions on both sides. A missing key or a mismatched parameter in any language fails the build, so translations can't drift. Numbers, money and dates are formatted the same way in the browser and in Kotlin.

<Badge type="info" text="Gradle" /> <Badge type="warning" text="Generated files" /> <Badge type="tip" text="Ktor plugin" />

This page is part of [Frontend libraries](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries#i18n).

## Quick start

```kotlin
svelte {
    libraries {
        i18n {
            locales("en", "de")
        }
    }
}
```

```json
{
  "app-title": "Notes",
  "server-greeting": "Hello {name}, greetings from Ktor!"
}
```

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { m } from '#i18n';
</script>

<h1>{m.appTitle()}</h1>
<p>{m.serverGreeting({ name: 'Ada' })}</p>
```

## Settings

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.gradle.LocaleStrategy

svelte {
    libraries {
        i18n {
            locales("en", "de")
            defaultLocale = "en"
            strategy = LocaleStrategy.Cookie
        }
    }
}
```

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `locales(...)` | required | The languages, as tags such as `en`, `de` or `pt-BR` |
| `defaultLocale` | The first locale | The language when nothing else decides, and the one the other files are compared with |
| `strategy` | `LocaleStrategy.Cookie` | How the language is chosen and kept, see [Strategies](#strategies) |
| `messagesDir` | `frontend/messages` | The folder with one JSON file per language |

The build stops when there is no locale, when `defaultLocale` is not one of the locales, or when a locale is not a tag such as `en` or `pt-BR`.

## Message files

Keep one JSON file per language in `frontend/messages`, such as `en.json` and `de.json`. `svelteInit` creates an empty file for every locale you configured, and never touches one that is already there. Files are flat, and `{name}` is a parameter:

```json
{
  "server-greeting": "Hello {name}, greetings from Ktor!",
  "app-title": "Notes"
}
```

- Each key becomes a function named in camel case: `app-title` is `m.appTitle()` in TypeScript and `appTitle()` in Kotlin.
- Every key must exist in every file, with the same parameters. Otherwise the build fails and names the key.
- Parameters are plain text replacements. For "1 note" and "2 notes", use [plurals](#plurals).

## In Svelte

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { getLocale, localizeHref, locales, m, setLocale } from '#i18n';
</script>

<h1>{m.appTitle()}</h1>
<p>{m.serverGreeting({ name: 'Ada' })}</p>
<a href={localizeHref('/about')}>About</a>
<button onclick={() => setLocale('de')}>Deutsch</button>
```

| Export | What it is |
|---|---|
| `m` | One function per message, typed with its parameters |
| `locales` | The configured locales, in order |
| `Locale` | The union of those locales, such as `'en' \| 'de'` |
| `defaultLocale` | The default locale |
| `getLocale()` | The current visitor's locale |
| `setLocale(locale)` | Saves the locale and shows the page in it. With cookies the page reloads, with URL prefixes it goes to the same page under the new prefix |
| `localizeHref(path)` | The path with the locale prefix when that strategy is on, and unchanged otherwise |

## In Kotlin

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.Messages
import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.messages

get("/api/hello") {
    call.respondText(call.messages.serverGreeting("Ada"))
}

val german = Messages.forLocale("de").appTitle()
```

| Name | What it is |
|---|---|
| `call.messages` | The messages in the visitor's language |
| `Messages.forLocale(locale)` | The messages in another language, for an email to someone else. An unknown locale gives the default one |
| `Messages.locales`, `Messages.defaultLocale` | The configured locales |
| `call.svelteLocale` | The visitor's locale as text, from `io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte` |
| `call.localizeHref(path)` | Like `localizeHref`, for redirects from Ktor |
| `call.formats` | [Formats](#numbers-money-and-dates) in the visitor's language |

Messages make server errors readable in the visitor's language:

```kotlin
post("/api/register") {
    if (users.isTaken(email)) {
        return@post call.respond(HttpStatusCode.Conflict, Problem(call.messages.problemEmailTaken()))
    }
}
```

## Strategies

Choose how the language is picked with `strategy`:

| Strategy | URLs | Best for | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Cookie` (default) | `/about` | Apps behind a login | Prerendered pages hold the default language and switch on load, so others can flash briefly, and search engines mostly see one language |
| `UrlPrefix` | `/de/about` | Public sites and SEO | Every language gets its own prerendered pages. Plain paths redirect to the visitor's language. Links must use `localizeHref`, or [typed routes](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/routes), or pages won't be prerendered per language |

### Cookie

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.gradle.LocaleStrategy

svelte {
    libraries {
        i18n {
            locales("en", "de")
            strategy = LocaleStrategy.Cookie
        }
    }
}
```

URLs stay as they are. `setLocale` saves the choice in a cookie for a year and reloads the page.

### URL prefix

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.gradle.LocaleStrategy

svelte {
    libraries {
        i18n {
            locales("en", "de", "fr")
            strategy = LocaleStrategy.UrlPrefix
        }
    }
}
```

Every page lives under its language, such as `/de/about`. ktor-svelte generates `src/hooks.ts` for the prefixes. Write links through `localizeHref` or typed routes:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { localizeHref } from '#i18n';
</script>

<a href={localizeHref('/about')}>About</a>
```

### How the language is chosen

On the server, `call.svelteLocale` and `call.messages` follow the same rules as the browser:

1. The URL prefix, if that strategy is on.
2. The cookie.
3. `Accept-Language`.
4. Your default locale.

`localizeHref` is safe with either strategy, and `call.localizeHref` does the same for redirects from Ktor.

## Live reload while developing

While `svelteDevAll` or `svelteDev` runs, saving a message file updates the frontend functions at once, and Vite reloads them, with no Gradle run. Under `svelteDevAll` the Kotlin `Messages` follow and the app restarts. With `svelteDev` alone, they update the next time Kotlin compiles. A file with a missing key or a mismatched parameter is reported in the console, and the last good version stays until you fix it.

## Plurals

"1 note" and "2 notes" are one message with two forms, and how many forms there are depends on the language. Write the forms into the message:

```json
{
    "notes-count": "{count, plural, =0 {No notes} one {# note} other {# notes}} in {folder}"
}
```

`#` stands for the number. The generated functions take the count as a number and pick the form for the current language, in TypeScript and in Kotlin alike:

```ts
m.notesCount({ count: notes.length, folder: 'Inbox' });
```

```kotlin
call.messages.notesCount(notes.size, "Inbox")
```

- The forms are `zero`, `one`, `two`, `few`, `many` and `other`. A language uses only some of them: English and German `one` and `other`, Russian and Polish `one`, `few`, `many` and `other`, Japanese only `other`. Every plural needs `other`.
- `=0`, `=1` and so on match one exact number, before the forms of the language. That is how "No notes" is written.
- A form can hold other placeholders, and another plural.
- Counts are whole numbers.

The same message in German:

```json
{
    "notes-count": "{count, plural, =0 {Keine Notizen} one {# Notiz} other {# Notizen}} in {folder}"
}
```

`svelteSync` checks the messages: a plural without `other`, a form the language of that file never uses, a form name that does not exist, or a count in one language that is plain text in another all stop it with the key named.

In the browser the choice of form comes from `Intl.PluralRules`. In Kotlin it comes from rules that are generated for the configured languages, checked against the browser's for the languages the plugin knows: the western and northern European ones, the Slavic and Baltic ones, Romanian, Hebrew, Arabic, and those without plural forms such as Japanese, Chinese and Korean. A language outside that list is treated like English in Kotlin.

## Numbers, money and dates

A price on the page and the same price in an email from the server should read the same. With `toLocaleString` in the browser and `NumberFormat` on the JVM they often do not: the two carry different versions of the locale data, and disagree about spaces, month names and where the currency sign goes.

With `i18n` on, both sides get the same five functions, generated from one table for the configured languages. In TypeScript they come from `#format`, in Kotlin from `call.formats`:

```ts
import { formatDate, formatDateTime, formatMoney, formatNumber, formatTime } from '#format';

formatNumber(1234567.891, 2); // 1,234,567.89   or  1.234.567,89
formatMoney(order.total, 'EUR'); // the euro sign and 1,234.50, in the order the language uses
formatDate(note.dueOn); // Mar 7, 2026      or  07.03.2026
formatDateTime(note.createdAt); // Dec 24, 2026, 3:05 PM
formatTime(note.createdAt);
```

```kotlin
val formats = call.formats
formats.formatMoney(order.total, "EUR")
formats.formatDate(note.dueOn)
formats.formatDateTime(note.createdAt, call.timeZone)
```

What is supported, and nothing else, so the two sides cannot drift apart:

| Function | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `formatNumber(value, decimals = 0)` | A number, or decimal text such as a `Decimal` | Grouped in threes, rounded half up to exactly `decimals` places. |
| `formatMoney(amount, currency)` | As above, and a currency code | The sign and decimal places of the currency for 37 common currencies, the code and two places for others. |
| `formatDate(value, style)` | An ISO date, or a `Date`. In Kotlin a `LocalDate` | `short` (3/7/26), `medium` (Mar 7, 2026, the default) or `long` (March 7, 2026). |
| `formatDateTime(value, style)` | An ISO date-time, or a `Date`. In Kotlin an `Instant` and a `ZoneId` | `short` or `medium` date with the time in hours and minutes. |
| `formatTime(value)` | As above | Hours and minutes, with AM and PM where the language uses them. |

### Date styles

```ts
formatDate(note.dueOn, 'short'); // 3/7/26
formatDate(note.dueOn, 'medium'); // Mar 7, 2026
formatDate(note.dueOn, 'long'); // March 7, 2026
formatDateTime(note.createdAt, 'short');
```

In Kotlin the style is the generated `DateStyle` enum: `DateStyle.Short`, `DateStyle.Medium` and `DateStyle.Long`.

### Another language or time zone

- The language is the visitor's, as for messages. Every function takes a locale as its last argument in TypeScript, and `Formats.forLocale(...)` gives another one in Kotlin.
- Dates and times are printed in the browser's time zone in TypeScript. In Kotlin you pass the zone, and [`call.timeZone`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#the-visitor-s-time-zone) is the visitor's.

```ts
formatMoney(invoice.total, 'CHF', 'de');
```

```kotlin
val forCustomer = Formats.forLocale(customer.locale)
forCustomer.formatDateTime(invoice.sentAt, ZoneId.of("Europe/Zurich"), DateStyle.Short)
```

### What is covered

- The table covers 64 locales. A region without its own entry uses its language, and a language that is not in the table is formatted like English.
- Not covered: weekday names, seconds, time zone names, compact numbers such as 1.2K, percent, and digits other than 0 to 9. For those, format on one side only.
- The data comes from the JDK's copy of the Unicode locale data and is fixed in each plugin version, so a new JDK or browser does not change what your app prints.

## Relative time

`timeAgo` from `#format` tells a time as its distance from now, in the visitor's language: "now", "3 minutes ago", "yesterday", "in 2 hours". It is for the browser only and uses the browser's own words, through `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`:

```ts
import { timeAgo } from '#format';

timeAgo(note.createdAt);
```

It also takes the moment to count from and a locale: `timeAgo(value, now, locale)`.

Text made once goes stale while the page stays open. With `components()`, [`<TimeAgo value={note.createdAt} />`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#timeago) keeps itself current: it renders a `<time>` element with the exact date and time as its tooltip, and every instance on the page is refreshed by one shared timer, twice a minute.

## Messages nobody translated yet

A key has to exist in every language file, or the build fails. The quick way to get past that is to paste the English text into the other files and translate later, and "later" is easy to forget. In development the [dev panel](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow) shows a **Not translated** section whenever you look at the app in another language than the default one. It lists every message on the page whose text is the same as in the default language, with its key.

Tick **Outline them on the page** and those texts get a dashed outline where they appear, so you see what a visitor in that language would read in the wrong one. The choice is remembered in your browser.

Some words are the same in two languages on purpose, such as "Name" or "Status" in English and German. They are listed too, which is why the outline is off until you ask for it.

## Messages nothing uses

A missing message fails the build, but one that is no longer used stays in every locale file and keeps being translated. `svelteVerifyMessages` lists them:

```bash
./gradlew svelteVerifyMessages
```

```text
old-banner  ->  nothing calls oldBanner() and no source names 'old-banner'
```

A message counts as used when its generated function is called anywhere in the frontend or in Kotlin, or when its key appears as a string, because it may then be looked up by name. The task only lists what it finds. Add `--strict` to fail the build instead:

```bash
./gradlew svelteVerifyMessages --strict
```

## LocaleSwitch

With `components()` on, [`LocaleSwitch`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#themetoggle-and-localeswitch) is a ready-made language select. It lists each language under its own name, such as English and Deutsch, and switches with `setLocale`:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import LocaleSwitch from '#components/LocaleSwitch.svelte';
    import { m } from '#i18n';
</script>

<LocaleSwitch label={m.settingsLanguage()} />
```

## Translating built-in texts

Some generated pieces bring English texts of their own. Translate them like this:

| Piece | How |
|---|---|
| [Error page](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#errorpage) | Add the `error-...` keys to your messages |
| [Offline page](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/installable-app#offline-page) | Add `offline-title`, `offline-text` and `offline-retry` |
| [Toasts](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#toasts) | Set `toastMessages` once at startup |
| [Confirm dialog](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#confirm-before-a-call) | Set `confirmMessages` once at startup |
| [Components](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components) | Pass `label`, `labels` and the text props, such as `empty` on `DataTable` |

## Full example

An account page in two languages: a plural, money and dates formatted in the visitor's language, and a relative time. The server sends a receipt email with the same formats, in the customer's language rather than the visitor's.

::: code-group

```json [messages/en.json]
{
  "account-title": "Your account",
  "account-orders": "{count, plural, =0 {No orders yet} one {# order} other {# orders}}",
  "account-spent": "Spent so far: {amount}",
  "account-member-since": "Member since {date}",
  "receipt-subject": "Your order from {date}",
  "receipt-total": "Total: {amount}"
}
```

```json [messages/de.json]
{
  "account-title": "Dein Konto",
  "account-orders": "{count, plural, =0 {Noch keine Bestellungen} one {# Bestellung} other {# Bestellungen}}",
  "account-spent": "Bisher ausgegeben: {amount}",
  "account-member-since": "Mitglied seit {date}",
  "receipt-subject": "Deine Bestellung vom {date}",
  "receipt-total": "Summe: {amount}"
}
```

```svelte no-check [account/+page.svelte]
<script lang="ts">
    import LocaleSwitch from '#components/LocaleSwitch.svelte';
    import TimeAgo from '#components/TimeAgo.svelte';
    import { formatDate, formatMoney } from '#format';
    import { m } from '#i18n';
    import type { PageProps } from './$types';

    let { data }: PageProps = $props();
</script>

<svelte:head>
    <title>{m.accountTitle()}</title>
</svelte:head>

<div class="mb-6 flex items-center justify-between">
    <h1 class="text-3xl font-bold">{m.accountTitle()}</h1>
    <LocaleSwitch />
</div>

<p>{m.accountMemberSince({ date: formatDate(data.account.createdAt, 'long') })}</p>
<p>{m.accountOrders({ count: data.orders.length })}</p>
<p>{m.accountSpent({ amount: formatMoney(data.account.spent, 'EUR') })}</p>

<ul class="mt-6 grid gap-2">
    {#each data.orders as order (order.id)}
        <li class="flex justify-between">
            <span>{formatMoney(order.total, order.currency)}</span>
            <TimeAgo value={order.placedAt} class="opacity-70" />
        </li>
    {/each}
</ul>
```

```kotlin no-check [Receipts.kt]
import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.DateStyle
import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.Formats
import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.Messages

fun receiptEmail(order: Order, customer: Customer): Email {
    val messages = Messages.forLocale(customer.locale)
    val formats = Formats.forLocale(customer.locale)
    val placed = formats.formatDateTime(order.placedAt, customer.zone, DateStyle.Short)
    return Email(
        to = customer.email,
        subject = messages.receiptSubject(placed),
        text = messages.receiptTotal(formats.formatMoney(order.total, order.currency)),
    )
}
```

The page and the email print the same amount and date the same way, because both come from the same table.

## Use cases

- An app behind a login, used in a few languages: the default `Cookie` strategy.
- A public site where each language should be found by search engines: [`UrlPrefix`](#url-prefix).
- Prices, invoices and dates that must read the same on the page and in emails: [`#format` and `call.formats`](#numbers-money-and-dates).
- Error messages from the server in the visitor's language: `call.messages` in a `Problem`.
- Keeping message files clean: [`svelteVerifyMessages`](#messages-nothing-uses).

## Good to know

**The build guards the files**
A missing key, a mismatched parameter or a broken plural in any language fails the build, with the key named.

**Prerendered pages with cookies**
With the `Cookie` strategy, prerendered pages hold the default language and switch on load. Use `UrlPrefix` when that brief flash, or search engines seeing one language, matters.

**Where the generated files are**
`src/lib/ktor-svelte/i18n.ts` (`#i18n`) and `src/lib/ktor-svelte/format.ts` (`#format`) in the frontend, and `Messages`, `Formats` and the `call.messages` and `call.formats` extensions in the [generated Kotlin package](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries#what-ktor-svelte-owns).

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components

# Components

`components()` generates Svelte components for the things a ktor-svelte app does all the time: form fields with validation, date inputs, enum selects, a paged table, file uploads, an error page, theme and language switches. Every project with generated files also gets helpers for modals, confirmations and toasts, a guide for coding assistants and lint rules.

<Badge type="info" text="Gradle" /> <Badge type="warning" text="Generated files" />

This page is part of [Frontend libraries](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries).

## Quick start

```kotlin
svelte {
    libraries {
        daisyUi()
        components()
    }
}
```

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { TaskInput } from '#api';
    import Field from '#components/Field.svelte';

    let draft = $state(TaskInput.empty());
</script>

<Field label="Title" bind:value={draft.title} bounds={TaskInput.bounds.title} />
```

## How the components work

`components()` generates Svelte components into `src/lib/ktor-svelte/components`, imported as `#components/...`. They are the pieces that exist because of something the plugin already generates: a component here is a few lines of markup over a generated helper, written once. They use DaisyUI's classes when `daisyUi` is on, and plain class names with a minimal style otherwise.

The files belong to the plugin and are rewritten by `svelteSync`. For a different look, write your own component on the same helper. The generated ones are short enough to copy as a start.

The components import from `#api`, so they need `generateTs = true` on the server.

| Component | Generated when | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [`Field`](#field) | `components()` | A label, an input, a hint and its validation errors |
| [`DateInput`, `DateTimeInput`](#dateinput-and-datetimeinput) | `components()` | Date and date-time inputs bound to the API's date text, `null` when empty |
| [`EnumSelect`](#enumselect) | `components()` | A select over a generated enum |
| [`DataTable`](#datatable) | `components()` | A table over a route that returns `Page<T>` |
| [`FileDrop`](#filedrop) | `components()` | A drop area with progress for an upload route |
| [`ErrorPage`](#errorpage) | `components()` | The page SvelteKit shows when a page fails, with `+error.svelte` |
| [`NavigationProgress`](#navigationprogress) | `components()` | A thin bar while a navigation waits |
| [`ThemeToggle`](#themetoggle-and-localeswitch) | `components()` and `daisyUi` | Switches the theme |
| [`LocaleSwitch`](#themetoggle-and-localeswitch) | `components()` and `i18n` | Switches the language |
| [`TimeAgo`](#timeago) | `components()` and `i18n` | "3 minutes ago" that stays current |

| Helper | Generated when | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [`modal`](#modals) | Any generated files | Opens a `<dialog>` and returns its result |
| [`confirmed`](#confirm-before-a-call) | Any generated files | Asks before a call |
| [`toast`](#toasts) | `toasts()` | Shows a short message in the corner |
| [`AGENTS.md`](#guide-for-coding-assistants) | Any generated files | A guide for coding assistants |
| [`eslint.js`](#lint-rules) | Any generated files | Lint rules for ktor-svelte mistakes |

## Field

One form field: its label, the input, an optional hint, and the validation errors.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { NoteInput } from '#api';
    import Field from '#components/Field.svelte';
    import { formState } from '#lib/api/form-state.svelte.ts';

    const form = formState<NoteInput>(NoteInput.empty(), { validate: NoteInput.validate });
</script>

<Field label="Title" bind:value={form.draft.title} bounds={NoteInput.bounds.title} errors={form.errors.title} hint="Shown in the list." />
<Field label="Text" multiline rows={4} bind:value={form.draft.body} errors={form.errors.body} />
```

| Prop | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `label` | The text of the `<label>`, tied to the input. Required |
| `bind:value` | The value, as with an `<input>` |
| `bounds` | The limits from the DTO, such as `NoteInput.bounds.title`. They become `required`, `maxlength` and the like |
| `errors` | The messages for this field, from `validate()` or from a 422 |
| `hint` | A line under the input, announced with it by screen readers |
| `multiline` | Renders a `<textarea>` |
| `id` | The input's id. Without it, one is made up |
| `class` | Added to the wrapper |
| `control` | A snippet for a control that is not a plain input, see below |

Everything else, such as `type`, `autocomplete`, `placeholder` or `rows`, goes to the input unchanged. Underneath it is the [`field` action](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/validation), so errors appear and disappear the same way as with `use:field`.

### Password and email fields

```svelte
<Field label="Email" type="email" autocomplete="email" bind:value={login.email} errors={errors.email} />
<Field
    label="New password"
    type="password"
    autocomplete="new-password"
    bind:value={password.next}
    bounds={PasswordChange.bounds.next}
    errors={errors.next}
    hint="At least {PasswordChange.bounds.next.minlength} characters."
/>
```

### A custom control

For a control that is not a plain input, pass it as the `control` snippet. It gets the `id` the label points at and the `options` for `use:field`, and the label, hint and errors stay as they are:

```svelte
<Field label="Color" errors={form.errors.color}>
    {#snippet control({ id, options })}
        <input {id} type="color" bind:value={form.draft.color} use:field={options} />
    {/snippet}
</Field>
```

## DateInput and DateTimeInput

A date from the API is an `IsoDate`, text such as `2026-12-24`, and a field that may be empty is `null`. A plain `<input type="date">` gives `''` for empty and plain text otherwise, so pages convert by hand. `DateInput` binds to the value as it is:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import DateInput from '#components/DateInput.svelte';
    import DateTimeInput from '#components/DateTimeInput.svelte';
</script>

<DateInput label="Due on" bind:value={form.draft.dueOn} errors={form.errors.dueOn} />
<DateTimeInput label="Starts at" bind:value={form.draft.startsAt} />
<DateTimeInput label="Opens at" local bind:value={form.draft.opensAt} />
```

Both take the props of `Field` (`label`, `bounds`, `errors`, `hint`, `id`, `class` and any input attribute such as `min` or `max`), and an empty input is `null`.

| Component | Kotlin type | What it sends |
|---|---|---|
| `DateInput` | `LocalDate` | The date as typed, such as `2026-12-24` |
| `DateTimeInput` | `Instant` | Shows the moment in the visitor's own time zone and stores it as the UTC text the server expects |
| `DateTimeInput local` | `LocalDateTime` | The wall-clock text as typed, with no time zone |

## MaskedInput

A text field that formats while you type, for values people read in groups: phone numbers, IBANs, dates and money. The field shows the friendly form, and the bound value is the clean one your API expects:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import MaskedInput from '#components/MaskedInput.svelte';
</script>

<MaskedInput label="Phone" mask="phone" bind:value={form.draft.phone} />
<MaskedInput label="IBAN" mask="iban" bind:value={form.draft.iban} />
<MaskedInput label="Birthday" mask="date" bind:value={form.draft.birthday} />
<MaskedInput label="Price" mask="money" bind:value={form.draft.price} />
```

| `mask` | You see while typing | Bound value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `phone` | `+49 301 234 567`, `0301 2345 67` | `+49301234567`: digits and a leading `+` |
| `iban` | `DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00`, in capitals | `DE89370400440532013000` |
| `date` | `24.12.2026` in German, `12/24/2026` in American English | `2026-12-24`, an `IsoDate`, once the date is complete and real; `null` before |
| `money` | `1.234.567,8` in German, `1,234,567.8` in English | `1234567.8`, a plain decimal for a [`Decimal`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/typescript#money-and-durations) field |

| Prop | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | required | The label, as for `Field` |
| `mask` | required | `'phone'`, `'iban'`, `'date'`, `'money'`, or your own `Mask` |
| `value` | | The clean value, `bind:value`; `null` while the field is empty or a date is incomplete |
| `locale` | the page's `lang` | Which order and separators `date` and `money` use |
| `bounds`, `errors`, `hint`, `class` | | As for `Field` |

- The caret stays after the same character you typed, even when a space or a separator is added in front of it.
- The field sets `inputmode`, so phones show the number or phone keyboard.
- Money keeps a decimal separator you just typed, so `1234,` stays on screen while the value is `1234`. It never goes through a JavaScript number, so large amounts keep every digit.
- When you leave the field, a complete value is shown in its tidy form. An incomplete date stays as typed, with `null` as the value, so the form's validation can say it is required.
- For another format, pass an object with `show(clean)`, `retype(typed)`, `clean(typed)`, `keeps(character)` and `inputMode`, the same shape `masks.ts` exports for the four built-in ones.

## ErrorSummary

A box that lists every error of a form, each a link that moves focus to its field. Put it above or below the submit button of a long form:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import ErrorSummary from '#components/ErrorSummary.svelte';
</script>

<ErrorSummary errors={form.errors} labels={{ name: 'Name', email: 'Email', password: 'Password' }} />
```

| Prop | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `errors` | required | The errors per field, usually `form.errors` |
| `labels` | `{}` | The text to show for each field; the field name when there is none |
| `title` | `Please check these fields:` | The heading of the box; pass a message for other languages |
| `class` | | More classes for the box |

- It shows nothing while there are no errors, and is announced as an alert when it appears.
- A link finds its field by `id` first, then by `name`, so give the fields an `id` or `name` equal to the property, as `<Field id="email" ...>` does.
- With DaisyUI it is an `alert alert-error`; without, it has a small style of its own.

## PasswordStrength

A meter and a checklist under a password field, driven by the same rule the server enforces with [`@Rule.StrongPassword`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/validation#ready-made-rules). Nobody has to guess what "strong" means, and the browser can never accept a password the server will refuse:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import Field from '#components/Field.svelte';
    import PasswordStrength from '#components/PasswordStrength.svelte';
</script>

<Field label="New password" type="password" bind:value={form.draft.password} errors={form.errors.password} />
<PasswordStrength password={form.draft.password} />
```

| Prop | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `password` | required | The password typed so far |
| `requirements` | `{}` | Your own text per requirement, keyed by the English text, such as `{ 'a digit': m.passwordDigit() }` |
| `label` | `Password strength` | Accessible name of the meter |
| `strongText` | `Strong enough.` | Announced once every rule is met |
| `class` | | More classes |

The rules come from the generated client, so you can also use them without the component:

```ts
import { passwordMessage, passwordRules, passwordStrength } from '#api';

const strength = passwordStrength('Correct1horse');
strength.score;
strength.strong;
strength.missing.map((rule) => rule.requirement);
```

| Name | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `passwordRules` | Every part of the rule: `pattern` and `requirement`, such as `at least 10 characters`, `a lowercase letter`, `an uppercase letter`, `a digit` |
| `passwordStrength(password)` | `met`, `missing`, `score` from 0 to 1, and `strong` when nothing is missing |
| `passwordMessage` | The message the server answers with when the rule fails |

- Each rule is shown with a `+` or a `-` and a color, so it does not depend on color alone.
- Screen readers hear the meter's value and, once, that the password is strong enough, instead of every keystroke.
- Use it only for a property with `@Rule.StrongPassword`; for your own rule, write your own list.

## NumberInput

A number field that groups digits and uses the decimal separator of the visitor's language, and never rounds. Bind it to a [`Decimal`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/typescript#money-and-durations) for money and exact amounts, or to a `number`:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import NumberInput from '#components/NumberInput.svelte';
</script>

<NumberInput label="Price" bind:value={form.draft.price} />
<NumberInput label="Rate" bind:value={form.draft.rate} fractionDigits={4} />
<NumberInput label="Seats" bind:value={form.draft.seats} fractionDigits={0} number />
```

| Prop | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | | `bind:value`; a `Decimal` string such as `"1234.5"`, or a `number`; `null` while empty |
| `fractionDigits` | `2` | How many digits after the separator can be typed; `0` for whole numbers, where the separator is not accepted at all |
| `number` | `false` | Bind a `number` instead of a string; also on by itself when the value already is a number |
| `locale` | the page's `lang` | Which separators to use |
| `label`, `bounds`, `errors`, `hint`, `class` | | As for `Field` |

- In German, typing `1234567,8` shows `1.234.567,8` and binds `"1234567.8"`; in English the same amount is `1,234,567.8`.
- A `Decimal` never goes through a JavaScript number, so `12345678901234567890.1234` keeps every digit. Use `number` only for values that fit a double, such as counts.
- The keyboard on phones is the decimal one, and the caret stays where you are typing, as in [MaskedInput](#maskedinput), which this component builds on.

## Breadcrumbs

A ready breadcrumb trail for the open page, built from the titles your pages declare in [`_nav`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/routes#menu-titles-and-breadcrumbs). It comes with `components()` when `routes()` is on too:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import Breadcrumbs from '#components/Breadcrumbs.svelte';

    let { data } = $props();
</script>

<Breadcrumbs current={data.task.title} />
```

On `/admin/tasks` this shows "Home / Admin / All tasks", each part a link except the last.

| Prop | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `current` | | The name of the open page, such as a record's title. It replaces the page's own title, or is added when the page has none, as for `/tasks/[id]` |
| `labels` | `{}` | Other names for parts of the trail, keyed by their link, such as `{ '/projects/7': project.name }` |
| `label` | `Breadcrumb` | The accessible name of the `<nav>`; pass a message for other languages |
| `class` | | More classes |

- The trail follows the page's place in your routes: every parent folder with a title is a step. Groups such as `(app)` are left out.
- It shows nothing on a page with no parents, so you can put it in a layout.
- The current page is marked with `aria-current="page"` and is not a link.
