- With DaisyUI it uses the `breadcrumbs` class; without, a small style with `/` between the parts.

## EnumSelect

A `<select>` over a generated enum object:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { Status } from '#api';
    import EnumSelect from '#components/EnumSelect.svelte';
</script>

<EnumSelect label="Status" options={Status} bind:value={form.draft.status} labels={{ TODO: 'To do', DONE: 'Done' }} placeholder="Any" />
```

It lists every value of the enum, so a value added in Kotlin appears after the next `svelteGenerateTs`. The bound value has the enum's type, so no cast is needed.

| Prop | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `label` | The label. Required |
| `options` | The generated enum object, such as `Status` |
| `bind:value` | The chosen value, or `null` |
| `labels` | The text to show per value, as text or as a function for translations. A value without one shows its name |
| `placeholder` | Adds a first option that stands for `null` |
| `bounds`, `errors`, `hint`, `id`, `class` | As on `Field` |

Translated labels are functions, so they follow the language:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { Priority } from '#api';
    import EnumSelect from '#components/EnumSelect.svelte';
    import { m } from '#i18n';

    const priorityLabels: Record<Priority, () => string> = {
        LOW: m.priorityLow,
        NORMAL: m.priorityNormal,
        HIGH: m.priorityHigh
    };
</script>

<EnumSelect label={m.fieldPriority()} options={Priority} labels={priorityLabels} bind:value={draft.priority} />
```

## DataTable

A table over any route that returns [`Page<T>`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/pagination). It loads the pages, and shows a line while it loads, when there is nothing, and when a load failed, with a button to try again.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { api } from '#api';
    import DataTable from '#components/DataTable.svelte';

    let search = $state('');
</script>

<input type="search" bind:value={search} aria-label="Search" />
<DataTable
    load={api.notes.list}
    query={{ search, limit: '20' }}
    key={(note) => note.id}
    columns={[
        { key: 'title', label: 'Title' },
        { key: 'createdAt', label: 'Created', text: (note) => new Date(note.createdAt).toLocaleDateString() },
        { id: 'size', label: 'Size', text: (note) => `${note.body.length} characters` }
    ]}
/>
```

`load` is the generated function of the route, and the rows have the type it returns. So a column's `key` must be a property of the item, a typo fails `svelteCheck`, and `text` gets the typed item. A column that is not one property has an `id` and a `text` instead.

| Prop | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `load` | The generated function of a route that returns `Page<T>` |
| `columns` | The headers, and what each cell shows |
| `query` | The query parameters besides the cursor. When they change, the table loads again from the start |
| `key` | A stable id per row, such as `(note) => note.id` |
| `paging` | `'more'` (the default) adds rows with a Load more button. `'pages'` shows one page with Previous and Next |
| `first` | A first page that a `load` function already fetched, so the table does not fetch it again |
| `caption` | A caption for the table |
| `row` | A snippet that renders the cells of one row, see below |
| `empty`, `loading`, `more`, `previous`, `next`, `retry` | The texts, in English unless given: "Nothing here yet.", "Loading", "Load more", "Previous", "Next", "Try again" |
| `class` | Added to the wrapper |

### Choosing columns

With `chooser`, a "Columns" menu above the table lets people hide columns and change their order. With `remember`, the choice is kept in the browser for next time:

```svelte
<DataTable load={api.tasks.list} columns={columns} chooser remember="admin-tasks" />
```

| Prop | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chooser` | `false` | Shows the menu with a checkbox per column and buttons to move it up or down |
| `remember` | | A name for this table. The order and the hidden columns are kept in `localStorage` under `ktor-svelte-table:<name>` |
| `columnsLabel`, `moveUp`, `moveDown` | `Columns`, `Up`, `Down` | The texts of the menu, for other languages |

- The last visible column cannot be hidden.
- A column you add to `columns` later shows up at the end; one you remove is forgotten.
- The move buttons say which column they move, such as "Up: Status", for screen readers.
- A [custom `row`](#cells-with-markup) gets the visible columns as its second argument, `{#snippet row(task, columns)}`, so its cells can follow the choice.

### Selecting rows and acting on them

Give the table `actions`, and every row gets a checkbox. A bar above the table shows how many are chosen and a button per action, which calls your function for each chosen row:

```svelte
<DataTable
    load={api.tasks.list}
    key={(task) => task.id}
    {columns}
    actions={[
        { label: 'Mark as done', run: (task) => api.tasks.status(task.id, { status: 'DONE' }) },
        { label: 'Delete', run: (task) => api.tasks.delete(task.id), confirm: 'Delete the chosen tasks?' }
    ]}
/>
```

| Prop | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | `[]` | `{ label, run, confirm? }` per action; `run` is called once per chosen row, one after the other |
| `key` | | Needed to keep choices across pages and for "Select every page" |
| `selectRow` | `Select all on this page: <first column>` | The accessible name of a row's checkbox |
| `selectPage`, `selectEverything`, `clearSelection` | `Select all on this page`, `Select every page`, `Clear` | Button and checkbox texts |
| `selectedText`, `workingText`, `doneText` | `2 selected`, `Working: 1 of 2`, `Done: 2 of 2 worked.` | Functions that build the status texts, for other languages |

- The checkbox in the header chooses every row on the page, and shows a mixed state when only some are chosen.
- "Select every page" loads the remaining pages and chooses everything, so an action can run over the whole list, not only what is visible.
- While an action runs, the bar counts up and the checkboxes are locked. When it ends, the bar says how many calls worked, the choice is cleared and the table reloads.
- A failing call does not stop the others; with [toasts](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/components#toasts) on, each failure is shown too.
- `confirm` asks with the browser's dialog before the action starts.

### Sorting by a click on the header

Mark a column with `sort`, and its header becomes a button. The first click sorts ascending, the second descending, the third goes back to the order of the route:

```svelte
<DataTable
    load={api.tasks.list}
    columns={[
        { key: 'title', label: 'Title', sort: true },
        { key: 'createdAt', label: 'Created', sort: 'created' }
    ]}
    sortParam="sort"
/>
```

| | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| With `sortParam` | The table asks the route again with `?sort=title` or `?sort=-title` (a leading `-` for descending), from the first page. Use this for lists with many pages; the route decides how to sort. `sort: 'created'` sends that name instead of the column's key |
| Without `sortParam` | The rows that are loaded are sorted in the browser, numbers as numbers and text in the visitor's language. This suits short lists that fit on one page; on a list with more pages, only the loaded rows are sorted |

- The header gets `aria-sort` (`ascending` or `descending`), and a small `^` or `v` shows the direction.
- With `sortParam`, the route reads the value like any other query parameter, such as `call.queryParameters["sort"]`; list it in `describe` to have it typed.

### When there is nothing to show

An empty table is either a fresh start or a filter that matches nothing, and people need to hear different things. The table tells them apart by its `query`: any value other than `cursor` and `limit` counts as a filter.

```svelte
<DataTable
    load={api.tasks.list}
    query={{ search }}
    {columns}
    empty="No tasks yet."
    noResults="No task matches your search."
>
    {#snippet emptyAction()}
        <a class="btn btn-primary" href={routes.tasksNew()}>Create the first task</a>
    {/snippet}
</DataTable>
```

| Prop | Default | When it shows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `empty` | `Nothing here yet.` | No rows and no filter |
| `emptyAction` | | A snippet under `empty`, such as a button that creates the first item; not shown for a filter |
| `noResults` | `Nothing matches this filter.` | No rows while a filter is set |
| `filtered` | worked out from `query` | Set it yourself when the filter lives elsewhere, for example in the route's path |

The block carries `data-empty="none"` or `data-empty="filtered"`, handy for tests and styles.

### Placeholder rows while loading

While the first page loads, the table shows a few grey rows shaped like its columns instead of an empty box, so the page does not jump when the data arrives. Later loads keep the rows you already see.

```svelte
<DataTable load={api.tasks.list} {columns} skeletonRows={5} />
```

- `skeletonRows` sets how many, `3` by default, and `0` turns them off.
- The rows are `aria-hidden`; screen readers still hear the `loading` text.
- With DaisyUI they use its `skeleton` class; without, a small pulsing bar of their own. Each carries `data-skeleton`.

### Long lists

With `virtual`, the table sits in a box of its own height, renders only the rows in view, and loads the next page when you scroll near the end. Thousands of rows stay as quick as twenty:

```svelte
<DataTable load={api.tasks.list} query={{ limit: 50 }} key={(task) => task.id} {columns} virtual={{ rowHeight: 40, height: '28rem' }} />
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rowHeight` | required | The height of one row in pixels; every row gets exactly this height |
| `height` | `24rem` | The height of the scrolling box, any CSS length |
| `overscan` | `5` | Rows rendered above and below the visible ones, so fast scrolling does not show gaps |

- The paging buttons go away; scrolling is the paging.
- The table keeps `aria-rowcount` with the number of loaded rows, and each row its `aria-rowindex`, so screen readers still know where they are.
- Keep cells to one line, since rows have a fixed height. For text that wraps, use normal paging instead.
- Rows that can be [chosen](#selecting-rows-and-acting-on-them) and [sorted](#sorting-by-a-click-on-the-header) work the same; sorting in the browser sorts the rows loaded so far.

### Opening a row, with the mouse or the keyboard

Give the table `onopen`, and each row opens with a click or with Enter. The rows become one stop in the tab order, and the arrow keys move between them:

```svelte
<DataTable load={api.tasks.list} {columns} onopen={(task) => goto(routes.tasksId({ id: task.id }))} />
```

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Reaches the table once, on the last row you were on |
| Arrow down, Arrow up | The next or the previous row |
| Home, End | The first or the last loaded row |
| Page down, Page up | Ten rows on, or a box height with [`virtual`](#long-lists) |
| Enter | Calls `onopen` with that row |

- Clicks and keys on controls inside a row, such as the [selection](#selecting-rows-and-acting-on-them) checkbox or a link in a custom cell, do their own thing and do not open the row.
- With `virtual`, moving to a row that is not rendered scrolls to it first.
- The focused row shows an outline; with DaisyUI it also highlights on hover.

### Cells with markup

For cells with markup, such as a link or a button, pass a `row` snippet. It renders the cells of one row, and `columns` then only gives the headers:

```svelte
<DataTable load={api.notes.list} columns={[{ key: 'title', label: 'Title' }, { id: 'open', label: '' }]}>
    {#snippet row(note)}
        <td>{note.title}</td>
        <td><a href={routes.notesId({ id: note.id })}>Open</a></td>
    {/snippet}
</DataTable>
```

### Reloading

After a change elsewhere on the page, `bind:this` the table and call its `reload()`:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    let table = $state<{ reload(): Promise<void> }>();

    async function remove(id: number) {
        await api.notes.delete(id);
        await table?.reload();
    }
</script>

<DataTable bind:this={table} load={api.notes.list} columns={[{ key: 'title', label: 'Title' }]} />
```

### A server-rendered first page

```ts
export const load: PageLoad = async (event) => {
    return { first: await apiWith(event).notes.list({ limit: '20' }) };
};
```

```svelte
<DataTable load={api.notes.list} query={{ limit: '20' }} first={data.first} columns={[{ key: 'title', label: 'Title' }]} />
```

The route's pages are cursors, so there are no page numbers: the table can go forward and back, not jump.

## FileDrop

A drop area with a file input for an [upload route](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/uploads). Files can be dropped on it or chosen, and each one is shown while it travels: a preview for images, the name and size, a progress bar, and the reason when it was refused.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { api, uploadRules } from '#api';
    import FileDrop from '#components/FileDrop.svelte';

    let documents = $state<StoredFile[]>([]);
</script>

<FileDrop
    label="Add documents"
    hint="PDF or images, up to 5 MiB each."
    multiple
    rules={uploadRules['documents.create']}
    upload={(file, options) => api.documents.create({ file }, options)}
    onuploaded={(stored) => (documents = [...documents, stored])}
/>
```

| Prop | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `upload` | Sends one file. Pass the route's generated function, and hand it the `options` it is given: they carry the progress |
| `label` | The label of the file input. Required |
| `rules` | The route's entry in `uploadRules`. Its types become the input's `accept` |
| `hint` | A line under the input |
| `multiple` | Takes several files. They are sent one after another, each in its own request |
| `onuploaded` | Called with the route's answer and the file, after each one that went through |
| `problem` | Turns a failed upload into the text to show, for your own wording or language. Without it the server's message is shown |
| `uploading` | The start of the progress bar's accessible name, `Uploading` unless given |
| `disabled`, `id`, `class` | As on an input |

The route's rules are checked before a file is sent, as with any call to the generated function, so a file that is too large or of the wrong type is refused at once and nothing is uploaded. A file that went through leaves the list, and one that failed stays with its reason until the next files are chosen.

### Translated problems

The showcase attaches files to a task and names the problem in the visitor's language:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { api, errorMessage, isUploadError, uploadRules, type Attachment } from '#api';
    import FileDrop from '#components/FileDrop.svelte';
    import { m } from '#i18n';

    let { task, attachments = $bindable() }: { task: Task; attachments: Attachment[] } = $props();

    function uploadProblem(error: unknown): string {
        if (!isUploadError(error)) return errorMessage(error);
        return error.body.code === 'upload.tooLarge' ? m.problemFileTooLarge() : m.problemFileType();
    }
</script>

<FileDrop
    label={m.attachmentsAdd()}
    uploading={m.attachmentsUploading()}
    multiple
    rules={uploadRules['tasks.attachments']}
    upload={(file, options) => api.tasks.attachments(task.id, { file }, options)}
    problem={uploadProblem}
    onuploaded={(stored) => (attachments = [...attachments, ...stored])}
/>
```

## ErrorPage

`components()` also writes `src/routes/+error.svelte`, the page SvelteKit shows when a page cannot be shown. It is three lines around `<ErrorPage />`, which shows:

- the status, such as 404
- the message: the one the server sent in the error body when a call failed, the one you passed to `error(...)`, and otherwise a sentence for 404, 403, 401 or anything else
- the request ID for a status of 500 and above, so a visitor can quote it and you can find the request in the log
- a link back to the start page, `home="/"` unless you pass another

| Prop | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `home` | `"/"` | Where the link back leads |

A `load` function no longer has to translate a failed call into a page error. Let it throw:

```ts
export const load: PageLoad = async (event) => {
    return { note: await apiWith(event).notes.get(event.params.id) };
};
```

When the server answers 404 with `{ "message": "That note does not exist." }`, the error page shows 404 and that message. This works through `handleError` in `src/hooks.client.ts`, which `svelteSync` writes. It puts the status, message, request ID and [error code](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#error-codes) of a failed call into `page.error`, typed through `App.Error`, so your own components can read `page.error.code` too.

The sentences are English until your messages have their keys. With `i18n` on, add the ones you want translated and run `svelteSync`:

| Key | Default |
|---|---|
| `error-not-found` | This page does not exist. |
| `error-forbidden` | You are not allowed to see this page. |
| `error-sign-in` | Sign in to see this page. |
| `error-failed` | Something went wrong. Please try again. |
| `error-request-id` | Request ID: |
| `error-home` | Back to the start page |

Your own files win. If `src/routes/+error.svelte` exists and is not the generated one, it is left alone, and you can use `<ErrorPage />` inside it or not. To change the generated one, remove its first line, and it is yours. The same goes for `src/hooks.client.ts` when `toasts()` is off: keep your own and add `export { handleError } from '#lib/ktor-svelte/errors.ts';` to it.

An error page of your own that keeps the generated content, inside the app's frame:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import ErrorPage from '#components/ErrorPage.svelte';
    import { page } from '$app/state';
</script>

<div class="mx-auto max-w-xl py-16 text-center">
    <ErrorPage home="/board" />
    {#if page.error?.code === 'NotYours'}
        <p class="mt-4">Ask the person who created it to share it with you.</p>
    {/if}
</div>
```

## ThemeToggle and LocaleSwitch

The theme and i18n helpers already know the themes and languages you configured. These two components put them on the page, so a new app has both switches from the start:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import LocaleSwitch from '#components/LocaleSwitch.svelte';
    import ThemeToggle from '#components/ThemeToggle.svelte';
</script>

```

`ThemeToggle` is generated when `daisyUi` is on. With two themes it is a button that flips between them, with more it is a `<select>`. It applies the theme at once and remembers it, as [`setTheme`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/styling#switch-themes-in-the-frontend) does.

`LocaleSwitch` is generated when `i18n` is on. It lists each language under its own name, such as English and Deutsch, and switches with [`setLocale`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/i18n#in-svelte).

| Prop | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `label` | `Theme`, `Language` | The accessible name. Pass a translated one |
| `labels` | none | An object from theme or language to the text to show, to name single entries yourself |
| `id` | none | The id of the button or select |
| `class` | none | Added to the button or select |

```svelte
<ThemeToggle id="theme" class="w-36" label={m.settingsTheme()} labels={{ 'shadcn-light': 'Light', 'shadcn-dark': 'Dark' }} />
<LocaleSwitch id="locale" class="w-28" label={m.settingsLanguage()} />
```

## TimeAgo

"3 minutes ago", "yesterday", in the visitor's language, and kept current while the page stays open. Generated when `i18n` is on.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import TimeAgo from '#components/TimeAgo.svelte';
</script>

<p>{comment.author.name} <TimeAgo class="opacity-70" value={comment.createdAt} /></p>
```

| Prop | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `value` | An ISO date-time text, or a `Date` |
| `class` | Added to the `<time>` element |

It renders a `<time>` element with the exact date and time as its tooltip, and every instance on the page is refreshed by one shared timer, twice a minute. The words come from [`timeAgo`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/i18n#relative-time).

## NavigationProgress

A thin bar at the top of the page while SvelteKit navigates, which includes the time a `load` function waits for the server. Without it, a click on a link to a slow page looks like nothing happened. Put it in the root layout, once:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import NavigationProgress from '#components/NavigationProgress.svelte';

    let { children } = $props();
</script>

{@render children()}
```

| Prop | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `delay` | `150` | Milliseconds a navigation must take before the bar appears, so quick ones do not flash |
| `label` | `Loading page` | The accessible name of the progress bar |
| `class` | none | Added to the bar |

- Its color is the theme's primary color with DaisyUI, and the text color otherwise. Set the CSS variable `--ktor-svelte-progress` to choose another.
- It is announced as a progress bar with the name `label`.
- With "reduce motion" set in the visitor's system, it is a still line.

## Modals

A `<dialog>` normally needs a `bind:this`, a `showModal()` and a way to learn how it was closed. `modal()` from `#lib/ktor-svelte/modal.ts` is those three:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { modal } from '#lib/ktor-svelte/modal.ts';

    const rename = modal<string>();
    let name = $state('');

    async function askForName() {
        const chosen = await rename.open();
        if (chosen) console.log('renamed to', chosen);
    }
</script>

<button onclick={askForName}>Rename</button>

<dialog class="modal" use:rename.attach>
    <div class="modal-box">
        <input bind:value={name} aria-label="New name" />
        <button onclick={() => rename.close(name)}>Save</button>
        <button onclick={() => rename.close()}>Cancel</button>
    </div>
</dialog>
```

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `modal<T>(options)` | Makes a modal whose result has the type `T` |
| `attach` | The action for the `<dialog>`: `use:rename.attach` |
| `open()` | Shows the dialog and returns a promise of the result |
| `close(result)` | Closes it, and the promise resolves with `result` |
| `isOpen` | Whether it is showing |
| `closeOnBackdrop: false` | An option that keeps a click beside the box from closing it |

`open()` resolves with what `close(result)` was given, or with `undefined` when the dialog was closed any other way: `close()` without a value, Escape, or a click beside the box. Calling `open()` while it is already open returns the same promise.

The markup is yours, so it works with DaisyUI's `modal` classes, as above, and with a plain `<dialog>`.

## Confirm before a call

To only ask a yes or no question before a call, use `confirmed` from `#lib/ktor-svelte/confirm.ts`, which brings its own dialog:

```ts
import { confirmed } from '#lib/ktor-svelte/confirm.ts';

const deleted = await confirmed('Delete this note?', () => api.notes.delete(id), {
    details: 'It cannot be restored.',
    confirm: 'Delete',
    danger: true
});
```

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `details` | A line under the question |
| `confirm`, `cancel` | The button labels. They default to `confirmMessages.confirm` and `confirmMessages.cancel` |
| `danger` | A red confirm button, with the focus on Cancel |

With DaisyUI on, the question is a modal in your theme that stays open while the call runs and shows its error. Without DaisyUI it is the browser's own `confirm`. The full description is in [Ask before a call](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#ask-before-a-call).

## Toasts

With `toasts()` on, failed API calls show up as toasts by themselves, see [Show errors automatically](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#show-errors-automatically). You can also show your own, from `#lib/ktor-svelte/toasts.ts`:

```ts
import { toast } from '#lib/ktor-svelte/toasts.ts';

toast('Saved.', { kind: 'success' });
toast('Note archived.', { action: { label: 'Undo', run: restore } });
toast('We just shipped an update.', { duration: 0, action: { label: 'Reload', run: () => location.reload() } });
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `'info'` | `'info'`, `'success'`, `'warning'` or `'error'` |
| `duration` | `5000` | Milliseconds until it goes away. `0` keeps it until it is closed |
| `action` | none | A button: `{ label, run }`. A click runs it and closes the toast |

- With DaisyUI, toasts are DaisyUI alerts in your theme. Otherwise they bring their own small style.
- Errors and warnings are announced to screen readers as alerts, the others politely.
- Change the built-in texts, such as the network message or the close button's name, through `toastMessages`.
- The server can send toasts too, with `call.toast(...)`, see [Toasts from the server](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#toasts-from-the-server).

## Full example

A "new task" form built from generated components, with validation in the browser and from the server, a confirmation before deleting, and toasts. It uses the showcase's `TaskInput`:

::: code-group

```kotlin no-check [Model.kt]
import io.ktor.openapi.JsonSchema

@Serializable
data class TaskInput(
    @Trim
    @JsonSchema.MinLength(1)
    @JsonSchema.MaxLength(120)
    val title: String,
    @JsonSchema.MaxLength(4000)
    val description: String = "",
    val priority: Priority = Priority.NORMAL,
    val dueOn: LocalDate? = null,
    val remindAt: Instant? = null,
)
```

```svelte no-check [tasks/new/+page.svelte]
<script lang="ts">
    import { goto } from '$app/navigation';
    import { api, Priority, TaskInput } from '#api';
    import DateInput from '#components/DateInput.svelte';
    import DateTimeInput from '#components/DateTimeInput.svelte';
    import EnumSelect from '#components/EnumSelect.svelte';
    import Field from '#components/Field.svelte';
    import { m } from '#i18n';
    import { formState } from '#lib/api/form-state.svelte.ts';
    import { confirmed } from '#lib/ktor-svelte/confirm.ts';
    import { toast } from '#lib/ktor-svelte/toasts.ts';
    import { routes } from '#routes';

    const form = formState<TaskInput>({ ...TaskInput.empty(), priority: 'NORMAL' }, { validate: TaskInput.validate });

    const priorityLabels: Record<Priority, () => string> = {
        LOW: m.priorityLow,
        NORMAL: m.priorityNormal,
        HIGH: m.priorityHigh
    };

    async function create(event: SubmitEvent) {
        event.preventDefault();
        const task = await form.submit((draft) => api.tasks.create(draft));
        if (!task) return;
        toast(m.taskCreated({ title: task.title }), { kind: 'success' });
        await goto(routes.tasksId({ id: task.id }));
    }

    async function discard() {
        if (!form.dirty) return goto(routes.board());
        const sure = await confirmed(m.taskDiscardQuestion(), async () => true, { confirm: m.taskDiscard(), danger: true });
        if (sure) await goto(routes.board());
    }
</script>

<h1 class="mb-6 text-3xl font-bold">{m.navNewTask()}</h1>

<form class="grid max-w-xl gap-3" novalidate onsubmit={create}>
    <Field label={m.fieldTitle()} bind:value={form.draft.title} bounds={TaskInput.bounds.title} errors={form.errors.title} />
    <Field
        label={m.fieldDescription()}
        multiline
        rows={4}
        bind:value={form.draft.description}
        bounds={TaskInput.bounds.description}
        errors={form.errors.description}
        hint={m.taskDescriptionHint()}
    />
    <div class="grid gap-3 sm:grid-cols-3">
        <EnumSelect label={m.fieldPriority()} options={Priority} labels={priorityLabels} bind:value={form.draft.priority} />
        <DateInput label={m.fieldDueOn()} bind:value={form.draft.dueOn} errors={form.errors.dueOn} />
        <DateTimeInput label={m.fieldRemindAt()} bind:value={form.draft.remindAt} errors={form.errors.remindAt} />
    </div>
    <div class="flex gap-2">
        <button class="btn btn-primary" type="submit" disabled={form.submitting}>{m.taskCreate()}</button>
        <button class="btn btn-ghost" type="button" onclick={discard}>{m.taskDiscard()}</button>
    </div>
</form>
```

```svelte no-check [+layout.svelte]
<script lang="ts">
    import LocaleSwitch from '#components/LocaleSwitch.svelte';
    import NavigationProgress from '#components/NavigationProgress.svelte';
    import ThemeToggle from '#components/ThemeToggle.svelte';
    import '#lib/ktor-svelte/app.css';
    import { m } from '#i18n';

    let { children } = $props();
</script>

<NavigationProgress label={m.navLoading()} />

<header class="navbar bg-base-100 border-base-300 gap-2 border-b px-4">
    <span class="flex-1 text-lg font-semibold">{m.appTitle()}</span>
    <ThemeToggle class="w-36" label={m.settingsTheme()} />
    <LocaleSwitch class="w-28" label={m.settingsLanguage()} />
</header>

<main class="mx-auto my-8 max-w-4xl px-4">
    {@render children()}
</main>
```

- The `JsonSchema` bounds on the DTO reach the inputs through `bounds`, so the browser knows the title is required and at most 120 characters. See [Validation](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/validation).
- `form.submit` runs `validate` first and sends nothing while a field is invalid. When the server still answers 422, its messages land in `form.errors` and show under the fields.
- `form.submit` resolves to `undefined` when the call failed, and with `toasts()` on any other failure shows as a toast by itself, so `create` only handles success.

## Guide for coding assistants

`svelteSync` also writes `src/lib/ktor-svelte/AGENTS.md`, a short guide for coding assistants such as Claude Code, Cursor or Copilot. It tells them what they otherwise get wrong in a project like this:

- which files are generated and must not be edited, and which Gradle setting or Kotlin route to change instead
- that the backend is called through the typed client from `#api`, with `apiWith(event)` in `load` functions, never through a hand-written `fetch`
- the libraries you turned on and how to use them: icons, messages, themes, toasts
- your pages by their typed route name, when `routes()` is on
- the Gradle commands to run

It describes your project, not ktor-svelte in general: a project without i18n gets no word about messages. Like every generated file it is kept current by `svelteSync` and checked by `svelteVerifySync`.

Assistants that read nested `AGENTS.md` files find it when they work in the frontend. To make sure, link it from the file your assistant reads at the project root, such as `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`:

```md
Read `frontend/src/lib/ktor-svelte/AGENTS.md` before changing anything.
```

Projects created by the setup script have that `AGENTS.md` already. ktor-svelte never edits a root `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` of yours.

## Lint rules

Next to the generated files, `svelteSync` writes `src/lib/ktor-svelte/eslint.js`, a small ESLint plugin with rules for mistakes that are easy to make in a ktor-svelte app. They show up in the editor while you type:

| Rule | What it flags |
|---|---|
| `ktor-svelte/no-string-page-links` | An `href`, `goto` or `redirect` that leads to one of your pages as a string, when [typed routes](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/routes) are on |
| `ktor-svelte/fetch-in-load` | An API call inside a `load` function that goes through neither `apiWith(event)` nor `{ fetch }`, which SvelteKit reports at runtime as `window_fetch_in_load` |
| `ktor-svelte/no-error-body-message` | Reading `error.body.message` from a caught error without narrowing it with `isApiError` first, where [`errorMessage`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api) is the safe choice |

A project made by the setup script has them wired in. In an existing project, add two lines to `eslint.config.js`:

```js
import ktorSvelte from './src/lib/ktor-svelte/eslint.js';

export default [
    ...ktorSvelte.configs.recommended
];
```

All three are warnings. To turn one off or make it an error, set it like any other rule:

```js
import ktorSvelte from './src/lib/ktor-svelte/eslint.js';

export default [
    ...ktorSvelte.configs.recommended,
    { rules: { 'ktor-svelte/fetch-in-load': 'error' } }
];
```

The page list inside the file follows your routes, so the first rule stays current the same way `routes.ts` does. For a one-off check across the whole project, and to rewrite string links automatically, use [`svelteVerifyRoutes`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/routes#finding-links-that-are-still-strings).

## Use cases

- Forms that show the server's validation next to each field: [`Field`](#field), [`DateInput`](#dateinput-and-datetimeinput), [`EnumSelect`](#enumselect).
- Admin lists over a paged route: [`DataTable`](#datatable).
- Attachments with a progress bar: [`FileDrop`](#filedrop).
- A friendly 404 with the server's own message: [`ErrorPage`](#errorpage).
- An app frame with theme and language switches: [`ThemeToggle` and `LocaleSwitch`](#themetoggle-and-localeswitch), [`NavigationProgress`](#navigationprogress).
- Dialogs that return a value: [`modal`](#modals). Deleting things: [`confirmed`](#confirm-before-a-call).

## Good to know

**The components are a starting point**
The generated files are rewritten by every `svelteSync`, so do not edit them. For a different look, write your own component on the same helper. The generated ones are short enough to copy as a start: put the copy in your own folder, such as `src/lib/components`, and change its relative imports to the aliases, such as `#theme` or `#components/Field.svelte`.

**They need the generated client**
The components import from `#api`, so the server needs `generateTs = true`.

**Without DaisyUI**
The components use plain class names, such as `ktor-svelte-field-input`, with a minimal style of their own. Toasts and the confirm dialog work too: toasts bring their own small style, and `confirmed` uses the browser's `confirm`.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/installable-app

# Installable app

`installable { }` makes the app installable, on phones and on desktops: a web manifest, icons in every size, a theme color and a small service worker with an offline page. Name, colors and icon are set once, in Gradle.

<Badge type="info" text="Gradle" /> <Badge type="warning" text="Generated files" />

This page is part of [Frontend libraries](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries).

## Quick start

```kotlin
svelte {
    libraries {
        installable {
            name = "Notes"
            icon = file("app-icon.png")
        }
    }
}
```

```bash
./gradlew svelteSync
```

Put a square PNG of at least 512 pixels next to the build file. After the next build, browsers offer to install the app.

## Settings

```kotlin
svelte {
    libraries {
        installable {
            name = "Notes"
            shortName = "Notes"
            description = "Notes for the whole team"
            themeColor = "#4f46e5"
            backgroundColor = "#ffffff"
            display = "standalone"
            icon = file("app-icon.png")
        }
    }
}
```

| Setting | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | required | The name shown when the app is installed and in the app list |
| `shortName` | `name` | The name under the icon on a home screen, where space is short |
| `description` | none | What the app does, shown by some install dialogs |
| `themeColor` | `#ffffff` | Color of the browser bar and the title bar of the installed app, as a hex color |
| `backgroundColor` | `#ffffff` | Color of the splash screen while the app starts, and behind the maskable and Apple icons |
| `display` | `standalone` | `standalone`, `fullscreen`, `minimal-ui` or `browser` |
| `icon` | required | A square PNG of at least 512 pixels |

Colors are hex colors with three or six digits, such as `"#4f46e5"` or `"#fff"`.

### Display modes

| `display` | What the installed app looks like |
|---|---|
| `standalone` | Its own window, without the browser's address bar. The usual choice |
| `fullscreen` | The whole screen, without the system's status bar either. For games and kiosks |
| `minimal-ui` | Its own window with a few browser controls, such as back and reload |
| `browser` | A normal browser tab |

## What svelteSync writes

- `static/ktor-svelte/manifest.webmanifest`, with `start_url` and `scope` set to `/` and the default locale as `lang` when i18n is on.
- `static/ktor-svelte/icon-48.png` to `icon-512.png` in nine sizes, `icon-maskable-192.png` and `icon-maskable-512.png` with the icon inside the safe zone on the background color, and `apple-touch-icon.png`.
- `src/service-worker/index.ts` and its `tsconfig.json`, which SvelteKit builds and registers by itself.
- The manifest link, the `theme-color` tag and the Apple icon in the head of every page, through the generated server hook.

The icons are made from your PNG with plain Java, so nothing else needs to be installed. `svelteVerifySync` compares them by their pixels, so a build on another JDK, which may compress PNGs differently, does not count as a change. Commit the files like the rest of the generated ones. `static/ktor-svelte` carries its own `.gitattributes` that keeps the PNGs binary.

## What the service worker does

- It caches the hashed files of the build, everything under `_app/immutable/`, when it is installed, and serves them from that cache.
- When a page cannot be loaded because there is no connection, it answers with an [offline page](#offline-page) in the app's colors.
- It never caches API responses or HTML pages, so a deploy is never hidden behind a stale copy.
- Requests to other sites, and anything but GET, go straight to the network.

### Updates

A new build installs a new worker, which takes over once every tab of the old version is closed and then deletes the old cache. Open tabs keep the files of the version they started with. Use `toasts { reloadPrompt() }` to offer a reload:

```kotlin
svelte {
    libraries {
        toasts { reloadPrompt() }
        installable {
            name = "Notes"
            icon = file("app-icon.png")
        }
    }
}
```

See [Reload after a deploy](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#reload-after-a-deploy).

## Offline page

When a page cannot be loaded because there is no connection, the worker answers with an offline page in the app's colors, which reloads by itself once the connection is back.

The offline page is in English. To translate it, add these keys to your [messages](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/i18n#message-files), with your own wording, for example:

```json
{
  "offline-title": "You are offline",
  "offline-text": "Check your connection. This page reloads by itself once you are back online.",
  "offline-retry": "Try again"
}
```

The page uses the default locale, since a service worker cannot know the visitor's. Like every message, the keys must be in every language file.

## On the server

On the server nothing needs setting up. The files are served like the rest of the build, without a long cache time, so a new manifest or worker is picked up right away. When the app answers `svelte(public = ...)` and asks for a sign-in everywhere else, `/service-worker.js` and `/ktor-svelte/*` stay public, since a browser fetches them without a session.

## Full example

An app for a German-speaking team, based on the showcase example: installable, with a reload prompt after a deploy and a German offline page.

::: code-group

```kotlin [build.gradle.kts]
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.gradle.DaisyTheme
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.gradle.LocaleStrategy

svelte {
    libraries {
        daisyUi {
            themes(DaisyTheme.ShadcnLight, DaisyTheme.ShadcnDark)
        }
        installable {
            name = "ktor-svelte showcase"
            shortName = "Showcase"
            description = "A team board in one JAR"
            themeColor = "#7f52ff"
            backgroundColor = "#fdfcff"
            icon = file("app-icon.png")
        }
        toasts { reloadPrompt() }
        i18n {
            locales("de", "en")
            defaultLocale = "de"
            strategy = LocaleStrategy.Cookie
        }
    }
}
```

```json [messages/de.json]
{
  "offline-title": "Keine Verbindung",
  "offline-text": "Diese Seite laedt neu, sobald du wieder online bist.",
  "offline-retry": "Erneut versuchen"
}
```

```text [Generated files]
frontend/
  static/ktor-svelte/
    manifest.webmanifest
    icon-48.png ... icon-512.png
    icon-maskable-192.png
    icon-maskable-512.png
    apple-touch-icon.png
    .gitattributes
  src/service-worker/
    index.ts
    tsconfig.json
```

`en.json` needs the same three keys, in English. The offline page shows the German text, because `de` is the default locale.

To try it on a phone, open the app over [HTTPS in development](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow#https-in-development) and choose "Install" or "Add to Home Screen" in the browser's menu.

## Use cases

- An internal tool people open many times a day: an icon on the desktop or home screen, in its own window.
- A field app on phones with a patchy connection: a clear offline page instead of the browser's error.
- Faster repeat visits: the hashed files of the build come from the worker's cache.

## Good to know

**HTTPS or localhost only**
Service workers only run on `https` or on `localhost`. Test on another device with [HTTPS in development](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow#https-in-development).

**Your own service worker**
If you already have `src/service-worker/index.ts`, sync stops instead of overwriting it.

**Turning it off**
Turning `installable` off again removes the files, and browsers unregister the old worker when `/service-worker.js` no longer exists.

**What the build checks**
`svelteSync` stops with a message when `name` or `icon` is missing, when the icon file does not exist, is not a PNG Java can read, is not square or is smaller than 512 pixels, when a color is not a hex color, or when `display` is not one of the four modes. The message links to [Frontend libraries](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries).

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/auth

# Auth and users

Say once in Kotlin who is signed in, what they may do and which pages need a session. The server enforces it, and the generated client gets the same user, the same permissions and the same page rules, typed.

<Badge type="tip" text="Ktor plugin" /> <Badge type="warning" text="Generated client" />

ktor-svelte does not replace Ktor's authentication. You keep your sessions, tokens and `authenticate` blocks. What it adds is the part every app writes twice: the user in the browser, permissions on both sides, page guards, user preferences and the trip to the login page and back.

## Quick start

Tell the plugin how to find the signed-in user:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    currentUser<User> { sessions.get<UserSession>()?.let { users.find(it.userId) } }
}
```

Use it on any page:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { currentUser } from '#api';
</script>

{#if currentUser.user}
    Hello, {currentUser.user.name}
{:else if currentUser.ready}
    <a href="/login">Sign in</a>
{/if}
```

That is all it takes for a typed user in the browser and `call.user<User>()` in every route. The sections below add permissions, page guards, preferences and the login page, a few lines each.

## At a glance

| You want to | Use | Section |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Know who is signed in, in the browser | `currentUser<User> { }` and `currentUser` from `#api` | [The current user](#the-current-user) |
| Get the user in a route | `call.user<User>()`, `call.requireUser<User>()` | [In routes](#in-routes) |
| Warn before the session ends | `sessionEnds`, `extendSession`, `currentUser.sessionEnding` | [When the session ends](#when-the-session-ends) |
| Write a rule once for both sides | `permissions<Permission, User> { }`, `requires`, `can` | [Permissions](#permissions) |
| Say which pages need a session or a permission | `guards { }`, `signedInUser`, `guardPages` | [Page guards](#page-guards) |
| Keep small choices per person | `preferences<Preferences, User>(...)`, `preferences` from `#api` | [User preferences](#user-preferences) |
| Send visitors to the login page and back | `loginPage`, `respondLoginRedirect`, `afterLogin` | [The login page](#the-login-page) |
| Keep the HTML of every page behind a login | `SvelteRouting.Manual` and `svelte(public = ...)` | [Put the frontend behind a login](#put-the-frontend-behind-a-login) |

## Put the frontend behind a login

To put the frontend behind Ktor's authentication, take over its routing. List what stays public. Those paths must include your login page and `/_app/*`, or the login page cannot load. Anyone can still download the JS bundles under `/_app`, so keep secrets on the server.

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    routing = SvelteRouting.Manual
}

routing {
    svelte(public = listOf("/login", "/_app/*"))
    authenticate("session") {
        svelte()
    }
}
```

- Pages served by a plain `svelte()` get `private` caching, so shared proxies do not keep them. Paths in the `public` list keep normal caching.
- In development mode, `svelte(public = ...)` also opens the paths Vite needs, so hot reload works on your login page.
- Files that browsers and crawlers ask for without a session, such as `/favicon.ico`, `/robots.txt` and `/sitemap.xml`, go in the `public` list too if visitors should get them. The showcase example lists them.

**Not every app needs this**
Most apps only need the API to be private, which [page guards](#page-guards) do without manual routing. Use manual routing when the HTML of a page must not reach a visitor at all.

## The current user

Every app with a login needs to know who is signed in, on both sides. Say once how the server finds that person:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    currentUser<User> { sessions.get<UserSession>()?.let { users.find(it.userId) } }
}
```

The block gets the call and returns the user, or `null` when nobody is signed in. `User` is any `@Serializable` class. Whatever it holds is sent to the browser, so leave the password hash out of it. An app has one kind of signed-in user: a second `currentUser` fails at startup.

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `/api/current-user`, under your first API prefix | Where the endpoint answers. Must start with `/`, such as `path = "/api/whoami"` |
| `signInMessage` | `Sign in first.` | The message of the 401 from `call.requireUser()`. See [In routes](#in-routes) |
| `sessionEnds` | none | When the session ends. See [When the session ends](#when-the-session-ends) |
| `extendSession` | none | Makes the session last longer. See [When the session ends](#when-the-session-ends) |

### In the browser

From that one line the frontend gets `currentUser`, typed as your class:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { currentUser } from '#api';
</script>

{#if currentUser.user}
    <span>{currentUser.user.name}</span>
{:else if currentUser.ready}
    <a href="/login">Sign in</a>
{/if}
```

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `currentUser.user` | The signed-in user, or `null`. Reactive |
| `currentUser.ready` | `false` until the first answer is there, so you can tell "nobody" from "not known yet" |
| `currentUser.signedIn` | `true` when there is a user |
| `currentUser.load()` | Asks the server once and resolves to the user. Every later call resolves to what is known, without a request |
| `currentUser.reload()` | Asks again |
| `currentUser.set(user)`, `currentUser.clear()` | Set or forget the user by hand |
| `currentUser.can(permission)` | Whether the user has a [permission](#permissions). `can` from `#api` does the same |
| `currentUser.sessionEnds`, `currentUser.sessionEnding`, `currentUser.extend()` | See [When the session ends](#when-the-session-ends) |

### Protect a layout

`load()` is what a layout uses to protect its pages:

```ts
import { redirect } from '@sveltejs/kit';
import { currentUser } from '#api';

export const load = async () => {
    const user = await currentUser.load();
    if (!user) redirect(307, '/login');
    return { user };
};
```

With [page guards](#page-guards) and a [login page](#the-login-page), the generated `signedInUser(url)` does this in one line and adds the way back.

### Tell the browser when the user changes

The store has to learn when the user changes. Tell it from the routes that change it, with one line each:

```kotlin
post("/api/session") {
    val user = users.check(call.receive<Login>()) ?: return@post call.respond(HttpStatusCode.Unauthorized)
    call.sessions.set(UserSession(user.id))
    call.currentUserChanged()
    call.respond(user)
}

delete("/api/session") {
    call.sessions.clear<UserSession>()
    call.currentUserChanged()
    call.respond(HttpStatusCode.NoContent)
}
```

`currentUserChanged()` adds a header to the response. The generated client sees it and loads the user again, before your own code continues after the call, so a `goto` right after signing in lands on a page that already knows the user. Call it after a profile change too, and the name in the header of the page follows. A 401 from any API call clears the store.

### How it works

- The plugin serves `GET /api/current-user`, under your first API prefix, which answers `{"user": ...}` and is never cached. Pass `path = "/api/whoami"` to `currentUser` to move it.
- The endpoint is open to everyone and answers `{"user": null}` to a visitor.
- It runs outside any `authenticate` block, so the block that finds the user reads the session or checks the token itself, and `call.principal()` is empty there.
- With [permissions](#permissions) declared, the answer also carries the user's permissions, and with `sessionEnds` the time that is left.

### In routes

The same declaration gives every route the user, typed:

```kotlin
get("/api/tasks") {
    val user: User = call.requireUser()
    call.respond(tasks.visibleTo(user))
}

get("/api/greeting") {
    val user = call.user<User>()
    call.respond(Greeting(if (user == null) "Hello" else "Hello, ${user.name}"))
}
```

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `call.user<User>()` | The signed-in user, or `null` |
| `call.requireUser<User>()` | The signed-in user. For a visitor the route ends there with a 401 and `{"message": "Sign in first."}` |

Both work in any route, inside or outside `authenticate`, and need no user store passed along. The user is looked up once per call, however often a route and its helpers ask. `currentUserChanged()` forgets that answer, so a route that signs someone in can ask again and gets the new user. Asking for another class than the one `currentUser` declares fails with a message that names both.

The 401 message is yours to set, for example to translate it:

```kotlin
currentUser<User>(signInMessage = { call -> call.messages.signInFirst() }) {
    sessions.get<UserSession>()?.let { users.find(it.userId) }
}
```

To have the 401 in the generated types of your routes, declare it once with `errorResponse<YourError>(HttpStatusCode.Unauthorized)`.

### When the session ends

A session that ends while someone fills in a long form costs them the form. The server knows when that will be, so say it, next to how the user is found:

```kotlin
currentUser<User>(
    sessionEnds = { sessions.get<UserSession>()?.ends },
    extendSession = { sessions.get<UserSession>()?.let { sessions.set(it.copy(ends = Instant.now().plusSeconds(1800))) } },
) {
    sessions.get<UserSession>()?.let { users.find(it.userId) }
}
```

`sessionEnds` returns the `java.time.Instant` the session ends at, or `null` when it has no end. ktor-svelte does not own your session, so the end is whatever your session says: a field in the session cookie as here, a row in a table, or the expiry of a token. `extendSession` is optional and does whatever makes your session last longer.

The store then knows three more things:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `currentUser.sessionEnds` | The `Date` the session ends at, or `null` |
| `currentUser.sessionEnding` | `true` in the last two minutes. Reactive, so a warning is an `{#if}` |
| `currentUser.extend()` | Runs `extendSession` on the server and takes the new end |

```svelte
{#if currentUser.sessionEnding}
    <div class="alert alert-warning" role="status">
        You will be signed out soon.
        <button type="button" onclick={() => currentUser.extend()}>Stay signed in</button>
    </div>
{/if}
```

Set `apiConfig.sessionWarning` to another number of milliseconds to warn earlier or later:

```ts
import { apiConfig } from '#api';

apiConfig.sessionWarning = 5 * 60_000; // five minutes before the end
```

- The end stays right without extra requests. The answer of the current user endpoint carries it, and so does every API response, in a header, so a session that grows with each request is known to last longer after each one.
- The server sends the time that is left and not a clock time, so a wrong clock on the visitor's computer does not matter.
- When the time is up, the store asks the server once. If the session is really over, `currentUser.user` becomes `null` and the page shows it at that moment, not at the next click.
- `extend()` posts to the current user endpoint with `/extend` added. For a visitor it changes nothing and answers like the current user endpoint.

## Permissions

A "Delete" button that the API then refuses is a bug, and so is a hidden button for something the API would allow. Both come from writing the rule twice. Write it once, as an enum and one function from the user to what they may do:

```kotlin
enum class Permission { NotesRead, NotesDelete, UsersManage }

install(Svelte) {
    currentUser<User> { sessions.get<UserSession>()?.let { users.find(it.userId) } }
    permissions<Permission, User> { user ->
        if (user.role == Role.Admin) Permission.entries.toSet() else setOf(Permission.NotesRead)
    }
}
```

The function runs with the call as its receiver, so it can read more than the user when it has to. An app has one enum of permissions, with at least one entry.

### On the server

Check it where it matters:

```kotlin
requires(Permission.UsersManage) {
    route("/api/admin") {
        get("/users") { call.respond(users.all()) }
    }
}

delete("/api/notes/{id}") {
    call.requirePermission(Permission.NotesDelete)
    notes.delete(call.parameters["id"])
    call.respond(HttpStatusCode.NoContent)
}
```

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `requires(...) { }` | Every route inside needs the permissions |
| `call.requirePermission(...)` | The same check inside one route |
| `call.can(permission)` | `true` or `false`, for a rule with more to it, such as "admins, or the author" |

A visitor gets a 401 and a signed-in user without the permission a 403 with `{"message": "You are not allowed to do that."}`. Pass `refusedMessage = { call -> ... }` to `permissions` for your own words. The permissions of a user are worked out once per call.

A rule with more to it, "the author, or anyone who may delete every note", reads like this:

```kotlin
delete("/api/notes/{id}") {
    val user = call.requireUser<User>()
    val note = notes.find(call.parameters["id"]) ?: return@delete call.respond(HttpStatusCode.NotFound)
    if (note.authorId != user.id && !call.can(Permission.NotesDelete)) return@delete call.respond(HttpStatusCode.Forbidden)
    notes.delete(note.id)
    call.respond(HttpStatusCode.NoContent)
}
```

### In the browser

The frontend gets the same enum and a `can` function:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { can, Permission } from '#api';
</script>

{#if can(Permission.NotesDelete)}
    <button onclick={remove}>Delete</button>
{/if}
```

`can('NotesDelete')` works too, and a name that is not in the enum does not compile. The answer is reactive and comes with the current user, so it changes when someone signs in or out, with no request of its own. Rename a permission in Kotlin and every `can` that used the old name fails `svelteCheck`.

**The browser only decides what is shown**
`can` in the browser decides what is shown. What is allowed is decided by the check on the route, so every hidden button needs one.

## Owner checks

Permissions say what someone may do in general; an owner check says whether one record is theirs. `requireOwner` takes the record you looked up and a rule, and answers for you when it is not theirs:

```kotlin
get("/api/drafts/{id}") {
    val draft = call.requireOwner(drafts.find(call.pathParameter<Int>("id"))) { user: User, draft ->
        draft.ownerId == user.id
    }
    call.respond(draft)
}.ownerChecked()
```

| The call | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| No record (`null`) | `404` `{"message": "This does not exist."}` |
| Nobody signed in | `401`, the same as everywhere else, including your `signInMessage` |
| Somebody else's record | `404`, so a stranger cannot tell that it exists |
| Somebody else's record, with `OtherOwner.Forbidden` | `403` with your `refusedMessage` |
| The owner | the record, and your route goes on |

- The user type is the one you gave `currentUser<User> { }`; write it on the rule's first parameter, as above, and Kotlin works out the rest.
- Pass `OtherOwner.Forbidden` as the second argument when a 403 is more helpful than hiding the record, for example inside a team where everybody sees the list anyway.
- `.ownerChecked()` describes the 401, 403 and 404 answers for the generated client, so `isApiError(error, 'drafts.get')` knows them. The compiler plugin cannot see answers that the plugin sends for you.
- Use it together with [permissions](#permissions): a permission for what a role may do at all, an owner check for the one record.

## Page guards

Which pages need a signed-in user, and which a permission, is one more rule that both sides have to agree on. Declare it once, by page:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    guards {
        signedIn(FrontendRoutes.board, FrontendRoutes.settings, "/tasks")
        permission(Permission.UsersManage, FrontendRoutes.admin)
    }
}
```

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `signedIn(pages...)` | The pages need a signed-in user |
| `permission(permission, pages...)` | The pages need a user with that permission |

- A guard covers the page and everything below it: `/tasks` also covers `/tasks/4`. When two guards cover a page, the deeper one decides.
- A guard takes the path of a page, such as `"/admin"` or `FrontendRoutes.admin`. A path with `[`, `]`, `?`, `#` or `*` is refused at startup, and so is a page that is guarded twice.

### The API is closed by the server

With the guards above, every route under `/api/tasks` answers a visitor with a 401, and every route under `/api/admin` answers a user without `UsersManage` with a 403. This is the part that protects your data, and it needs no `authenticate` or `requires` around those routes. A route with another name, such as `/api/stats` for the board page, is not covered and keeps its own check.

### The pages are guarded in the browser

One generated function does it. Use it in the layout of the route group that holds the pages:

```ts
// src/routes/(app)/+layout.ts
import { signedInUser } from '#api';

export const ssr = false;

export const load = async ({ url }) => ({ user: await signedInUser(url) });
```

`signedInUser(url)` resolves to the user, typed and never `null`. A visitor is sent to [the login page](#the-login-page) with the way back, and a user without the permission that the page's guard asks for gets your error page with a 403. Without a `loginPage`, a visitor gets your error page with a 401 instead.

`guardPages` does the same for a layout that has no use for the user:

```ts
import { guardPages } from '#api';

export const load = guardPages;
```

It only acts on pages that a guard covers, and only in the browser.

**Not in the root layout**
Do not put either in the root `+layout.ts`. SvelteKit cannot show your error page for an error from the root layout, and the visitor would see a bare "Forbidden".

The guard in the browser is a convenience: it spares the visitor a page that would only fail. Anyone can skip it, so what must stay private is kept private by the API.

### Show only the links a user may open

The guards are in the client too, as `pageGuards`, and `matchGuard` finds the one that covers a path. A menu filters with them, so it never offers a page that would refuse:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { can, currentUser, matchGuard, pageGuards } from '#api';
    import { nav } from '#routes';

    const links = $derived(
        nav.filter((item) => {
            const guard = matchGuard(pageGuards, item.to());
            if (!guard) return true;
            return currentUser.signedIn && (!guard.permission || can(guard.permission));
        })
    );
</script>

{#each links as link (link.to.id)}
    <a href={link.to()}>{link.title()}</a>
{/each}
```

`nav` comes from [typed routes](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/routes).

## User preferences

A theme, a language, a compact list: small choices that people expect to find again on their phone after making them on their laptop. Declare them as a class, and say how you keep them:

```kotlin
@Serializable
data class Preferences(
    val theme: String? = null,
    val locale: String? = null,
    val compactBoard: Boolean = false,
)

install(Svelte) {
    currentUser<User> { sessions.get<UserSession>()?.let { users.find(it.userId) } }
    preferences<Preferences, User>(
        defaults = Preferences(),
        load = { user -> store.preferences(user.id) },
        save = { user, preferences -> store.save(user.id, preferences) },
    )
}
```

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `defaults` | What a visitor, and someone who has saved nothing yet, gets |
| `load` | Reads the saved preferences of a user. Returns `null` for someone who has saved nothing yet, who then gets the defaults |
| `save` | Stores them |
| `path` | Moves the endpoint, such as `path = "/api/settings"`. Must start with `/` |

You store them: a table, a JSON column, a document. ktor-svelte adds the endpoint, the type and the store:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { preferences } from '#api';
</script>

<input
    type="checkbox"
    checked={preferences.value.compactBoard}
    onchange={(event) => preferences.set({ compactBoard: event.currentTarget.checked })}
/>
<ul class:compact={preferences.value.compactBoard}>...</ul>
```

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `preferences.value` | The preferences, typed as your class and reactive. The defaults until the server has answered, and for a visitor |
| `preferences.ready` | `false` until the first answer |
| `preferences.set({ ... })` | Changes some of them. The page shows the change at once, and it is saved in the background |
| `preferences.load()` | Resolves when they are loaded. Reading `value` starts loading on its own |

- The store loads once, loads again when someone signs in, and goes back to the defaults when they sign out.
- A visitor's changes stay in the page and are not saved.
- What is saved is checked like every request body, so `@JsonSchema` bounds on the class apply.
- The endpoint is `GET` and `PUT /api/preferences`, under your first API prefix. Pass `path = "/api/settings"` to move it.
- Keep preferences to plain values: text, numbers, booleans, enums and lists of them.

### Theme and language

A field called `theme` or `locale` is tied to the cookie that [DaisyUI themes](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries#daisyui) and [i18n](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries#i18n) use, so the generated switches keep working unchanged and their choice now belongs to the person:

- Someone picks a theme or a language, with the generated switch or your own code. It is saved for them.
- They sign in on another device. The saved theme is applied at once, and for a saved language the page loads again in that language.
- They pick another theme on that device. That one is saved, and the first device shows it the next time a page loads there.

The rule behind it: each browser remembers the value it last had in common with the server. If its cookie differs from that, the change was made here and is saved. If not, the saved value is newer and is shown.

## The login page

Someone opens a link to a page that needs a session, or their session ends while they fill in a form. Both should end the same way: at the login page, and after signing in, back where they were. Say where the login page is:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    loginPage = "/login"
}
```

With [typed routes](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/routes) that is `loginPage = FrontendRoutes.login`. Three things follow from it.

### A 401 from the API opens the login page

The generated client sends the browser to `/login?next=...`, with the page the visitor was on. There is no `apiConfig.onUnauthorized` to write.

- It does not happen on the login page itself, where a 401 means a wrong password.
- It does not happen for calls made with `silent: true`.
- If you do set `apiConfig.onUnauthorized`, yours runs instead.

### The server's redirect carries the page too

Use it where Ktor's authentication turns a visitor away:

```kotlin
install(Authentication) {
    session<UserSession>("session") {
        validate { session -> users.find(session.userId)?.let { session } }
        challenge {
            if (call.request.path().startsWith("/api/")) call.respond(HttpStatusCode.Unauthorized) else call.respondLoginRedirect()
        }
    }
}
```

`respondLoginRedirect()` answers with a redirect to `/login?next=%2Fboard` for a visitor who asked for `/board`. Only a `GET` carries its page along. Other methods, and a request for the login page itself, are sent to the plain login page. Without `loginPage` set, it fails with a message that says how to set it.

### After signing in, go back

`afterLogin` reads the page from the address, and takes your fallback when there is none:

```ts
import { goto } from '$app/navigation';
import { afterLogin, api } from '#api';

await api.session.create(draft);
await goto(afterLogin('/board'));
```

A layout that protects its pages in the browser builds the same address with `loginPath`:

```ts
import { redirect } from '@sveltejs/kit';
import { currentUser, loginPath } from '#api';

export const load = async ({ url }) => {
    const user = await currentUser.load();
    if (!user) redirect(307, loginPath(url));
    return { user };
};
```

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `loginPath(from?)` | The login page with `?next=` for `from`, a path or a `URL`. Without an argument, the page that is open. On the login page itself, the plain login page |
| `afterLogin(fallback = '/', from?)` | The page in `next`, or `fallback` when there is none |

Only a path inside your app is accepted as the page to go back to. An address of another site in `next` is ignored on both sides, so a crafted link to your login page cannot send someone elsewhere after they sign in.

## Full example

A team app where members sign in with a session cookie, admins manage users, a guard closes the members' pages, and a warning appears before the session ends. It is a shortened version of `examples/showcase`.

::: code-group

```kotlin no-check [Auth.kt]
@Serializable
data class UserSession(val userId: Int, val endsAt: Long = 0) {
    val ends: Instant get() = Instant.ofEpochSecond(endsAt)
    val current: Boolean get() = Instant.now().isBefore(ends)
}

fun Application.configureAuth(users: UserStore) {
    install(Sessions) {
        cookie<UserSession>("session") {
            cookie.path = "/"
            cookie.httpOnly = true
            cookie.secure = !developmentMode
            cookie.extensions["SameSite"] = "Lax"
            transform(SessionTransportTransformerMessageAuthentication(hex(System.getenv("SESSION_SIGN_KEY"))))
        }
    }
    install(Authentication) {
        session<UserSession>("session") {
            validate { session -> session.takeIf { it.current && users.findActive(it.userId) != null } }
            challenge {
                if (call.request.path().startsWith("/api/")) {
                    call.respond(HttpStatusCode.Unauthorized, Problem("Sign in first."))
                } else {
                    call.respondLoginRedirect()
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

fun Route.sessionRoutes(users: UserStore) {
    rateLimit(RateLimitName("login")) {
        post("/api/session") {
            val login = call.receive<Login>()
            val user = users.check(login.email, login.password)
                ?: return@post call.respond(HttpStatusCode.Unauthorized, Problem("Wrong email or password."))
            call.sessions.set(UserSession(user.id, Instant.now().epochSecond + 3600))
            call.currentUserChanged()
            call.respond(user)
        }
    }
    delete("/api/session") {
        call.sessions.clear<UserSession>()
        call.currentUserChanged()
        call.respond(HttpStatusCode.NoContent)
    }
}
```

```kotlin no-check [Application.kt]
enum class Role { ADMIN, MEMBER }

enum class Permission { ManageUsers, DeleteAnyTask }

fun Application.module() {
    val users = UserStore()
    configureAuth(users)

    install(Svelte) {
        loginPage = FrontendRoutes.login
        currentUser<User>(
            sessionEnds = { sessions.get<UserSession>()?.ends },
            extendSession = {
                sessions.get<UserSession>()?.let { sessions.set(it.copy(endsAt = Instant.now().epochSecond + 3600)) }
            },
        ) {
            sessions.get<UserSession>()?.takeIf { it.current }?.let { users.findActive(it.userId) }
        }
        permissions<Permission, User> { user ->
            if (user.role == Role.ADMIN) Permission.entries.toSet() else emptySet()
        }
        preferences<Preferences, User>(
            defaults = Preferences(),
            load = { user -> users.preferences(user.id) },
            save = { user, preferences -> users.savePreferences(user.id, preferences) },
        )
        guards {
            signedIn(FrontendRoutes.board, "/tasks", FrontendRoutes.settings)
            permission(Permission.ManageUsers, FrontendRoutes.admin)
        }
        errorResponse<Problem>(HttpStatusCode.Unauthorized, HttpStatusCode.Forbidden)
        rateLimit { limit("login", requests = 10, per = 1.minutes) }
    }

    routing {
        sessionRoutes(users)
        get("/api/admin/users") { call.respond(users.all()) } // closed by the admin guard
        get("/api/tasks") { call.respond(tasks.visibleTo(call.requireUser<User>())) } // closed by the /tasks guard
    }
}
```

```ts no-check [(app)/+layout.ts]
import { signedInUser } from '#api';
import type { LayoutLoad } from './$types';

export const prerender = false;
export const ssr = false;

export const load: LayoutLoad = async ({ url }) => ({ user: await signedInUser(url) });
```

```svelte no-check [login/+page.svelte]
<script lang="ts">
    import { goto } from '$app/navigation';
    import { afterLogin, api, isApiError, Login } from '#api';
    import { routes } from '#routes';

    let draft = $state(Login.empty());
    let message = $state('');

    async function signIn(event: SubmitEvent) {
        event.preventDefault();
        message = '';
        try {
            await api.session.create(draft);
            await goto(afterLogin(routes.board()));
        } catch (error) {
            if (isApiError(error, 'session.create')) message = error.body.message;
            else throw error;
        }
    }
</script>

<form onsubmit={signIn}>
    <input type="email" autocomplete="username" required bind:value={draft.email} />
    <input type="password" autocomplete="current-password" required bind:value={draft.password} />
    <p role="alert">{message}</p>
    <button type="submit">Sign in</button>
</form>
```

```svelte no-check [+layout.svelte]
<script lang="ts">
    import { onMount } from 'svelte';
    import { goto } from '$app/navigation';
    import { api, can, currentUser, Permission } from '#api';
    import { routes } from '#routes';

    let { children } = $props();

    onMount(() => void currentUser.load());

    async function signOut() {
        await api.session.delete();
        await goto(routes.login());
    }
</script>

<header>
    {#if can(Permission.ManageUsers)}
        <a href={routes.admin()}>Admin</a>
    {/if}
    {#if currentUser.user}
        <span>{currentUser.user.name}</span>
        <button type="button" onclick={signOut}>Sign out</button>
    {:else if currentUser.ready}
        <a href={routes.login()}>Sign in</a>
    {/if}
</header>

{#if currentUser.sessionEnding}
    <div role="status">
        You will be signed out soon.
        <button type="button" onclick={() => currentUser.extend()}>Stay signed in</button>
    </div>
{/if}

{@render children()}
```

## Use cases

- **An app behind a login:** `currentUser`, `loginPage` and one `signedIn` guard for the route group. Step by step in [Sign in with a session cookie](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/sessions).
- **Members and admins:** add `permissions` and a `permission` guard. See [A role-based app](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/role-based-app) and [Add an admin area](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/admin-area).
- **Long forms:** `sessionEnds` and `extendSession`, so nobody loses their work to an expired session.
- **Settings that follow the person:** `preferences` with `theme` and `locale` fields, so the [theme and language switches](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries#themetoggle-and-localeswitch) remember per account.
- **A public site with a members area:** guards for the members' pages only, and the rest stays open.

## Good to know

- `currentUser`, `permissions` and `preferences` can each be declared once. A second one fails at startup and names the first.
- Permissions, guards, preferences and `call.user` all need `currentUser`. Without it, the first call that needs the user fails with a message that says how to declare it.
- The current user and preferences endpoints are under your first API prefix, so the [API request guards](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/security#api-request-guards) apply to them, such as the origin check on writes.
- `call.principal()` is only set inside `authenticate`. The `currentUser` block also runs for the current user endpoint and for guards, outside `authenticate`, so it reads the session itself.
- A 401 from any API call clears the store and, with a `loginPage`, opens the login page.

**Which part protects what**
| Part | Protects | A visitor can skip it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A guard on the API (`guards { }`) | The routes under the guarded path | No |
| `requires`, `requirePermission`, `requireUser` | The routes they are in | No |
| `authenticate` around `svelte()` | The HTML of the pages | No |
| `signedInUser`, `guardPages` | Which page the browser shows | Yes |
| `can` in the browser | Which buttons are shown | Yes |

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/security

# Security

The protections that are on by default, and how to change them. A new app gets safe headers, a strict Content Security Policy, a guard against cross-site writes, size and shape limits on request bodies and a rate limit on writes, without a line of configuration.

<Badge type="tip" text="Ktor plugin" /> <Badge type="info" text="Gradle" />

## Quick start

There is nothing to turn on. Install the plugin and every protection on this page is active:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    generateTs = true
}
```

Change only what your app needs, such as a tighter limit for the login route or a script from another origin:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    rateLimit { limit("login", requests = 5, per = 1.minutes) }
    securityHeaders { allowCspSources("script-src", "https://plausible.io") }
}
```

## At a glance

| Protection | Default | Setting | Section |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options`, `Referrer-Policy` | On | `securityHeaders { }` | [Security headers](#security-headers) |
| Content Security Policy for HTML pages | On, with hashes of the inline scripts | `securityHeaders { }` | [Content Security Policy](#content-security-policy) |
| Cross-site writes to the API | Refused with 403 | `originCheck`, `allowedOrigins(...)` | [API request guards](#api-request-guards) |
| Size of API request bodies | 1 MiB | `maxApiBodySize` | [Body size limit](#body-size-limit) |
| Nesting of JSON bodies | 64 levels | `maxJsonDepth`, `maxJsonStringLength` | [JSON shape](#json-shape) |
| Exception messages in production | Hidden | `hideErrorDetails` | [Error details](#error-details) |
| Writes per client | 120 per minute | `rateLimit { }` | [Rate limits](#rate-limits) |
| Broken paths and `Host` headers | 400 | none | [Malformed requests](#malformed-requests) |
| Status endpoint and API docs | This machine, or development only | `internalAccess { }` | [Internal endpoints](#internal-endpoints) |

## Security headers

Security headers are on by default. Every response gets `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`. Each is a property you can change, or set to `null` to leave out:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    securityHeaders {
        referrerPolicy = "no-referrer"
    }
}
```

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `contentTypeOptions` | `"nosniff"` | The `X-Content-Type-Options` header |
| `frameOptions` | `"DENY"` | The `X-Frame-Options` header. Also sets the CSP's `frame-ancestors` |
| `referrerPolicy` | `"strict-origin-when-cross-origin"` | The `Referrer-Policy` header |
| `automaticContentSecurityPolicy` | `true` | The [automatic CSP](#content-security-policy) on HTML pages |
| `contentSecurityPolicy` | `null` | [Your own policy](#your-own-policy), sent unchanged on every response |
| `allowCspSources(directive, sources...)` | none | [Adds sources](#allow-other-origins) to the automatic policy |
| `enabled` | `true` | `false` turns off all security headers |

To let your pages be framed by your own site, for example:

```kotlin
securityHeaders {
    frameOptions = "SAMEORIGIN"
}
```

## Content Security Policy

Every HTML page from your build also gets a strict `Content-Security-Policy`:

```text
default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'sha256-...'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline';
img-src 'self' data: blob:; font-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none';
base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'
```

`script-src` lists the SHA-256 hash of each inline `<script>` in that page, which covers SvelteKit's startup script and the theme and locale script ktor-svelte adds, and nothing else. `svelteBundle` computes these hashes at build time and stores them in the manifest, so the server never reads a page to build its policy. For builds without them, such as a directory build in development, the server hashes each page once and caches the result. Other inline scripts and scripts from other origins are blocked.

The other directives exist for these reasons:

- `style-src 'unsafe-inline'`: Svelte transitions and many components set inline styles, and SvelteKit can inline small CSS files.
