- The permissions of a user are worked out once per call, and they travel with the current user to the browser, so `can` costs no request.
- A role change takes effect on the next request: `currentUser` and `permissions` run per call. Call `currentUserChanged()` when users change their own account, so their page follows at once.
- For a "deactivate" switch, have the `currentUser` block return `null` for inactive accounts, as `findActive` does. Their next request is a visitor's.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/admin-area

# Add an admin area

You want pages under `/admin` that only admins can open, backed by API routes under `/api/admin` that only admins can call, and an "Admin" link that only admins see.

**Time:** about 20 minutes. **Level:** intermediate. **You need:** a sign-in, as in [Sign in with a session cookie](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/sessions).

The rule to remember: protect the API on the server, and only hide the pages in the frontend. A page guard alone protects nothing, because anyone can call the API directly. With ktor-svelte's [page guards](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/auth#page-guards), one declaration does both.

## Step 1: say who is an admin

Declare a permission, and the function from a user to their permissions:

```kotlin no-check [Application.kt]
enum class Permission { ManageUsers }

install(Svelte) {
    loginPage = "/login"
    currentUser<User> { sessions.get<UserSession>()?.let { users.find(it.userId) } }
    permissions<Permission, User> { user -> if (user.admin) setOf(Permission.ManageUsers) else emptySet() }
}
```

## Step 2: guard the admin pages and their API

```kotlin no-check [Application.kt]
install(Svelte) {
    guards {
        permission(Permission.ManageUsers, "/admin")
    }
    errorResponse<Problem>(HttpStatusCode.Unauthorized, HttpStatusCode.Forbidden)
}
```

From now on every route under `/api/admin` answers a visitor with 401 and a signed-in user without `ManageUsers` with 403, before your route runs. `errorResponse` puts both in the generated error types.

## Step 3: the admin routes

They need no check of their own, because the guard covers them:

```kotlin no-check [AdminRoutes.kt]
fun Route.adminRoutes() {
    route("/api/admin") {
        get("/users") { call.respond(users.all()) }

        put("/users/{id}/active") {
            val change = call.receive<ActiveChange>()
            val user = users.setActive(call.parameters["id"].orEmpty(), change.active)
                ?: return@put call.respond(HttpStatusCode.NotFound, Problem("No such user."))
            call.respond(user)
        }
    }
}
```

A route outside `/api/admin` that only admins may call, such as deleting any comment, checks for itself with `call.requirePermission(Permission.ManageUsers)` or `requires(Permission.ManageUsers) { }`.

## Step 4: the admin pages

Put them in the route group that the signed-in pages share, so its layout guards them:

::: code-group

```ts no-check [(app)/+layout.ts]
import { signedInUser } from '#api';

export const ssr = false;

export const load = async ({ url }) => ({ user: await signedInUser(url) });
```

```ts no-check [(app)/admin/+page.ts]
import { error } from '@sveltejs/kit';
import { apiWith, isApiError } from '#api';
import type { PageLoad } from './$types';

export const load: PageLoad = async (event) => {
    try {
        return { users: await apiWith(event).admin.getUsers({ silent: true }) };
    } catch (cause) {
        if (isApiError(cause, 'admin.getUsers') && cause.status === 403) error(403, cause.body.message);
        throw cause;
    }
};
```

```svelte no-check [(app)/admin/+page.svelte]
<script lang="ts">
    import { api, type User } from '#api';
    import type { PageProps } from './$types';

    let { data }: PageProps = $props();
    let users = $derived<User[]>(data.users);

    async function setActive(user: User, toggle: HTMLInputElement) {
        try {
            const changed = await api.admin.putUsersActive(user.id, { active: toggle.checked });
            users = users.map((item) => (item.id === changed.id ? changed : item));
        } catch {
            toggle.checked = user.active;
        }
    }
</script>

<h1>Users</h1>
<table>
    {#each users as user (user.id)}
        <tr>
            <th scope="row">{user.name}</th>
            <td>
                <input type="checkbox" checked={user.active} onchange={(event) => setActive(user, event.currentTarget)} />
            </td>
        </tr>
    {/each}
</table>
```

- A visitor who opens `/admin` is sent to the login page and comes back after signing in.
- A member who opens `/admin` gets your error page with a 403. `signedInUser` already checks the guard's permission, and the `+page.ts` turns a 403 from the API into the same page.
- The load uses `apiWith(event)` so SvelteKit's `fetch` is used, and `silent: true` so the error page is shown instead of a toast.

## Step 5: show the link to admins only

```svelte no-check [+layout.svelte]
<script lang="ts">
    import { can, Permission } from '#api';
</script>

{#if can(Permission.ManageUsers)}
    <a href="/admin">Admin</a>
{/if}
```

`can` follows the current user, so the link appears when an admin signs in and goes when they sign out. To filter a whole menu by the guards, see [Show only the links a user may open](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/auth#show-only-the-links-a-user-may-open).

## Without the permissions helper

If you would rather not declare permissions, the same protection can be written as a route-scoped plugin. The API is still protected on the server, and the pages are still only hidden:

```kotlin
fun Route.admin(
    users: Users,
    build: Route.() -> Unit,
) {
    authenticate("session") {
        route("/api/admin") {
            install(
                createRouteScopedPlugin("AdminOnly") {
                    on(AuthenticationChecked) { call ->
                        val user = call.principal<UserSession>()?.let { users.find(it.userId) }
                        if (user?.admin != true) call.respond(HttpStatusCode.Forbidden, Problem("Admins only."))
                    }
                },
            )
            build()
        }
    }
}

routing {
    admin(users) {
        get("/users") { call.respond(users.all()) }
    }
}
```

The check has to run in `on(AuthenticationChecked)`. A plain `onCall` runs before Ktor has read the session, so `call.principal` is still empty there and the check would refuse everyone, admins included.

In SvelteKit, put the admin pages under `src/routes/admin/` and check the user once in their layout:

```ts
import { redirect } from '@sveltejs/kit';
import { apiWith } from '#api';
import type { LayoutLoad } from './$types';

export const ssr = false;

export const load: LayoutLoad = async (event) => {
    const me = await apiWith(event).me.list().catch(() => undefined);
    if (!me?.admin) redirect(307, '/login');
    return { me };
};
```

Pages inside it call `api.admin.getUsers()` and the other admin endpoints. Every one of them answers 403 for anyone who is not an admin, whatever the frontend shows.

## Good to know

- Keep at least one admin. The showcase refuses to demote or deactivate the last active admin, with a typed error code, so nobody locks everyone out.
- An admin page that edits users should call `call.currentUserChanged()` when an admin changes their own account, so their header follows.
- For several roles with different rights, see [A role-based app](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/role-based-app).
- To open the API docs or the status endpoint to admins, use `allow { call -> call.can(Permission.ManageUsers) }` in [`internalAccess`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/endpoints#who-may-see-internal-endpoints).

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/uploads

# Upload files

You want people to upload files, such as avatars or documents, see a progress bar while they upload, and be told at once when a file is too large or of the wrong type, by the browser and by the server alike.

**Time:** about 15 minutes. **Level:** beginner.

What you build, one step at a time:

1. A route that takes files, and a typed function that sends them with progress.
2. Rules for size, type and count, written once and checked on both sides.
3. A drop zone with previews, without writing one.
4. A form with named fields, such as a title and a cover image.

## Step 1: receive the files

Receive the parts in Ktor and describe the body once, so the generated function takes `FormData`:

```kotlin
post("/api/files") {
    val stored = mutableListOf<StoredFile>()
    call.receiveMultipart().forEachPart { part ->
        if (part is PartData.FileItem) {
            stored += files.store(part.originalFileName ?: "upload", part.provider().readRemaining().readByteArray())
        }
        part.dispose()
    }
    call.respond(HttpStatusCode.Created, stored)
}.describe {
    requestBody { ContentType.MultiPart.FormData() }
}
```

## Step 2: send them with progress

The generated function takes the `FormData` and an `onUploadProgress` option:

```ts
const form = new FormData();
for (const file of input.files ?? []) form.append('file', file);
const stored = await api.files.create(form, {
    onUploadProgress: ({ loaded, total }) => (progress = total ? loaded / total : 0)
});
```

`total` is missing when the browser does not know the size in advance, so check it before you divide.

## Step 3: raise the body limit

API bodies are limited to 1 MiB by default. Raise `maxApiBodySize` to the largest upload you accept, with a little room for the multipart framing:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    maxApiBodySize = 5L * 1024 * 1024 + 64 * 1024
}
```

See [Body size limit](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/security#body-size-limit).

## Rules for both sides

Which files a route takes is usually written twice: once in Kotlin, and again in the page, so the user is told before a 20 MB upload has finished. Declare it once, on the route:

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.receiveUploads
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.uploadRules

post("/api/avatars") {
    val stored = call.receiveUploads().map { file -> files.store(file.fileName ?: "upload", file.bytes) }
    call.respond(HttpStatusCode.Created, stored)
}.uploadRules(maxSize = 5L * 1024 * 1024, types = listOf("image/*", ".pdf"), maxFiles = 3)
```

| Rule | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `maxSize` | none | Largest size of each file, in bytes |
| `types` | any | Media types (`application/pdf`), families (`image/*`) or file endings (`.csv`) |
| `maxFiles` | none | Most files in one request |

- `uploadRules` describes the body as multipart form data, so no `describe { requestBody { } }` is needed, and it carries the rules into the generated client.
- `call.receiveUploads()` reads the files and enforces the rules. Each file has `field`, `fileName`, `contentType`, `bytes` and `size`. No file is read beyond its limit.
- A rule that is not a media type, a family or a file ending, or a size or count that is not positive, fails at startup.

A file that breaks a rule is answered with a status and a body like this one, and the route's own code never runs:

| Rule | Status | `code` | `message` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `maxSize` | 413 | `upload.tooLarge` | `photo.png is larger than 5 MiB.` |
| `types` | 415 | `upload.type` | `setup.exe is not an accepted file type.` |
| `maxFiles` | 400 | `upload.tooMany` | `At most 3 files can be sent at once.` |

### In the page

The generated function checks the same rules before it sends anything, and fails with the same `ApiError`, so the page handles one error whether the browser or the server noticed:

```ts
import { api, isUploadError, uploadRules } from '#api';

try {
    await api.avatars.create(form);
} catch (error) {
    if (isUploadError(error)) console.log(error.body.code, error.body.file, error.body.message);
}
```

- `uploadRules['avatars.create']` holds the rules as data, for an `<input type="file" accept={uploadRules['avatars.create'].types.join(',')}>` or a hint under the field.
- With `toasts()` on, the message is shown without any code of yours.
- For your own wording or another language, pass `{ silent: true }` and choose the text by `error.body.code`.

**Treat stored files as untrusted**
The server checks the type the browser declares and the file name, as the browser does. Neither proves what the bytes are, so treat stored files as untrusted when you serve them.

## A drop zone without the code

With `libraries { components() }`, the generated [`<FileDrop>`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries#filedrop) is the input, the drop area, the previews, the progress bars and the refusals for an upload route, in one component:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { api, uploadRules, type StoredFile } from '#api';
    import FileDrop from '#components/FileDrop.svelte';

    let avatars = $state<StoredFile[]>([]);
</script>

<FileDrop
    label="Add a picture"
    hint="Images or PDF, up to 5 MiB each."
    multiple
    rules={uploadRules['avatars.create']}
    upload={(file, options) => {
        const form = new FormData();
        form.append('file', file);
        return api.avatars.create(form, options);
    }}
    onuploaded={(stored) => (avatars = [...avatars, ...stored])}
/>
```

Hand the `options` it gives you to the generated function: they carry the progress.

## A form with named fields

With `uploadRules`, the generated function takes a `FormData`, and nothing checks the field names in it. When an upload comes with other values, or the field names matter, declare the form:

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.receiveForm
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.uploadForm

post("/api/documents") {
    val form = call.receiveForm()
    val title = form.text("title")
    val cover = form.file("cover")
    val pages = form.files("pages")
    call.respondText("$title: ${cover.fileName} and ${pages.size} pages")
}.uploadForm(maxSize = 5L * 1024 * 1024, types = listOf("image/*", ".pdf")) {
    text("title")
    text("note", required = false)
    file("cover")
    files("pages")
}
```

The generated function then takes an object with those fields, and builds the form itself:

```ts
await api.documents.create({ title: 'Report', cover, pages: [first, second] });
```

```ts
export const documentsCreate = (body: { title: string; note?: string; cover: File; pages?: File[] }, options?: RequestOptions) => ...
```

| Field | Required unless you say | In Kotlin |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text(name)` | Yes | `form.text(name)`, or `form.textOrNull(name)` when optional |
| `file(name)` | Yes | `form.file(name)`, or `form.fileOrNull(name)` when optional |
| `files(name)` | No | `form.files(name)`, a list |

- `maxSize`, `types` and `maxFiles` are the rules from above, for every file in the form. Both sides check them as before.
- `form.allFiles` lists every file in the form.
- Field names are letters, digits, `_` and `-`, each declared once.
- A request with a field the form does not have, without a required one, with a file where text belongs, or with two files for a `file` field, is answered with 400 and a `code` of `upload.field` or `upload.missing`.

On a route without `uploadForm`, `receiveForm()` takes any field, for forms whose fields are not known in advance.

## Full example

An avatar upload on a profile page, with a preview, a progress bar and the rules from the route:

::: code-group

```kotlin no-check [Routes.kt]
const val MAX_AVATAR_BYTES = 2L * 1024 * 1024

fun Route.avatarRoutes(storage: AvatarStorage) {
    // one picture per user, replaced on each upload
    post("/api/avatars") {
        val user = call.requireUser<User>()
        val file = call.receiveUploads().single()
        val url = storage.save(user.id, file.contentType, file.bytes) // stored under the user's id, not the file name
        call.respond(Avatar(url))
    }.uploadRules(maxSize = MAX_AVATAR_BYTES, types = listOf("image/png", "image/jpeg", "image/webp"), maxFiles = 1)
}
```

```svelte no-check [settings/+page.svelte]
<script lang="ts">
    import { api, isUploadError, uploadRules } from '#api';

    const rules = uploadRules['avatars.create'];

    let progress = $state(0);
    let busy = $state(false);
    let message = $state('');
    let avatar = $state<string | null>(null);

    async function upload(event: Event) {
        const file = (event.currentTarget as HTMLInputElement).files?.[0];
        if (!file) return;
        const form = new FormData();
        form.append('file', file);
        busy = true;
        message = '';
        try {
            avatar = (await api.avatars.create(form, {
                silent: true,
                onUploadProgress: ({ loaded, total }) => (progress = total ? loaded / total : 0)
            })).url;
        } catch (error) {
            if (isUploadError(error)) message = error.body.message;
            else throw error;
        } finally {
            busy = false;
        }
    }
</script>

{#if avatar}<img src={avatar} alt="Your avatar" width="96" height="96" />{/if}
<input type="file" accept={rules.types.join(',')} onchange={upload} disabled={busy} />
{#if busy}<progress value={progress}></progress>{/if}
<p role="alert">{message}</p>
```

## Good to know

- `readRemaining()` and `receiveUploads()` keep each file in memory. For large files, copy `part.provider()` to a file or object storage instead.
- Never use `originalFileName` as a path on disk. Store files under an ID you choose.
- An upload is a write, so the [origin check and the write rate limit](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/security#api-request-guards) apply to it.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/search-as-you-type

# Search as you type

You want a search box that updates the results while someone types, without flooding the server, and without an older, slower answer overwriting a newer one.

**Time:** about 10 minutes. **Level:** beginner.

What you use:

- A [query class](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#query-parameters-as-a-class) on the list route, so the search term is a typed field in the client.
- [`latest`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#search-as-you-type) from the generated client, which aborts the call before when a new one starts.
- A short pause before each call, so a fast typist sends one request, not ten.

## Step 1: a list route that takes a search term

Describe the query as a class. With [`resource`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/typescript#resource-routes), the `list` block takes it:

::: code-group

```kotlin no-check [With resource]
@Serializable
data class NoteQuery(
    val search: String? = null,
    val tag: String? = null,
)

resource<Note, Int>("/api/notes") {
    list<NoteQuery> { query -> store.list(query.search, query.tag) }
}
```

```kotlin no-check [With a plain route]
get("/api/notes") {
    val query = call.query<NoteQuery>()
    call.respond(store.list(query.search, query.tag))
}.queryOf<NoteQuery>()
```

An empty parameter counts as not given, as a form sends it for an empty field, so `?search=` reads as `null`. Run `./gradlew svelteGenerateTs`, and `api.notes.list` takes `{ search?: string; tag?: string }`.

Search in the database, not in memory, once the list is long: a `LIKE` or a full text index, and a limit on the number of results.

## Step 2: the search box

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { api, isAbortError, latest, type Note } from '#api';

    const search = latest(api.notes.list);

    let term = $state('');
    let results = $state<Note[]>([]);
    let searching = $state(false);
    let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;

    function onInput() {
        clearTimeout(timer);
        timer = setTimeout(run, 250);
    }

    async function run() {
        searching = true;
        try {
            results = await search({ search: term.trim() || undefined });
            searching = false;
        } catch (error) {
            if (isAbortError(error)) return;
            searching = false;
            throw error;
        }
    }
</script>

<input type="search" bind:value={term} oninput={onInput} placeholder="Search notes" aria-label="Search notes" />
{#if searching}<p>Searching...</p>{/if}
<ul>
    {#each results as note (note.id)}
        <li>{note.title}</li>
    {/each}
</ul>
```

Three things keep it fast and correct:

| Line | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `setTimeout(run, 250)` | Waits until typing pauses for a quarter of a second, so one request goes out per pause, not one per key |
| `latest(api.notes.list)` | Each call aborts the one before it, so a slow answer for "no" never replaces the answer for "notes" |
| `isAbortError(error)` | A superseded call always rejects with an `AbortError`, even when it was cancelled while its body was being read. It is not a failure, so it is ignored |

Your own `signal` still works alongside `latest`.

## Step 3: keep the term in the address

A search that survives a reload, and that can be shared as a link, keeps its term in the URL. Read it in the page's load, and replace the address as the visitor types:

::: code-group

```ts no-check [+page.ts]
import { apiWith } from '#api';
import type { PageLoad } from './$types';

export const load: PageLoad = async (event) => {
    const term = event.url.searchParams.get('q') ?? '';
    return { term, notes: await apiWith(event).notes.list({ search: term || undefined }) };
};
```

```svelte no-check [+page.svelte]
<script lang="ts">
    import { goto } from '$app/navigation';
    import { page } from '$app/state';
    import type { PageProps } from './$types';

    let { data }: PageProps = $props();
    let term = $state(data.term);
    let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;

    function onInput() {
        clearTimeout(timer);
        timer = setTimeout(() => {
            const url = new URL(page.url);
            if (term.trim()) url.searchParams.set('q', term.trim());
            else url.searchParams.delete('q');
            void goto(url, { replaceState: true, keepFocus: true, noScroll: true });
        }, 250);
    }
</script>

<input type="search" bind:value={term} oninput={onInput} aria-label="Search notes" />
<ul>
    {#each data.notes as note (note.id)}
        <li>{note.title}</li>
    {/each}
</ul>
```

`replaceState` keeps the history clean, and `keepFocus` leaves the cursor in the box while the page loads again.

## A searchable table without the code

With `libraries { components() }` and a paged route, the generated [`<DataTable>`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries#datatable) loads again from the start whenever its `query` changes, so a search box is one `bind:value`:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { api } from '#api';
    import DataTable from '#components/DataTable.svelte';

    let search = $state('');
</script>

<input type="search" bind:value={search} aria-label="Search" />
<DataTable load={api.notes.list} query={{ search, limit: '20' }} key={(note) => note.id} columns={[{ key: 'title', label: 'Title' }]} />
```

## Good to know

- A search is a `GET`, so it is never rate limited and never blocked by the origin check. A very public search box can still be costly: keep the result count small on the server.
- For a check of one value while the visitor types, such as whether an email is taken, use a [field check](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/validation#checks-only-the-server-can-make) instead. It has its own pause and drops stale answers for you.
- With [prefetch on hover](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#prefetch-on-hover), the detail page of a result can be loaded before the click.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/pagination

# Page through long lists

You want a list that can grow to thousands of rows, such as notes, orders or users, to load a page at a time, with a "Load more" button or Previous and Next, and with the same limits on the server whatever the browser asks for.

**Time:** about 15 minutes. **Level:** beginner.

What you use:

- `getPage` on the server, which reads `cursor` and `limit` and returns a typed `Page<T>`.
- `pages` in the browser, which walks through every page.
- With Exposed, `pageBy` and `toDto`, which write the query for you.
- With `components()`, a `<DataTable>` that does all of it.

## Step 1: a paged route

Declare the route with `getPage` and return a `Page<T>`:

```kotlin
route("/api/users") {
    getPage<User> { request -> users.page(request.cursor, request.limit) }
}
```

`Page<T>` has `items` and `next`, the cursor of the next page, or `null` on the last one. `getPage` reads the `cursor` and `limit` query parameters for you:

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `""` | The path below the current route, such as `getPage<Note>("/feed")` |
| `defaultLimit` | `50` | The limit when the query has none, or one that is not a number |
| `maxLimit` | `100` | The largest limit. The limit never leaves the range from 1 to `maxLimit` |

```kotlin
route("/api/notes") {
    getPage<Note>("/feed", defaultLimit = 20, maxLimit = 200) { request -> store.page(request.cursor, request.limit) }
}
```

It also describes the route, so the generated client knows the parameters and the `Page<User>` it returns, even without Ktor's compiler plugin.

## Step 2: make the cursor

Your store returns the rows after the cursor, and the cursor of the next page:

```kotlin
fun page(cursor: String?, limit: Int): Page<User> {
    val after = cursor?.toIntOrNull() ?: 0
    val rows = all.filter { it.id > after }.sortedBy { it.id }.take(limit + 1)
    val items = rows.take(limit)
    return Page(items, next = if (rows.size > limit) items.last().id.toString() else null)
}
```

- Use the ID or sort key of the last item as the cursor, not an offset, so rows added while someone pages do not shift the results.
- Ask for one row more than the limit: if it is there, there is a next page.
- Always cap `limit` on the server. `getPage` does it for you.

## Step 3: read every page in the browser

`pages` takes the generated function and walks through the pages, one array of items at a time:

```ts
import { api, pages } from '#api';

for await (const batch of pages(api.notes.getFeed, { limit: '20' })) notes.push(...batch);
```

It stops after the page whose `next` is `null`. The options you pass as the third argument, such as a `signal`, go to every request.

## Step 4: a "Load more" button

Most pages show the first page and load more on request:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { onMount } from 'svelte';
    import { api, type Note } from '#api';

    let items = $state<Note[]>([]);
    let next = $state<string | null | undefined>(undefined);
    let loading = $state(false);

    async function more() {
        loading = true;
        try {
            const page = await api.notes.getFeed({ cursor: next ?? undefined, limit: '20' });
            items.push(...page.items);
            next = page.next ?? null;
        } finally {
            loading = false;
        }
    }

    onMount(more);
</script>

<ul>
    {#each items as note (note.id)}
        <li>{note.title}</li>
    {/each}
</ul>

{#if next}
    <button type="button" onclick={more} disabled={loading}>Load more</button>
{/if}
```

## Show how many there are

Counting every row is often the slowest part of a list, so a page only carries a total when the client asks for it with `?total=true`. `page.total { }` runs your count only then:

```kotlin
routing {
    getPage<Note>("/api/notes/all") { page ->
        val rows = store.page(page.cursor, page.limit)
        Page(rows.items, rows.next, total = page.total { store.count().toLong() })
    }
}
```

```ts
import { api } from '#api';

const first = await api.notes.all({ total: true });
const heading = `${first.total} notes`;
```

| Asked with | `page.wantsTotal` | `total` in the answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no `total` | `false` | left out, your count is never run |
| `?total=true` or `?total=1` | `true` | the number your block returns |

Ask for it on the first page only, and keep the number while you load more. `Page.total` is a `Long?`; in TypeScript it is `total?: number | null` on every page type, including the one `pages()` reads.

## With filters

A paged route that reads more query parameters, such as a filter, is written by hand. `getPage` only does what these lines do:

```kotlin
get("/api/users") {
    val cursor = call.queryParameters["cursor"]
    val limit = call.queryParameters["limit"]?.toIntOrNull() ?: 50
    val page: Page<User> = users.page(cursor, limit.coerceIn(1, 100))
    call.respond(page)
}
```

For typed filters, read the query into a class with [`call.query<T>()`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#query-parameters-as-a-class), with `cursor` and `limit` as two of its fields, and describe the route with `.queryOf<T>()`.

```ts
import { api, pages } from '#api';

for await (const users of pages(api.users.list, { limit: '100' })) table.push(...users);
```

## With Exposed

For apps that use [Exposed](https://www.jetbrains.com/exposed/) with JDBC, two helpers do the usual parts. They are only loaded when you call them, so the library does not bring Exposed with it.

`pageBy` pages a query by a column and returns a `Page`. It adds the condition for the cursor, the order and the limit, and makes the next cursor from the last row:

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.pageBy
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.toDto

getPage<Note>("/api/notes") { request ->
    transaction {
        Notes.selectAll().where { Notes.owner eq userId }.pageBy(Notes.id, request) { it.toDto<Note>() }
    }
}
```

- The column is what the list is ordered by, newest first unless you pass `descending = false`. Use one whose values are unique, such as the id, or rows with equal values can be skipped between pages.
- It takes a `PageRequest` or a cursor and a limit, for `Int` and `Long` columns. For another type, pass `parse` to turn the cursor text back into a value.
- Do not order the query yourself. A cursor that the list never gave out is answered with 400.

`toDto` turns a row into a `@Serializable` class by matching property names to column names, `starCount` to `star_count` too. Enums stored as text, nullable columns and properties with defaults work as you would expect. For a property the row does not have, or one that is stored differently, pass the value:

```kotlin
row.toDto<Note>("createdAt" to Instant.fromEpochMilliseconds(row[Notes.createdAt]), "author" to author)
```

When a required property has neither a column nor a passed value, the error names it and lists the row's columns. After a join, two tables may have a column of the same name, and the first one selected is used.

## A table without the code

With `libraries { components() }`, the generated [`<DataTable>`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries#datatable) does all of the above for a table: it takes the route's function and a list of columns, and loads, pages and shows the empty and failed states itself.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { api } from '#api';
    import DataTable from '#components/DataTable.svelte';
</script>

<DataTable
    load={api.notes.getFeed}
    query={{ limit: '20' }}
    paging="pages"
    key={(note) => note.id}
    columns={[
        { key: 'title', label: 'Title' },
        { key: 'createdAt', label: 'Created', text: (note) => new Date(note.createdAt).toLocaleDateString() }
    ]}
/>
```

`paging="pages"` shows one page with Previous and Next, and the default `'more'` adds rows with a Load more button. The pages are cursors, so the table can go forward and back, not jump to page 7.

## Good to know

- Cursor paging has no page numbers and no total. If you need "page 3 of 12", count separately and accept that rows can move between pages.
- `limit` arrives as text in the generated client (`{ limit: '20' }`) on `getPage` routes, because the route only declares the parameter, not its type. A route with a [query class](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#query-parameters-as-a-class) gets a typed number.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/live-updates

# Stream live updates

You want a page to change while someone looks at it: a counter that ticks, a list that grows when a colleague adds an item, a progress bar for a job that runs on the server.

**Time:** about 15 minutes. **Level:** intermediate.

Server-sent events need no extra client library, and the generated client turns them into an async generator. The browser opens one long `GET`, the server writes events into it, and the page reads them in a `for await` loop.

## Step 1: an event route

Install Ktor's `SSE` plugin (`io.ktor:ktor-server-sse`) and declare the route. The `describe` block gives the events a type:

```kotlin
install(SSE)
routing {
    sse("/api/ticks") {
        repeat(10) { count ->
            send(ServerSentEvent(Json.encodeToString(Tick(count))))
            delay(1000)
        }
    }.describe {
        responses {
            HttpStatusCode.OK {
                ContentType.Text.EventStream { schema = jsonSchema<Tick>() }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

Without the `describe` block, each event is a string. Run `./gradlew svelteGenerateTs` and the client has `api.ticks.list`.

## Step 2: read the events in a component

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { api, type Tick } from '#api';

    let ticks = $state<Tick[]>([]);

    $effect(() => {
        const controller = new AbortController();
        (async () => {
            for await (const tick of api.ticks.list({ signal: controller.signal })) ticks.push(tick);
        })().catch(() => undefined);
        return () => controller.abort();
    });
</script>

<p>{ticks.length} ticks so far</p>
```

- Each event's `data` is parsed as JSON into the declared type.
- Aborting the signal when the component goes away closes the connection. Without it, the stream stays open after the visitor has left the page.
- The loop ends when the server closes the stream.

## Step 3: send one change to everyone

A real app sends an event when something happens, to every open page. Keep a `MutableSharedFlow` of changes, emit into it from the routes that write, and let each event route collect it:

::: code-group

```kotlin no-check [Changes.kt]
@Serializable
data class NoteChanged(val id: Int, val kind: String)

class Changes {
    private val flow = MutableSharedFlow<NoteChanged>(extraBufferCapacity = 64)
    val events: SharedFlow<NoteChanged> = flow
    fun publish(change: NoteChanged) {
        flow.tryEmit(change)
    }
}
```

```kotlin no-check [Routes.kt]
fun Route.liveNotes(store: NoteStore, changes: Changes) {
    post("/api/notes") {
        val note = store.create(call.receive<NoteInput>())
        changes.publish(NoteChanged(note.id, "created"))
        call.respond(HttpStatusCode.Created, note)
    }

    sse("/api/notes/changes") {
        changes.events.collect { change -> send(ServerSentEvent(Json.encodeToString(change))) }
    }.describe {
        responses {
            HttpStatusCode.OK {
                ContentType.Text.EventStream { schema = jsonSchema<NoteChanged>() }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

```svelte no-check [notes/+page.svelte]
<script lang="ts">
    import { api, isAbortError, type Note } from '#api';

    let { data } = $props();
    let notes = $state<Note[]>(data.notes);

    $effect(() => {
        const controller = new AbortController();
        (async () => {
            for await (const change of api.notes.getChanges({ signal: controller.signal })) {
                if (change.kind === 'created') notes = await api.notes.list();
            }
        })().catch((error) => {
            if (!isAbortError(error)) console.warn('Live updates stopped', error);
        });
        return () => controller.abort();
    });
</script>

{#each notes as note (note.id)}
    <p>{note.title}</p>
{/each}
```

`tryEmit` never blocks the route that writes. A page that is too slow to keep up misses events beyond the buffer, which is why the page above reloads the list instead of patching it event by event.

## Good to know

- SSE counts as a GET, so it is never rate limited or blocked by the origin check.
- The default API compression leaves `text/event-stream` alone, so events arrive as soon as they are sent.
- An event route under a [page guard](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/auth#page-guards) or inside `authenticate` needs a session like any other route. The browser sends the cookie with the stream.
- When the connection drops, the loop ends with an error. Start it again after a short pause if the page must stay live.
- For simpler cases you may not need a stream at all: [refresh the page after a write](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#refresh-the-page-after-a-write), [toasts from the server](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#toasts-from-the-server) and [navigation from the server](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#navigation-from-the-server) all ride on normal responses.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/multilingual-site

# A multilingual site

You want a site in several languages, with each language at its own address such as `/de/about`, so search engines index every one. Texts, error messages from the server, dates and prices should all be in the visitor's language, and the same on the page and in an email from the server.

**Time:** about 30 minutes. **Level:** intermediate.

What you use:

- [`i18n`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries#i18n) with `LocaleStrategy.UrlPrefix`: one JSON file per language, typed functions on both sides, a prefix per language.
- [Typed routes](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/routes), which put the language in front of every link.
- [Shared formatting](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries#numbers-money-and-dates): `formatDate`, `formatMoney` and friends, the same text in TypeScript and Kotlin.
- `<LocaleSwitch>` from [`components()`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries#themetoggle-and-localeswitch).

## Step 1: turn it on

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.gradle.LocaleStrategy

svelte {
    libraries {
        routes()
        components()
        i18n {
            locales("en", "de", "fr")
            defaultLocale = "en"
            strategy = LocaleStrategy.UrlPrefix
        }
    }
}
```

```bash
./gradlew svelteSync
```

`svelteSync` writes the typed functions, `src/hooks.ts` for the prefixes, and an empty message file for every language that has none yet, in `frontend/messages`.

| Strategy | URLs | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `UrlPrefix` | `/de/about` | Public sites and SEO. Every language gets its own prerendered pages |
| `Cookie` (default) | `/about` | Apps behind a login. Prerendered pages hold the default language and switch on load |

This recipe uses `UrlPrefix`. For an app behind a login, `Cookie` is simpler and everything below works the same, except the addresses.

## Step 2: write the messages

One flat JSON file per language. `{name}` is a parameter, and a plural is written into the message:

::: code-group

```json [messages/en.json]
{
    "app-title": "Bookshop",
    "home-welcome": "Welcome, {name}!",
    "cart-count": "{count, plural, =0 {Your cart is empty} one {# book in your cart} other {# books in your cart}}",
    "cart-total": "Total: {amount}"
}
```

```json [messages/de.json]
{
    "app-title": "Buchladen",
    "home-welcome": "Willkommen, {name}!",
    "cart-count": "{count, plural, =0 {Dein Warenkorb ist leer} one {# Buch im Warenkorb} other {# Buecher im Warenkorb}}",
    "cart-total": "Summe: {amount}"
}
```

```json [messages/fr.json]
{
    "app-title": "Librairie",
    "home-welcome": "Bienvenue, {name} !",
    "cart-count": "{count, plural, =0 {Votre panier est vide} one {# livre dans votre panier} other {# livres dans votre panier}}",
    "cart-total": "Total : {amount}"
}
```

A missing key or a mismatched parameter in any language fails the build, so translations can't drift. While `svelteDev` runs, saving a file updates the functions at once.

## Step 3: use them in the pages

```svelte no-check [+page.svelte]
<script lang="ts">
    import { m } from '#i18n';
    import { formatMoney } from '#format';
    import { routes } from '#routes';

    let { data } = $props();
</script>

<svelte:head>
    <title>{m.appTitle()}</title>
</svelte:head>

<h1>{m.homeWelcome({ name: data.user.name })}</h1>
<p>{m.cartCount({ count: data.cart.items.length })}</p>
<p>{m.cartTotal({ amount: formatMoney(data.cart.total, 'EUR') })}</p>
<a href={routes.cart()}>{m.cartCount({ count: data.cart.items.length })}</a>
```

- `m.cartCount` picks "1 book" or "2 books" by the rules of the language: `one` and `other` in English, German and French, more forms in Polish or Russian.
- `routes.cart()` gives `/de/cart` on a German page. With typed routes every link keeps the language, and every language gets prerendered.
- For a link written as text, wrap it: `localizeHref('/about')` from `#i18n`.

## Step 4: let visitors switch

```svelte no-check [+layout.svelte]
<script lang="ts">
    import LocaleSwitch from '#components/LocaleSwitch.svelte';
    import '#lib/ktor-svelte/app.css';

    let { children } = $props();
</script>

<header>
    <LocaleSwitch label="Language" />
</header>

{@render children()}
```

It lists each language under its own name, such as English and Deutsch, and goes to the same page in the chosen language. Your own button does the same with `setLocale('de')` from `#i18n`.

How a language is chosen, on both sides:

1. The prefix of the address, such as `/de/...`.
2. The language cookie, which the switch sets.
3. The browser's `Accept-Language`.
4. Your `defaultLocale`.

A plain address such as `/about` is redirected to the visitor's language, such as `/de/about`, by the server.

## Step 5: translate the server

The same messages are typed functions in Kotlin. `call.messages` is in the visitor's language, by the same rules:

```kotlin no-check [Routes.kt]
import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.Messages
import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.formats
import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.localizeHref
import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.messages

get("/api/cart/summary") {
    val cart = carts.of(call.requireUser<User>())
    call.respondText(call.messages.cartCount(cart.items.size) + ", " + call.messages.cartTotal(call.formats.formatMoney(cart.total, "EUR")))
}

post("/api/orders") {
    val order = orders.place(call.requireUser<User>())
    call.toast(call.messages.orderPlaced())
    call.respondRedirect(call.localizeHref(FrontendRoutes.ordersId(order.id.toString())))
}

// an email sent later, in the customer's saved language
val german = Messages.forLocale("de")
```

Translate what the server says on its own too:

```kotlin no-check [Application.kt]
install(Svelte) {
    currentUser<User>(signInMessage = { call -> call.messages.problemSignIn() }) { /* ... */ }
    permissions<Permission, User>(refusedMessage = { call -> call.messages.problemNotAllowed() }) { user -> permissionsOf(user) }
    errorCodes<ShopError> { call, code ->
        when (code) {
            ShopError.OutOfStock -> call.messages.problemOutOfStock()
        }
    }
}
```

## Step 6: dates and money

A price on the page and the same price in an email from the server should read the same. Both sides have the same five functions, from one table for your languages:

::: code-group

```ts [In the browser]
import { formatDate, formatDateTime, formatMoney, formatNumber, formatTime } from '#format';

formatNumber(1234567.891, 2); // 1,234,567.89 in English, 1.234.567,89 in German
formatMoney(1234.5, 'EUR');
formatDate('2026-03-07'); // Mar 7, 2026 in English, 07.03.2026 in German
formatDate('2026-03-07', 'long');
formatDateTime(new Date());
formatTime(new Date());
```

```kotlin no-check [On the server]
val formats = call.formats
formats.formatMoney(order.total, "EUR")
formats.formatDate(order.placedOn)
formats.formatDateTime(order.placedAt, call.timeZone)
```

- In the browser, dates and times are in the browser's time zone. In Kotlin you pass the zone, and [`call.timeZone`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#the-visitor-s-time-zone) is the visitor's.
- `formatMoney` knows the sign and decimal places of 37 common currencies, and uses the code and two places for others.
- For "3 minutes ago", use `timeAgo` from `#format`, or `<TimeAgo value={order.placedAt} />` with `components()`, which keeps itself current.
- Weekday names, seconds, time zone names, compact numbers such as 1.2K, percent and digits other than 0 to 9 are not covered. Format those on one side only.

## Step 7: titles and link previews per language

Give each page a title and a description as message keys in its `_nav`, and the prerendered page of each language gets the preview tags in that language:

```ts no-check [about/+page.ts]
export const _nav = {
    title: 'about-title',
    description: 'about-lead'
};
```

See [Link previews](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/routes#link-previews). The [sitemap](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/endpoints#sitemap-and-robots-txt) lists the prerendered pages of every language.

## Step 8: remember the language per person

With a sign-in, a `locale` field in the [user preferences](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/auth#theme-and-language) saves the choice for the account, so it follows them to their phone:

```kotlin
@Serializable
data class Preferences(val locale: String? = null)
```

## Keep the translations complete

- In development, the [dev panel](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow) lists every message on the page that still has the default language's text, and can outline them on the page. See [Messages nobody translated yet](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries#messages-nobody-translated-yet).
- `./gradlew svelteVerifyMessages` lists messages that nothing uses any more. See [Messages nothing uses](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries#messages-nothing-uses).
- `svelteSync` refuses a plural without `other`, a form that a language never uses, or a count that is a number in one language and text in another.

## Good to know

- With `UrlPrefix`, a link that bypasses `routes` and `localizeHref` leads to the plain path, which then redirects. It works, but the page is not prerendered in that language. `svelteVerifyRoutes` finds string links.
- A page with a parameter, such as `/books/[id]`, is not prerendered, so it sets its own title when it runs.
- Kotlin plural rules are generated for the configured languages and checked against the browser's for the western and northern European, Slavic and Baltic languages, Romanian, Hebrew, Arabic, and languages without plural forms such as Japanese. A language outside that list is treated like English in Kotlin.
- Formatting covers 64 locales. A region without its own entry uses its language, and a language that is not in the table is formatted like English.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/ktor

# Ktor settings

Every setting of `install(Svelte) { }`, grouped by topic, with its default. To pick settings with checkboxes instead, use the [configurator](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/configurator). To see the settings your app really runs with, run [`./gradlew svelteConfig`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/gradle#review-your-configuration).

<Badge type="tip" text="Ktor plugin" />

## All defaults at a glance

The values shown are the defaults.

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    apiPrefixes("/api")
    paramRoutes()
    spaFallback = "200.html"
    notFoundPage = "404.html"
    source = SvelteSource.Classpath
    generateTs = false
    generateTsOutput = null
    apiDocs = false
    apiDocsPath = "/api/docs"
    routing = SvelteRouting.Automatic
    loginPage = null
    statusEndpoint = false
    internalAccess { }
    healthEndpoint = false
    originCheck = true
    hideErrorDetails = true
    apiCompression = true
    inlinePublicConfig = true
    buildHeader = true
    requestIds = true
    accessLog = false
    publicBuildInfo = false
    defaultTimeZone = "UTC"
    allowedOrigins()
    maxApiBodySize = 1048576
    maxJsonDepth = 64
    maxJsonStringLength = null
    sitemap = true
    defaultFavicon = true
    siteUrl = null

    securityHeaders {
        enabled = true
        contentTypeOptions = "nosniff"
        frameOptions = "DENY"
        referrerPolicy = "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
        contentSecurityPolicy = null
        automaticContentSecurityPolicy = true
    }

    cache {
        immutable = "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"
        html = "no-cache"
        other = "no-cache"
    }

    dev {
        url = "http://localhost:5173"
        mode = DevMode.Auto
        allowRemote = false
        slowApiCall = 500.milliseconds
        panel = true
        browserLogs = true
        refreshAfterRestart = true
        errorOverlay = true
        startupTiming = true
    }

    rateLimit {
        enabled = true
        apiWrites = 120
        period = 1.minutes
        algorithm = RateLimitAlgorithm.FixedWindow
    }

    transport {
    }
}
```

Features that are off until you call them, such as `frontendErrors()`, `webVitals()`, `idempotency()`, `currentUser`, `guards` or `errorCodes`, are in the tables below.

## Serving the frontend

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `apiPrefixes(...)` | `"/api"` | Paths the frontend never answers, and the routes included in `generateTs`. `/api` matches `/api` and `/api/x`, not `/apiary` |
| `paramRoutes(...)` | none | SvelteKit route patterns such as `/items/[id]`, `/docs/[...rest]` and `/blog/[[page]]`. Matching paths get the fallback even when the request does not accept HTML, for example link previews or tests. Paths with a file extension still return 404. Also used to group [page timings](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/monitoring#page-timings) |
| `spaFallback` | `"200.html"` | Page for client-side routes. Must match the adapter's `fallback` option. `null` disables it |
| `notFoundPage` | `"404.html"` | Page served with status 404. `null` disables it |
| `source` | `SvelteSource.Classpath` | Where the build comes from. `SvelteSource.Directory(path)` serves a build from disk |
| `routing` | `SvelteRouting.Automatic` | `Manual` lets you place the frontend yourself with [`svelte()`](#route-svelte), for example behind authentication. See [Auth](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/auth) |
| `cache { }` | see below | `Cache-Control` values |
| `sitemap` | `true` | Serves a generated `/sitemap.xml` and `/robots.txt` when the build has none. See [Sitemap and robots.txt](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/endpoints#sitemap-and-robots-txt) |
| `siteUrl` | `null` | Public address used in the sitemap, such as `https://example.com`. `null` takes it from the request |
| `defaultFavicon` | `true` | Serves a ktor-svelte favicon while the app has none of its own. See [Default favicon](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/endpoints#default-favicon) |

### cache { }

| Setting | Default | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `immutable` | `"public, max-age=31536000, immutable"` | Hashed files under `_app/immutable/**` |
| `html` | `"no-cache"` | HTML pages |
| `other` | `"no-cache"` | Every other file |

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    paramRoutes("/notes/[id]", "/docs/[...rest]")
    cache {
        other = "public, max-age=3600"
    }
}
```

## Generated TypeScript and API docs

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `generateTs` | `false` | Generates TypeScript from your routes in development mode. See [Generated TypeScript](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/typescript) |
| `generateTsOutput` | `null` | Output directory. `null` means `src/lib/api` in your frontend |
| `apiDocs` | `false` | Serves Swagger UI in development mode, and elsewhere when `internalAccess` is set. See [API docs](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/endpoints#api-docs) |
| `apiDocsPath` | `"/api/docs"` | Path of the Swagger UI page |
| `errorResponse<T>(statuses)` | none | Declares an error body that handlers outside your routes send, so the generated client types it. Takes status codes of 400 and above. See [Calling the API](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api) |
| `errorCodes<E>(message)` | none | One enum of named error codes for the whole app, optionally with a message for each. See [Error codes](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#error-codes) |
| `constants(...)` | none | Kotlin objects whose values are copied into the frontend. See [Shared constants](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/typescript#shared-constants) |
| `cookies(...)` | none | [Typed cookies](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/sessions#typed-cookies) that both sides read and write. A name may be declared once |

## Runtime config

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `publicConfig(value)` | none | Values for the frontend. `publicConfig { ... }` reads them again on every request in development. See [Runtime config](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/runtime-config) |
| `inlinePublicConfig` | `true` | Puts the public config into every page, so the frontend has it without a request |
| `defaultTimeZone` | `"UTC"` | What [`call.timeZone`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#the-visitor-s-time-zone) returns when a request does not say which zone the visitor is in |

## Users and sign-in

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `currentUser<T>(path, signInMessage, sessionEnds, extendSession) { find }` | none | How the server finds the signed-in user. Served at `/api/current-user` (under your first API prefix) unless you pass `path`. See [The current user](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/auth#the-current-user) |
| `permissions<P, U>(refusedMessage) { of }` | none | One enum of permissions and how to read a user's set. See [Permissions](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/auth#permissions) |
| `guards { }` | none | Which pages need a signed-in user (`signedIn(...)`) or a permission (`permission(p, ...)`). Closes the API below the same name too. See [Page guards](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/auth#page-guards) |
| `preferences<T, U>(defaults, path, load, save)` | none | Per-user preferences kept on the server. Served at `/api/preferences` unless you pass `path`. See [User preferences](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/auth#user-preferences) |
| `loginPage` | `null` | Path of the login page. A 401 from the API then opens it with the current page as `next`. See [The login page](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/auth#the-login-page) |

An app has one `currentUser`, one `permissions` enum, one `errorCodes` enum and one `preferences` class. Declaring one twice fails at startup.

## Security

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `originCheck` | `true` | Refuses cross-site requests to API paths for every method except GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE. See [API request guards](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/security#api-request-guards) |
| `allowedOrigins(...)` | none | Extra origins, such as `https://admin.example.com`, that may write to the API |
| `maxApiBodySize` | `1048576` (1 MiB) | Largest request body on API paths, in bytes. `null` disables it |
| `maxJsonDepth` | `64` | Refuses JSON request bodies on API paths that nest deeper than this, with 400. `null` turns it off |
| `maxJsonStringLength` | `null` | Refuses JSON request bodies on API paths with a longer string, with 400. Off by default |
| `hideErrorDetails` | `true` | Answers unhandled exceptions in production without their message. See [API request guards](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/security#api-request-guards) |
| `securityHeaders { }` | see below | Security headers and the Content-Security-Policy |
| `rateLimit { }` | see below | Limits API writes per client, and holds named limits |
| `idempotency { }` | off | Answers a repeated `Idempotency-Key` with the stored first answer. See [Writes that are safe to send twice](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#writes-that-are-safe-to-send-twice) |

### securityHeaders { }

See [Security headers](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/security#security-headers).

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Sends security headers. `false` turns all of them off |
| `contentTypeOptions` | `"nosniff"` | `X-Content-Type-Options`. `null` leaves it out |
| `frameOptions` | `"DENY"` | `X-Frame-Options`. `null` leaves it out |
| `referrerPolicy` | `"strict-origin-when-cross-origin"` | `Referrer-Policy`. `null` leaves it out |
| `contentSecurityPolicy` | `null` | Your own policy, sent unchanged on every response. `null` uses the automatic policy |
| `automaticContentSecurityPolicy` | `true` | Sends a strict CSP built from the inline scripts of each HTML page |
| `allowCspSources(directive, sources)` | none | Adds sources to one directive of the automatic policy |

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    securityHeaders {
        allowCspSources("img-src", "https://images.example.com")
    }
}
```

### rateLimit { }

See [API request guards](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/security#api-request-guards).

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | `false` removes the default limit and lets you install Ktor's `RateLimit` yourself |
| `apiWrites` | `120` | Writes per client and period on API paths. `0` keeps the named limits but drops the default one |
| `period` | `1.minutes` | The period of the default limit |
| `algorithm` | `RateLimitAlgorithm.FixedWindow` | `FixedWindow`, `SlidingWindow` or `TokenBucket` |
| `key { call -> }` | the client address | What tells clients apart, for every limit |
| `limit(name, requests, per, algorithm, key)` | none | A named limit for Ktor's `rateLimit(RateLimitName(name))`, such as for login |

### idempotency { }

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `ttl` | `10.minutes` | How long an answer is kept. Must be above zero |
| `maxEntries` | `10000` | How many answers are kept in memory. At least 1 |

## Responses

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `apiCompression` | `true` | Compresses API responses of 1 KiB or more with gzip, deflate or zstd. See [API compression](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/transport#api-compression) |
| `transport { }` | nothing installed | JSON, XML and compression: `json { }`, `xml()`, `negotiation { }`, `compression { }`. See [Transport](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/transport) |
| `buildHeader` | `true` | Sends the frontend build fingerprint on API responses as `X-Ktor-Svelte-Build`, so the client can notice a deploy |
| `requestIds` | `true` | Gives every request an `X-Request-Id`, keeps one sent by the client and logs it with unhandled errors |

## Built-in endpoints

See [Built-in endpoints](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/endpoints).

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `healthEndpoint` | `false` | Serves `/_ktor-svelte/health` for load balancers and orchestrators. See [Health endpoint](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/endpoints#health-endpoint) |
| `healthCheck { }` | none | Adds a check of your own. Every check must return `true` for the app to be up |
| `statusEndpoint` | `false` | Serves build and proxy details at `/_ktor-svelte/status`, to this machine only. See [Status endpoint](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/endpoints#status-endpoint) |
| `internalAccess { }` | this machine only | Who may see the status endpoint and the API docs besides this machine: a `token`, `networks(...)` or your own `allow { }` check. See [Who may see internal endpoints](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/endpoints#who-may-see-internal-endpoints) |
| `publicBuildInfo` | `false` | Serves the app's [build info](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/monitoring#build-info) at `/_ktor-svelte/build.json`, for `loadBuildInfo()` in the browser. Off because it tells every visitor the version and the commit |

## Monitoring

See [Monitoring](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/monitoring).

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `accessLog` | `false` | Logs one line per request in production to the `ktor-svelte.access` logger: `method=GET path=/api/notes status=200 ms=12 id=...`. The query string is left out, because it can hold secrets, and requests for build assets under `/_app/` are skipped. Development mode never logs these |
| `frontendErrors { }` | off | Browsers report uncaught errors to the `ktor-svelte.frontend` logger. Settings: `perClientPerMinute = 10`, `maxBodyBytes = 8192` (256 to 65536) |
| `webVitals { }` | off | Browsers report page timings into `svelteMetrics`. Settings: `sampleRate = 0.1` (above 0, at most 1), `perClientPerMinute = 10` |

## Development

See [Dev workflow](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow).

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `dev.url` | `"http://localhost:5173"` | Vite URL. The `KTOR_SVELTE_DEV_SERVER` environment variable overrides it |
| `dev.mode` | `DevMode.Auto` | `Auto` follows Ktor's development mode. `Always` and `Never` force it |
| `dev.allowRemote` | `false` | Lets other machines use the dev proxy, and lets `dev.url` point at another machine |
| `dev.slowApiCall` | `500.milliseconds` | Logs API calls that take longer than this in development. `null` turns it off |
| `dev.panel` | `true` | Shows the [dev panel](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow#the-dev-panel) of recent API calls, with status, timing and validation errors, on pages proxied from Vite |
| `dev.browserLogs` | `true` | Sends browser console output, uncaught errors and unhandled rejections from pages proxied from Vite to the app's log |
| `dev.refreshAfterRestart` | `true` | After the app restarts in development, open pages rerun their `load` functions, so a Kotlin change shows up without a manual reload |
| `dev.errorOverlay` | `true` | Shows the Kotlin exception of a failed API call in the browser, in development. Needs `dev.panel` |
| `dev.startupTiming` | `true` | Logs what the startup time was spent on in development, with the parts you wrapped in [`startupStep`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow#startup-timing) |

## Route.svelte()

With `routing = SvelteRouting.Manual`, you place the frontend in your own routing. Call `install(Svelte)` first.

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| `svelte()` | Serves the frontend for every path under this route. Pages get `private` caching, so shared proxies do not keep them |
| `svelte(public = listOf(...))` | Serves only the listed paths, with normal caching. A path ending in `/*` covers everything below it |

```kotlin
routing {
    svelte(public = listOf("/login", "/_app/*"))
    authenticate("session") {
        svelte()
    }
}
```

The `public` list must include your login page and `/_app/*`, or the login page cannot load. In development mode, `svelte(public = ...)` also opens the paths Vite needs, so hot reload works on your login page. The files of an [installable app](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries#installable-app), such as `/service-worker.js` and `/ktor-svelte/*`, stay public too, since a browser fetches them without a session. See [Auth](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/auth).

## Functions for your routes

Besides the settings, the plugin gives your routes these helpers:

| Function | What it does | See |
|---|---|---|
| `call.pathParameter<T>(name)` | Reads a path parameter in the type you need | [Path parameters](#path-parameters) |
| `call.timeZone` | The visitor's time zone, or `defaultTimeZone` | [The visitor's time zone](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#the-visitor-s-time-zone) |
| `call.toast(...)` | Sends a toast with the answer | [Toasts from the server](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#toasts-from-the-server) |
| `call.navigateTo(path)` | Tells the client to go to a page after the call | [Navigation from the server](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#navigation-from-the-server) |
| `call.respondIfStale(sent, current) { record }` | Answers 409 with the current record when the write was based on an old version | [Two people, one record](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#two-people-one-record) |
| `call.requireOwner(record) { user: User, record -> ... }` | Returns the record when it belongs to the caller, answers 404, 401 or 403 otherwise; `route.ownerChecked()` describes those answers | [Owner checks](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/auth#owner-checks) |
| `call.respondLoginRedirect()` | Redirects to `loginPage`, carrying the current page | [The login page](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/auth#the-login-page) |
| `route.timeout(30.seconds)` | Cancels the handler after the limit with a 503, and makes the generated call use it as its timeout | [A time limit per route](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#a-time-limit-per-route) |
| `getPage<T>(path) { }` | A paged `GET` route with `cursor` and `limit` | [Page through long lists](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/pagination) |
| `resource<T, ID>(path) { }` | The routes of one class, declared in one block | [Resource routes](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/typescript#resource-routes) |
| `application.buildInfo` | Version, commit and commit time of the build | [Build info](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/monitoring#build-info) |
| `application.svelteMetrics` | Refusal counters and web vitals | [Monitoring](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/monitoring) |
| `startupStep(name) { }` | Names a part of startup for the dev startup log | [Startup timing](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow#startup-timing) |

## Path parameters

`call.pathParameter<T>(name)` reads a path parameter in the type you need, so a route does not parse it by hand:

```kotlin
get("/api/notes/{id}") {
    val id = call.pathParameter<Int>("id")
    call.respond(store.create(Note(id, "x")))
}
```

| Type | Reads |
|---|---|
| `String` | The text as it is |
| `Int`, `Long` | A whole number |
| `UUID` | A UUID |
| An enum | A constant by name, in any case |

A value that does not fit, such as `/api/notes/abc`, ends the request with Ktor's `NotFoundException`: the address names nothing, so the answer is 404, through your `StatusPages` if you have one. Asking for a parameter the route's path does not have, or for a type it cannot read, is a mistake in the route and fails with a 500 that says so.

## Good to know

- A route of yours such as `get("/{slug}")` beats the frontend. That is intended, but it can hide pages. The app logs it: "the Ktor route GET /about hides the frontend page about.html. Move the route or rename the page."
- ETags are content hashes from the manifest, so 304 responses are cheap and stay valid across restarts.
- If you set `adapter({ precompress: true })`, the `.br` and `.gz` files are served based on `Accept-Encoding`. Files the adapter did not compress, such as those from `static/`, are gzipped by `svelteBundle` unless you set `precompress = false` in [Gradle](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/gradle). `.zst` files next to them, for example from a Vite compression plugin, are bundled too and preferred for browsers that accept `zstd`, since they decompress faster.
- If the frontend build is missing, the app fails at startup in production with a message explaining what to do. In Ktor development mode it logs a warning instead, and frontend routes return a 503 explaining the problem.
- ktor-svelte installs Ktor's `RequestBodyLimit` and `RateLimit` itself. To use your own, set `maxApiBodySize = null` or `rateLimit { enabled = false }`. The same goes for `ContentNegotiation` and `Compression` when you use `transport { }`.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/gradle

# Gradle settings and tasks

Every setting of `svelte { }`, every task and every Gradle property.

<Badge type="info" text="Gradle" />

## All defaults at a glance

The values shown are the defaults.

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.gradle.PackageManager

svelte {
    frontendDir = layout.projectDirectory.dir("frontend")
    outputDir = "build"
    packageManager = PackageManager.Auto
    buildScript = "build"
    buildEnv = emptySet()
    addRuntimeDependency = true
    includeSourceMaps = false
    shortTaskNames = true
    timingSummary = true
    precompress = true
    verifyLeaks = true
    dev {
        port = 5173
        script = "dev"
        debugPort = 5005
        openBrowser = true
        https = false
        httpsPort = 8443
    }
}
```

`bunVersion` is unset by default, and `libraries { }` is empty.

## Settings

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `frontendDir` | `frontend` | Directory of the SvelteKit project |
| `outputDir` | `"build"` | Adapter output, a folder inside `frontendDir` given relative to it. Must match the adapter's `pages` option |
| `packageManager` | `PackageManager.Auto` | `Auto`, `Bun`, `Pnpm`, `Npm` or `Yarn`. `Auto` picks from `bun.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `package-lock.json` or `yarn.lock` |
| `bunVersion` | unset | An exact Bun version, such as `"1.3.14"`, that ktor-svelte downloads and uses instead of the Bun on `PATH`. See [Pin Bun](#pin-bun) |
| `buildScript` | `"build"` | `package.json` script that builds the frontend |
| `buildEnv` | empty | Environment variables that affect the build. Declare any your frontend reads through `$env`, or Gradle can reuse a stale build. Also counted as public by `svelteVerifyLeaks` |
| `addRuntimeDependency` | `true` | Adds `ktor-svelte-server` to `implementation`, at the plugin's own version, and `ktor-svelte-test` to a `browserTest` suite |
| `includeSourceMaps` | `false` | Ships `.map` files in the JAR, where anyone can download them |
| `shortTaskNames` | `true` | Registers `dev`, `sync`, `doctor` and `gen` as [short names](#short-task-names) for the tasks used most |
| `timingSummary` | `true` | Ends a build that ran the frontend with a short table of how long each step took. See [Build times](#build-times) |
| `precompress` | `true` | Gzips text files of 1 KiB or more that have no `.br` or `.gz` variant yet, such as SVG, JSON and fonts from `static/`, and keeps the result only when it saves at least 10% |
| `verifyLeaks` | `true` | Runs `svelteVerifyLeaks` before the build goes into the JAR. See [Secrets in the frontend build](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/runtime-config#secrets-in-the-frontend-build) |
| `libraries { }` | empty | Tailwind, DaisyUI, Lucide, i18n, typed routes and more. See [Libraries](#libraries) |

The package manager must already be installed unless you set `bunVersion`. The plugin does not download Node.

### dev { }

See [Dev workflow](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow#dev-settings).

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `dev.port` | `5173` | Port passed to Vite by `svelteDev` and `svelteDevAll` |
| `dev.script` | `"dev"` | `package.json` script that starts Vite |
| `dev.debugPort` | `5005` | Port where the app started by `svelteDevAll` listens for a debugger, on `127.0.0.1` only. `0` turns it off |
| `dev.openBrowser` | `true` | Opens the app in the default browser once `svelteDevAll` is ready, the first time only. Never in CI or without a display |
| `dev.https` | `false` | Serves the app started by `svelteDevAll` over HTTPS too, with a development certificate from `~/.ktor-svelte/dev-https`. See [HTTPS in development](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow#https-in-development) |
| `dev.httpsPort` | `8443` | Port of that HTTPS address, on `127.0.0.1` only |

### Misspelled settings

In a Groovy `build.gradle`, a misspelled setting such as `fronendDir = file('web')` fails with the closest name and the list of settings, instead of Gradle's generic missing property error. The same goes for the blocks inside `svelte { }`. The Kotlin DSL catches the same mistake when it compiles the script.

## Libraries

Everything in `libraries { }` is off until you call it. `svelteSync` installs what you turn on and writes the generated files. See [Frontend libraries](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries) for each one.

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.gradle.DaisyTheme

svelte {
    libraries {
        daisyUi {
            themes(DaisyTheme.Light, DaisyTheme.Dracula)
            defaultTheme(DaisyTheme.Light)
            prefersDark(DaisyTheme.Dracula)
        }
        lucide()
        routes()
        toasts()
        i18n {
            locales("en", "de")
        }
    }
}
```

| Call | Settings inside | Default inside |
|---|---|---|
| `tailwind { }` | `typography()`, `forms()` | both off |
| `daisyUi { }` | `themes(...)`, `defaultTheme(...)`, `prefersDark(...)`, `customTheme(name, colorScheme) { }`. Turns Tailwind on too | `colorScheme = "light"` for a custom theme |
| `lucide { }` | `allIcons()` | off: only the icons you use |
| `i18n { }` | `locales(...)`, `defaultLocale`, `strategy`, `messagesDir` | `defaultLocale` is the first locale, `strategy = LocaleStrategy.Cookie`, `messagesDir` is `frontend/messages` |
| `routes { }` | `dir` | `frontend/src/routes` |
| `toasts { }` | `reloadPrompt()` | off |
| `fonts(sans) { }` | `mono`, `variable` | `variable = true` |
| `installable { }` | `name`, `shortName`, `description`, `themeColor`, `backgroundColor`, `display`, `icon` | colors `"#ffffff"`, `display = "standalone"` |
| `images()` | none | |
| `components()` | none | |
| `charts()` | none | |
| `generatedPackage` | | `"io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte"`, the package of the generated Kotlin |

## Review your configuration

`./gradlew svelteConfig` gives an overview of how ktor-svelte is set up in your app. It lists the Gradle settings, then starts your app once to read the effective `install(Svelte) { }` settings, the same way `svelteGenerateTs` does, so it shows what really runs, including values set from environment variables. Settings you changed are marked with their default, which makes it easy to see what a new version changed or added after an upgrade.

Then it scores the setup and lists what to change:

```text
Scores
  Security              [#########-]  90%  10 of 11
  Performance           [##########] 100%  4 of 4
  Operations            [#######---]  66%  2 of 3
  Developer experience  [##########] 100%  5 of 5

Suggestions
  - [Security] Set maxJsonStringLength = 100_000, or the longest text your API accepts.
  - [Operations] Set healthEndpoint = true and point your orchestrator at /_ktor-svelte/health.
```

The checks cover the origin check, security headers and CSP, error details, body and JSON limits, rate limits, the dev proxy, source maps, compression, caching, image optimization, health and request IDs, the sitemap address, a pinned Bun, generated TypeScript, error toasts, typed routes and dev tooling. A suggestion is advice, not an error: a public API may well do without `healthEndpoint`. Without the `application` plugin, only the Gradle settings are shown.

## Pin Bun

A fresh CI image or laptop often has no package manager, so the first build fails. Set `bunVersion` and the plugin downloads that exact Bun from Bun's GitHub releases the first time a task needs it:

```kotlin
svelte {
    bunVersion = "1.3.14"
}
```

- The archive is checked against the release's `SHASUMS256.txt` before it is unpacked into `~/.gradle/ktor-svelte/bun/<version>/`, and every later build reuses it.
- Every task then uses this Bun, even when another one is on `PATH`, so all machines build with the same version.
- With `packageManager = AUTO`, Bun becomes the package manager. Bun runs Vite itself, so Node is not needed.
- It works on Windows, macOS and Linux, including Alpine, on x64 and arm64.
- Behind a proxy, set Java's `https.proxyHost` and `https.proxyPort` in `gradle.properties` with the `systemProp.` prefix.

## Build times

A build that installed or built the frontend ends with how long each step took, so you can see where a slow build spends its time:

```text
ktor-svelte build times:
  install          0.2s  up to date
  frontend build  12.4s
  bundling         0.3s
  Kotlin compile   4.1s  from cache
  total           17.0s
```

- It lists the steps of this project that were part of the build: `svelteInstall`, `svelteBuild`, `svelteBundle` and `compileKotlin`. A step that did no work says why: `up to date`, `from cache`, `skipped` or `failed`.
- A build where no frontend step ran, such as a second `./gradlew build` with nothing changed, prints nothing.
- It works with the configuration cache. Turn it off with `svelte { timingSummary = false }`.

## Format both sides

One command formats Kotlin and the frontend, and one checks them:

```bash
./gradlew format
```

```bash
./gradlew formatCheck
```

`format` runs the frontend's `format` script from `package.json`, and `formatCheck` runs its `lint` script. Projects made by the setup script have both, as `prettier --write .` and `prettier --check . && eslint .`. For Kotlin, they run `ktlintFormat` and `ktlintCheck` when the ktlint Gradle plugin is applied, or `spotlessApply` and `spotlessCheck` with Spotless. Without either, Kotlin is left alone and the task says so. A frontend without the script is skipped with a hint.

If your build already has a task called `format` or `formatCheck`, ktor-svelte does not register its own. The frontend half is always there as `svelteFormat` and `svelteFormatCheck`.

### Check before every commit

`svelteGitHooks` installs a git pre-commit hook in your clone that runs `formatCheck` and `svelteVerifySync`, so an unformatted file or a stale generated file never reaches a commit:

```bash
./gradlew svelteGitHooks
```

A commit that fails the check is stopped with the command that fixes it. `git commit --no-verify` skips the hook once, and `./gradlew svelteGitHooks --remove` takes it out again. The hook lives in `.git`, which git does not share, so everyone on the team runs the task once. A pre-commit hook that something else installed is never replaced: the task stops and tells you to call the two tasks from your own hook.

### Generated files without merge conflicts

Two branches that both add a page, an icon or an API route both change the same generated files, and git reports a conflict in a file nobody wrote. The same `svelteGitHooks` run ends that in your clone:
