- When both sides of a merge or a rebase changed a generated file, git keeps one side and does not stop.
- Right after the merge or rebase, `svelteSync` and `svelteGenerateTs` run and write the files as they belong to the merged code. If `git status` then shows changes, commit them.

It covers `src/lib/ktor-svelte` and `src/lib/api`, through a `merge=ktor-svelte` attribute in the `.gitattributes` of those folders. Run `svelteSync` and `svelteGenerateTs` once after upgrading so those files get the attribute. In a clone where nobody ran `svelteGitHooks`, git ignores the attribute and merges those files the way it always did.

A merge that stops for a conflict in one of your own files does not regenerate when you finish it. The pre-commit hook and `check` still notice stale generated files, and `./gradlew svelteSync svelteGenerateTs` fixes them. If a `post-merge` or `post-rewrite` hook from another tool is already there, such as Git LFS, it stays, and the task tells you to run those two tasks yourself after such a merge.

## Short task names

The four tasks you type most have a short name:

| Short | Same as |
|---|---|
| `./gradlew dev` | `svelteDevAll` |
| `./gradlew sync` | `svelteSync` |
| `./gradlew doctor` | `svelteDoctor` |
| `./gradlew gen` | `svelteGenerateTs` |

They are the same tasks under another name, so options work as well: `./gradlew doctor --fix`, `./gradlew dev --full-stack-traces`. `dev` and `gen` exist when the long tasks do, which is in a project with the `application` plugin.

A short name that your build or another plugin already uses is left alone, and the long name keeps working. Set `shortTaskNames = false` to register none of them. The docs use the long names, because those always exist.

## Gradle tasks

Tasks marked "app" exist only in a project with the `application` plugin, because they start your app. For what each check catches and what its output looks like, see [Checks and tooling](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/checks-and-tooling).

### Build

These run as part of `jar` and `processResources`, so you rarely call them yourself.

| Task | What it does |
|---|---|
| `svelteInstall` | Installs the frontend dependencies from the lockfile |
| `svelteBuild` | Builds the frontend with `buildScript` |
| `svelteVerifyLeaks` | Fails when a secret value from the environment or a `.env` file is in the frontend build. Runs after `svelteBuild` while `verifyLeaks` is on. See [Secrets in the frontend build](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/runtime-config#secrets-in-the-frontend-build) |
| `svelteBundle` | Copies the build into the JAR's resources with its manifest, and precompresses files |
| `svelteSync` | Installs configured libraries and writes their generated files. Short name `sync` |
| `svelteVerifySync` | Fails if libraries don't match your config. Runs before every frontend build |
| `svelteGenerateSources` | Generates Kotlin for your libraries. Runs before compiling |
| `svelteBuildInfo` | Writes the version, the git commit and its time into the build, for [`buildInfo`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/monitoring#build-info). Runs before resources are processed |

### Develop

| Task | Options | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `svelteDevAll` (app) | `--full-stack-traces` | Runs Vite, the Kotlin compiler and your app, and restarts the app when Kotlin changes. Short name `dev`. See [Dev workflow](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow) |
| `svelteDev` | | Starts Vite |
| `svelteGenerateTs` (app) | | Starts your app once to regenerate TypeScript. Needs `generateTs = true`. Short name `gen` |

### Check

| Task | Options | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `svelteVerifyTs` (app) | | Starts your app once and fails if the committed TypeScript is out of date. Runs as part of `check` |
| `svelteVerifyRoutes` | `--fix` | Lists links to pages that are written as strings, in the frontend and in Kotlin `respondRedirect` calls, with the [typed route](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/routes#finding-links-that-are-still-strings) to use instead, and fails if it finds any. `--fix` rewrites the ones it can |
| `svelteVerifyLinks` | `--strict` | Lists [internal links that lead to no page, no API route and no static file](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/routes#finding-links-that-lead-nowhere) |
| `svelteVerifyLoads` | | Fails if an API call inside a `load` function [uses neither `apiWith(event)` nor `{ fetch }`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#in-load-functions) |
| `svelteVerifyMessages` | `--strict` | Lists [i18n messages nothing uses](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries#messages-nothing-uses) |
| `svelteVerifyApiRoutes` | `--strict` | Lists [API routes that nothing in the frontend calls](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/typescript#routes-nothing-calls) |
| `svelteApiChanges` | `--against`, `--strict` | Lists [what changed in the API for callers](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/typescript#what-changed-for-callers) since `origin/main`, or the revision given with `--against`. `--strict` fails on a change that can break them |
| `svelteVerifyA11y` (app) | `--path`, `-Pbrowser` | Packages the app, opens its prerendered pages in a browser in light and dark, and fails on [accessibility problems](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/browser-tests#accessibility) that axe finds. Not part of `check` |
| `svelteSmokeTest` (app) | `--path`, `--skip`, `--start-seconds` | Packages the app, starts it in production mode, and fails unless [every prerendered page and the API routes are answered](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/deployment#smoke-test). Not part of `check` |
| `svelteDoctor` | `--fix` | Checks adapter, adapter output against `svelte.outputDir`, the bundled manifest, `#api`, tsconfig, Kit version, Node, tool and port, that every installed package still has its files, and that `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` points to a file, and says what to fix. `--fix` repairs what needs no decision. Short name `doctor` |
| `svelteConfig` | | Prints every setting of `svelte { }` and of `install(Svelte) { }`, marks the ones you changed from the default, scores the setup and suggests what to turn on. See [Review your configuration](#review-your-configuration) |
| `svelteCheck` | | Runs the frontend's `check` script |

### Create and change code

| Task | Options | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `svelteInit` | `--package-manager=bun` | Creates a working SvelteKit project in an empty `frontendDir`, then runs `svelteSync` and `svelteGenerateRunConfigurations` |
| `svelteAdd` | `--page`, `--route`, `--crud` | [Creates a page](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/routes#a-new-page) with a typed load: `svelteAdd --page=notes/[id]`. `--route` adds a Kotlin route to start from. `svelteAdd --crud=Note` writes [list, detail and form pages for a class](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/routes#pages-for-a-class) |
| `svelteRename` | `--page`, `--to`, `--force` | [Moves a page](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/routes#renaming-a-page) and rewrites its typed route calls in the frontend and in Kotlin: `svelteRename --page=notes/[id] --to=memos/[id]`. `--force` renames even with uncommitted changes |

### Test and deploy

| Task | Options | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `browserTest` | `-Pbrowser` | Yours: a test suite with this name gets [the browser test kit](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/browser-tests), the packaged app and the browser from `-Pbrowser` |
| `svelteRecordTest` (app) | `--name`, `-Pbrowser` | Opens the packaged app in a browser and writes what you do there as a [Kotlin browser test](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/browser-tests#record-a-test): `--name=SignIn` |
| `svelteDeploy` | `--host`, `--force` | Writes the [deploy configuration](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/deployment#railway) for a host from the project's settings. Railway so far |

### Format and git

| Task | Options | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `format`, `formatCheck` | | [Format, or check the formatting of, Kotlin and the frontend](#format-both-sides) in one go |
| `svelteFormat`, `svelteFormatCheck` | | The frontend half of those: run the `format` and the `lint` script |
| `svelteGitHooks` | `--remove` | Installs a [pre-commit hook](#check-before-every-commit) that runs `formatCheck` and `svelteVerifySync`, and keeps [generated files out of merge conflicts](#generated-files-without-merge-conflicts). `--remove` takes the hook out |

### Dependencies and cleanup

| Task | Options | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `svelteRun` | `--script`, `--args` | Runs any `package.json` script: `svelteRun --script=lint --args="--fix --quiet"`. Quote an argument that contains spaces |
| `svelteOutdated` | | Lists outdated frontend dependencies |
| `svelteUpdateDependencies` | | Updates frontend dependencies and the lockfile |
| `svelteClean` | | Deletes `node_modules`, `.svelte-kit` and the build output |
| `deepClean` | | Runs `clean`, then also deletes the project's `.gradle` and `.kotlin` directories, `node_modules`, `.svelte-kit`, `.vite`, `.turbo`, `.cache`, `.eslintcache` and the build output. Lockfiles and generated files are kept. Files a running Gradle daemon or IDE still holds, which happens on Windows, are skipped with a warning |

### IDE

| Task | Options | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `svelteLiveTemplates` | `--install`, `--config-dir` | Writes IntelliJ [live templates](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow#live-templates) to `build/ktor-svelte/live-templates/`. `--install` copies them into every IntelliJ IDEA and WebStorm configuration it finds, `--config-dir=...` picks another JetBrains folder |
| `svelteGenerateRunConfigurations` | | Writes IntelliJ [run configurations](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow#ide-run-configurations) to `.run/`, keeping any that exist: `Dev`, `Dev and debug`, `Debug app`, `Debug frontend`, `Ktor`, `Vite`, `Generate TypeScript`, `Build JAR`, `Type check frontend` and `Update frontend dependencies` |

## Gradle properties

| Property | Effect |
|---|---|
| `-Psvelte.skip=true` | Skips the frontend build, and warns if a JAR is being built |
| `-Psvelte.dev=true` | Same as skip, and also sets `-Dio.ktor.development=true` on `run` |
| `-Psvelte.verifyTs=false` | Leaves `svelteVerifyTs` out of `check` |
| `-Psvelte.verbose=true` | Shows the package manager and Vite output of `svelteInstall`, `svelteBuild`, `svelteSync` and `svelteInit`. Without it, that output is hidden when the command succeeds and printed in full when it fails. `--info` also shows it |
| `-Pbrowser=firefox` | Browser for `browserTest`, `svelteRecordTest` and `svelteVerifyA11y`: `chromium` (default), `firefox` or `webkit` |

Set one for every build in `gradle.properties`:

```properties
svelte.verbose=true
```

## Full example

A `build.gradle.kts` for a real app: pinned Bun, a frontend in another folder, an environment variable the build reads, libraries, and HTTPS in development.

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.gradle.DaisyTheme

svelte {
    frontendDir = layout.projectDirectory.dir("web")
    bunVersion = "1.3.14"
    buildEnv = setOf("PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN")
    dev {
        port = 5174
        https = true
    }
    libraries {
        daisyUi {
            themes(DaisyTheme.Light, DaisyTheme.Dark)
            defaultTheme(DaisyTheme.Light)
            prefersDark(DaisyTheme.Dark)
        }
        lucide()
        routes()
        components()
    }
}
```

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/how-it-works

# How it works

What happens at build time and how each request is answered.

At build time, three tasks run before `processResources`:

1. `svelteInstall` installs dependencies from your lockfile.
2. `svelteBuild` runs your build script.
3. `svelteBundle` copies the output to `ktor-svelte/public/` in your resources, and writes `ktor-svelte/manifest.json` with a hash of every file.

`svelteBundle` leaves out hidden files such as `.env` (but keeps `.well-known`), source maps and symlinks, and warns about any hidden files it skipped. `SvelteSource.Directory` also ignores hidden files and symlinks, but serves source maps. It streams each file through a non-blocking file channel with its exact `Content-Length`, which makes it a good fit for large builds served from a volume.

At run time, `install(Svelte)` adds a catch-all route. Ktor always prefers more specific routes, so yours win. GET and HEAD requests that reach the catch-all are resolved in this order:

| Step | Request | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Path under an API prefix | Not handled, so Ktor returns its normal 404 |
| 2 | Exact file in the manifest | Serve the file |
| 3 | `/about` when `about.html` exists, or `/about/` when `about/index.html` exists | Serve the page |
| 4 | `/about/` when only `about.html` exists, or `/about` when only `about/index.html` exists | 308 redirect to the form that exists, keeping the query string |
| 5 | Missing path under `/_app/`, `/.well-known/` or `/_ktor-svelte/`, or any path with a file extension | 404, never the fallback |
| 6 | Other path, with a fallback page and a request that accepts HTML, or a path matching `paramRoutes` | Serve the fallback with status 200 |
| 7 | Anything else | `404.html` with status 404 if it exists, otherwise a plain 404 |

Because your routes always win, a Ktor `GET /about` hides a prerendered `about.html`. The app warns about every such route at startup, for example `ktor-svelte: the Ktor route GET /about hides the frontend page about.html.` Routes under your API prefixes and routes with parameters are not checked.

Step 4 exists because prerendered pages load assets with relative paths, so serving `about.html` at `/about/` would break them. Every file from the build answers `Range: bytes=...` requests with 206 and `Content-Range`, so videos can seek and downloads can resume. Ranges are always served without `Content-Encoding`, `If-Range` is honoured, and a range past the end of the file answers 416. Other methods on a path that resolves to a page or file, such as a POST to `/about`, answer 405 with `Allow: GET, HEAD, OPTIONS`, and OPTIONS answers 204 with the same header. Paths that resolve to nothing stay 404. In development, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE still go to Vite first.

Step 5 lets SvelteKit recover from stale chunks after a deploy by doing a full page reload.

## Limits

- `adapter-static` only. There is no Node process in production, so `+page.server.ts`, `+server.ts` and form actions are not supported. Ktor is the backend. The [FAQ](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/faq) explains why and what to use instead.
- The app is mounted at the root. `paths.base` is not supported yet.
- Files are served whole or as one byte range. Requests for several ranges at once get the whole file. Very large media still makes the JAR large, so a CDN or object storage is often the better home for it.
- `generateTs` builds on Ktor's OpenAPI support, which Ktor still marks as experimental.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/architecture

# Architecture

How a SvelteKit build ends up in the JAR, and how a request reaches a file. Read this before changing the plugin or the runtime. [How it works](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/how-it-works) has the exact resolution rules.

## Build time

The Gradle plugin turns the frontend into resources of your app. Each step is a cacheable task, wired before `processResources`:

| Step | What it does | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `svelteInstall` | Installs dependencies from the lockfile with the detected package manager | `tasks/SvelteTasks.kt`, `PackageManager.kt` |
| `svelteBuild` | Runs the build script. Its inputs include a fingerprint of the package manager | `tasks/SvelteTasks.kt`, `tasks/ToolFingerprint.kt` |
| `svelteBundle` | Copies the output to `ktor-svelte/public/`, gzips what the adapter did not compress, hashes inline scripts and writes `ktor-svelte/manifest.json` | `tasks/SvelteBundleTask.kt`, `tasks/InlineScripts.kt` |
| `svelteSync` | Writes the frontend library setup and generated files from `svelte { libraries { } }` | `tasks/SvelteSyncTasks.kt`, `libraries/` |

Paths are relative to `ktor-svelte-gradle-plugin/src/main/kotlin/io/github/nijasc/ktor/svelte/gradle/`.

The manifest is the contract between the two halves. It lists every servable file with its size, hash, precompressed variants and, for HTML pages, the hashes of their inline scripts. The runtime never turns a request path into a file path. It only looks paths up in the manifest.

## Request time

`install(Svelte)` adds a catch-all route and a few hooks. Ktor prefers more specific routes, so your own routes always win.

| Step | What it does | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Guards | Origin check, body size, JSON shape limits and rate limits on API paths | `internal/security/RequestGuards.kt`, `JsonShapeLimits.kt`, `RateLimits.kt` |
| Catch-all | Takes GET and HEAD requests that no route of yours answered, and answers 405 for other methods on known pages | `internal/SvelteHandler.kt` |
| Resolution | Maps the path to a manifest entry, a 308 redirect, the SPA fallback or a 404 | `internal/assets/RequestResolver.kt` |
| Response | Sets `Cache-Control`, `ETag` and CSP, picks a precompressed variant, serves byte ranges and injects `publicConfig` | `internal/assets/AssetResponder.kt`, `ByteRanges.kt`, `ConfigInjector.kt` |
| Storage | Opens files from the classpath or from `SvelteSource.Directory` | `internal/assets/AssetStore.kt`, `Manifest.kt` |

Paths are relative to `ktor-svelte-server/src/main/kotlin/io/github/nijasc/ktor/svelte/`. The root package holds only the public API, such as `Svelte.kt` and `SvelteConfig.kt`.

## Development

In development mode the same catch-all sends frontend requests to Vite through `internal/dev/DevProxy.kt`, which uses the JDK `HttpClient` and only serves local clients. Your API routes still answer directly, so the browser talks to one origin.

`generateTs` reads Ktor's OpenAPI model of your routes when the app starts and writes the TypeScript client. That code lives in `internal/typescript/`, and the client templates are TypeScript files under `src/main/resources`. The development-only endpoints, such as the route table and the status page, are in `internal/dev/`.

`svelteDevAll` starts Vite and the app together, waits until both answer, and prints one ready banner. See `tasks/SvelteDevAllTask.kt` and `tasks/ReadyBanner.kt`.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/troubleshooting

# Troubleshooting

Find the message you see, then its cause and fix.

**Start with the doctor**
Run `./gradlew svelteDoctor` first: it checks the frontend setup and lists most problems on this page at once. Add `--fix` and it repairs the ones that need no decision from you: a missing `#api` import, a `tsconfig.json` that does not extend `$app/tsconfig`, `$lib` imports left over from SvelteKit 2, and a `node_modules` folder whose packages lost their files, which it deletes so the next build installs it again. It prints each change as `FIXED`, and everything else stays a finding for you. See [svelteDoctor](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/checks-and-tooling#sveltedoctor).

## At a glance

| You see | Go to |
|---|---|
| The build fails before the frontend is built | [Build](#build) |
| The app does not start | [Startup](#startup) |
| A request answers 403, 413, 429 or 503 | [Requests](#requests) |
| Something is off while `svelteDevAll` runs | [Development](#development) |
| A check, hook or browser test fails | [Checks and tests](#checks-and-tests) |

## Build

### ktor-svelte found no lockfile

- **Cause:** the frontend has no `bun.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `package-lock.json` or `yarn.lock`, so the plugin cannot tell which package manager to use.
- **Fix:** install the dependencies once with your package manager, or set `svelte { packageManager = PackageManager.Bun }`.

### ktor-svelte could not find bun on PATH

- **Cause:** the package manager the lockfile asks for is not installed, or Gradle cannot see it.
- **Fix:** install it and restart the Gradle daemon with `./gradlew --stop` so it picks up the new `PATH`, or set `packageManager` to one you have.
- **Or:** let the plugin download Bun for you with `svelte { bunVersion = "1.3.14" }`. See [Pin Bun](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/gradle#pin-bun).

### ktor-svelte found no HTML files

- **Cause:** the frontend build produced no pages where the plugin looked.
- **Fix:** check that the frontend uses `adapter-static`, and that `svelte { outputDir }` matches the adapter's `pages` option. The default for both is `build`.

### svelte.outputDir must be a path inside svelte.frontendDir

- **Cause:** `outputDir` points outside the frontend folder.
- **Fix:** give it relative to `frontendDir`, such as `outputDir = "build"`.

### ktor-svelte has no setting 'x' in svelte { }

- **Cause:** a Groovy build script assigns a setting that does not exist, usually a typo.
- **Fix:** the message names the closest setting and lists all of them. See [Gradle settings](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/gradle) for what each one does.

### Frontend libraries are out of sync

- **Cause:** `build.gradle.kts` changed the frontend libraries, but `package.json`, the lockfile or the generated files were not updated.
- **Fix:** run `./gradlew svelteSync` and commit the result.

### ktor-svelte generates vite.config.ts, but found your own version

- **Cause:** the plugin needs to own `vite.config.ts` and the hooks files once frontend libraries are on.
- **Fix:** move your own Vite settings to `vite.user.ts`, merge custom hooks by hand, delete those files and run `svelteSync`.

### Generated TypeScript is out of date

- **Cause:** `check` runs `svelteVerifyTs`, which found that a route or DTO changed but the committed client did not.
- **Fix:** run `./gradlew svelteGenerateTs`, or start the app in development mode, and commit the files in `frontend/src/lib/api`.

### ktor-svelte found secret values in the frontend build

- **Cause:** `svelteVerifyLeaks` found the value of a secret environment variable or a `.env` entry in the built files.
- **Fix:** read that value on the server only. A value that is meant to be public belongs in `svelte { buildEnv }`, or gets a name that starts with `PUBLIC_`. See [Secrets in the frontend build](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/runtime-config#secrets-in-the-frontend-build).

### undefined is not an object (evaluating 'ts.sys.readFile')

- **Cause:** the frontend uses TypeScript 7, which SvelteKit 3 cannot load yet. It usually arrives through an automatic dependency update.
- **Fix:** set `"typescript": "^6.0.0"` in `frontend/package.json` and install again.
- **Keep it away:** tell your update bot to ignore major versions of `typescript`.

### Cannot find module 'rolldown/parseAst', or another package that is installed

- **Cause:** the install was cut short: the package's folder exists in `node_modules`, but its files do not, and the package manager still reported success. `./gradlew svelteDoctor` names the packages that lost their files.
- **Fix:** run `./gradlew svelteClean` and install again.
- **If they come back empty:** the package manager's cache is the cause, so clear it with the command `svelteDoctor` prints, such as `bun pm cache rm`, and install once more.

### The frontend build failed with exit code 1

- **Cause:** ktor-svelte hides the package manager and Vite output while it succeeds and prints all of it when it fails, above this message. The real error is there.
- **Fix:** to see the output every time, add `-Psvelte.verbose=true`.

## Startup

### ktor-svelte found no frontend build

- **Cause:** the app runs in production mode, but the JAR has no frontend in it.
- **Fix:** build it with the Gradle plugin and without `-Psvelte.skip=true` or `-Psvelte.dev=true`.
- **During development:** start it with `-Dio.ktor.development=true`, or use `svelteDevAll`, which does that for you.

### ktor-svelte manifest has format version 2, but this runtime reads version 1

- **Cause:** the Gradle plugin and `ktor-svelte-server` have different versions.
- **Fix:** use the same version for both. With `addRuntimeDependency` on, which is the default, the plugin adds the matching runtime for you.

### ContentNegotiation is already installed

- **Cause:** you install `ContentNegotiation` yourself and also list formats in `transport { }`.
- **Fix:** keep one of the two. The same applies to `Compression` and `compression()`.

### RequestBodyLimit is already installed, or RateLimit is already installed

- **Cause:** ktor-svelte installs these plugins for its body and rate limits.
- **Fix:** to use your own, set `maxApiBodySize = null` or `rateLimit { enabled = false }`.

### ktor-svelte will not proxy to this URL because it is not on this machine

- **Cause:** `dev { url }` or `KTOR_SVELTE_DEV_SERVER` points at another host.
- **Fix:** use a loopback address, or set `dev { allowRemote = true }` if you trust that machine.

### Install the Svelte plugin before calling svelte() in routing

- **Cause:** with `routing = SvelteRouting.Manual`, `svelte()` ran before the plugin was installed.
- **Fix:** call `install(Svelte)` before the `routing { }` block that calls `svelte()`.

### errorCodes, currentUser, permissions or preferences is already set

- **Cause:** an app has one enum of error codes, one kind of signed-in user, one enum of permissions and one class of preferences, and one of them was declared twice.
- **Fix:** keep one declaration in `install(Svelte)`.

### The Ktor route GET /about hides the frontend page about.html

- **Cause:** a route in your app answers the same path as a prerendered page, so the page is never served.
- **Fix:** move the route under your API prefix, or rename the page.

## Requests

### 403: Cross-origin API request refused

- **Cause:** the origin check refused a write from another site.
- **Fix:** if that site is yours, such as a separate admin frontend, add it with `allowedOrigins("https://admin.example.com")`.
- **Behind a proxy that changes the host:** install `XForwardedHeaders` so the app sees the host the browser used. See [Security](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/security#api-request-guards).

### 413: Request body is larger than the limit

- **Cause:** API bodies are limited to 1 MiB.
- **Fix:** raise `maxApiBodySize` for apps that accept uploads.

### 400: Request JSON is nested deeper than 64 levels

- **Cause:** the JSON body nests deeper than `maxJsonDepth`, or has a string longer than `maxJsonStringLength`.
- **Fix:** raise the limit if your API really takes such bodies, or set it to `null`. See [Security](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/security#api-request-guards).

### 429: Too Many Requests

- **Cause:** a client sent more than 120 writes to API paths in a minute, or hit a named limit.
- **Behind a proxy:** install `XForwardedHeaders`, or all users share one limit.
- **Fix:** raise `rateLimit { apiWrites = ... }` if your app writes a lot.

### 503 in development: no Vite and no build

- **Cause:** the app runs in development mode, Vite is not running and there is no frontend build.
- **Fix:** start everything with `./gradlew svelteDevAll`, or Vite alone with `./gradlew svelteDev`.

### 403: The dev proxy only answers requests from this machine

- **Cause:** you opened the app from another device while it runs in development mode.
- **Fix:** set `dev { allowRemote = true }` on a network you trust.

### A page shows a blank screen after a deploy

- **Cause:** the browser has an old page that loads chunks which no longer exist. ktor-svelte answers those with 404 on purpose, so SvelteKit reloads the page.
- **Fix:** if it does not reload, check that nothing in front of the app caches HTML: pages are sent with `Cache-Control: no-cache`.

## Development

### The browser logs a WebSocket error for HMR

- **Cause:** without `server.hmr.clientPort` in `vite.config.ts`, Vite's client first tries Ktor's port. Hot reload still works after one error.
- **Fix:** set `server: { hmr: { clientPort: 5173, protocol: 'ws' } }`. Projects from `svelteInit` already set it.

### A port is already in use

- **Cause:** a Vite or app process from an earlier run is still alive, usually because a terminal was killed.
- **Fix:** `svelteDevAll` stops what an earlier `svelteDevAll` left running by itself. For anything else, run `./gradlew --stop`, or stop the process on that port. See [When a port is still in use](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow#when-a-port-is-still-in-use).

### Port 5173, which Vite needs, is in use by another program

- **Cause:** a program `svelteDevAll` did not start holds Vite's port or the debug port, so the task stops before starting anything.
- **Fix:** stop that program, or use another port with `svelte { dev { port = 5174 } }` or `dev { debugPort = ... }`.

### Types do not update after a Kotlin change

- **Cause:** the client is generated when the app starts in development mode with `generateTs = true`.
- **Fix:** with `svelteDevAll`, that happens after every Kotlin change. With separate terminals, restart the app, or run `./gradlew svelteGenerateTs`.

### The browser does not trust the HTTPS certificate in development

- **Cause:** the development certificate authority in `~/.ktor-svelte/dev-https` is not in your trust store yet.
- **Fix:** run the command the first `svelteDevAll` printed, such as `certutil -addstore -user Root` on Windows. In Firefox, import `ca.crt` under Settings, Certificates, Authorities. See [HTTPS in development](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow#https-in-development).

### The console warns with window_fetch_in_load

- **Cause:** an API call in a `load` function does not use SvelteKit's `fetch`.
- **Fix:** use `apiWith(event)`, or pass `{ fetch }` as the last argument. `./gradlew svelteVerifyLoads` finds every such call. See [In load functions](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#in-load-functions).

### The page signs me out after every Kotlin change

- **Cause:** your sessions do not survive a restart, such as with a signing key that is generated at startup.
- **Fix:** read the key from the environment, so it stays the same across restarts. To stop pages from reloading their data after a restart, set `dev { refreshAfterRestart = false }`.

## Checks and tests

### svelteDoctor found problems to fix

- **Cause:** at least one finding is an `ERROR`.
- **Fix:** each line says what to do. `./gradlew svelteDoctor --fix` repairs the ones that need no decision.

### The pre-commit hook already exists and was not written by ktor-svelte

- **Cause:** another tool installed a pre-commit hook, and `svelteGitHooks` never replaces it.
- **Fix:** call `./gradlew formatCheck svelteVerifySync` from that hook yourself, or delete it and run `svelteGitHooks` again.

### Not inside a git repository, so there is nowhere to install a hook

- **Cause:** `svelteGitHooks` ran in a folder that is not a git clone.
- **Fix:** run `git init` first, or run the task in the clone.

### The app did not answer within 60 seconds

- **Cause:** a browser test, `svelteSmokeTest` or `svelteVerifyA11y` started the packaged app, and it did not answer in time or stopped. Usually a variable or a database it needs is missing.
- **Fix:** read the app's output: `build/ktor-svelte/smoke-test.log` for the smoke test, the file in `app.log` in a browser test. Give the app what it needs, or more time with `--start-seconds` for the smoke test.

### The app ignores the port in tests

- **Cause:** the port is passed as the `PORT` variable and as `-port`, and the app reads neither.
- **Fix:** read one of them, as `EngineMain` does with `-port`.

## Still stuck?

Open an [issue](https://github.com/nijasc/ktor-svelte/issues) with the full message, your `install(Svelte)` and `svelte { }` blocks, and the output of `./gradlew svelteDoctor`.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/faq

# FAQ

Questions people ask before and while using ktor-svelte. Each answer is short and links to the page with the details.

## The idea

### Why `adapter-static` and no server-side rendering?

ktor-svelte exists to ship one JVM app. SSR needs a JavaScript runtime that renders every request, so production would need Node next to the JVM, or a JavaScript engine inside it. That means two processes or a slow embedded engine, two places for auth and config, and two things to deploy and monitor. With `adapter-static`, the frontend is plain files, Ktor is the only backend, and the JAR is the whole app.

### What about SEO and the first paint?

Prerender every page whose content is known at build time with `export const prerender = true`. Those pages are real HTML that search engines and slow devices see right away. Pages that depend on data from your API render in the browser, which suits dashboards, admin areas and anything behind a login. A [sitemap and robots.txt](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/endpoints#sitemap-and-robots-txt) are generated for you.

### Can I still add SSR later?

Yes, but not with ktor-svelte. Switch the frontend to `adapter-node`, run it as its own server, and keep Ktor as the API behind it. You lose the single JAR and the same-origin setup, and you need CORS or a proxy.

### Do I need Node in production?

No. The frontend is inside the JAR, and production runs one JVM process. Node or Bun is only needed to build. See [Deployment](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/deployment).

## Writing the app

### How do I load data for a page?

Call your Ktor routes from `load` in `+page.ts` or from the component, through the generated client. `+page.server.ts` and `+server.ts` need a Node server and do not exist here. Write that logic as a Ktor route instead. In a `load` function, use `apiWith(event)` or pass `{ fetch }`. See [In load functions](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/calling-the-api#in-load-functions).

### What replaces form actions?

A Ktor route that receives the form as JSON or form data. Validation errors come back as a 422 that `isValidationError` understands, so the form can show them next to each field. See [Validation](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/validation).

### Does a dynamic route like `/notes/[id]` work?

Yes. Unknown paths get the fallback page, and SvelteKit renders the route in the browser. List patterns in `paramRoutes` to serve the fallback for them even when a request does not accept HTML. See [Ktor settings](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/ktor#serving-the-frontend).

### My Ktor route hides a page. Why?

A route of yours such as `get("/{slug}")` beats the frontend. Keep API routes under your API prefix, `/api` by default. The app logs which route hides which page.

### How do I put pages behind a login?

Either declare [page guards](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/auth#page-guards) for the pages that need a user, or take over routing with `routing = SvelteRouting.Manual` and wrap `svelte()` in `authenticate`. See [Route.svelte()](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/ktor#route-svelte) and [Auth](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/auth).

### How do I keep secrets out of the frontend?

Read them from environment variables on the server, never in `publicConfig`. `svelteVerifyLeaks` fails the build when a secret value ends up in the built files. See [Secrets in the frontend build](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/runtime-config#secrets-in-the-frontend-build).

## Developing

### Which port do I open while developing?

Ktor's, such as `http://localhost:8080`, not Vite's. The [ready banner](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow#the-ready-banner) prints it, and the browser opens it the first time.

### Do I have to restart after a Kotlin change?

No. `svelteDevAll` restarts the app, regenerates the TypeScript client, and open pages reload their data by themselves. See [Hot reload and restart](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow#hot-reload-and-restart).

### How do I debug Kotlin and the frontend?

Start `Dev`, then `Debug app` for Kotlin and `Debug frontend` for the browser, or `Dev and debug` for both. Outside IntelliJ, attach a debugger to `127.0.0.1:5005`. See [Debugging](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow#debugging).

### How do I see why an API call failed?

Open the [dev panel](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow#the-dev-panel) with the **API** button. It lists every call with its status and validation errors, shows the server's exception as an overlay, and can replay a call or copy it as `curl`.

### How do I try the app from my phone during development?

Set `dev { allowRemote = true }`, and only on a network you trust. The phone must also reach Vite's port. See [The dev proxy](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow#the-dev-proxy).

### I need HTTPS locally, for `Secure` cookies or a sign-in provider.

Set `svelte { dev { https = true } }` and trust the development certificate once. See [HTTPS in development](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow#https-in-development).

## Checks and tests

### Which checks run on every build?

`svelteVerifySync` before every frontend build, `svelteVerifyLeaks` before the build goes into the JAR, and `svelteVerifyTs` as part of `check`. The others are yours to add. See [Checks and tooling](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/checks-and-tooling).

### Can I write browser tests in Kotlin?

Yes. A test suite called `browserTest` gets Playwright, the packaged app and an `api` that speaks your own classes. `svelteRecordTest` writes the first test while you click. See [Browser tests](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/browser-tests).

### How do I check accessibility?

While you build a page, with the **Accessibility** section of the dev panel. For every prerendered page, with `./gradlew svelteVerifyA11y`. For pages behind a login, with `page.accessibilityProblems()` in a browser test. See [Accessibility](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/browser-tests#accessibility).

### How do I know my production JAR works before I deploy it?

Run `./gradlew svelteSmokeTest`. It starts the JAR in production mode and requests every prerendered page and the `GET` API routes. See [Smoke test](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/deployment#smoke-test).

## Running in production

### How do I deploy?

Build one JAR with `./gradlew buildFatJar` and run it with `java -jar`, in Docker, on Railway or as a systemd service. See [Deployment](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/deployment).

### What do I need behind nginx or Caddy?

Install `XForwardedHeaders`, send HSTS from the proxy, and do not compress twice. See [Behind a reverse proxy](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/deployment#behind-a-reverse-proxy).

### How do I find out about errors in my users' browsers?

Turn on `frontendErrors()`, and uncaught errors from browsers land in your server log with the page and the request ID. See [Monitoring](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/monitoring#errors-from-the-browser).

### How do I know which version is running?

The startup log names the frontend fingerprint, and `application.buildInfo` has the version and commit. With `publicBuildInfo = true` the browser can read them too. See [Build info](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/monitoring#build-info).

### Is there a health check for my load balancer?

Yes: set `healthEndpoint = true` and point it at `GET /_ktor-svelte/health`. Add your own checks with `healthCheck { }`. See [Health endpoint](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/endpoints#health-endpoint).

### Something is wrong with my setup. Where do I start?

Run `./gradlew svelteDoctor` for the frontend setup and `./gradlew svelteConfig` for the settings in effect. Then see [Troubleshooting](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/troubleshooting).

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/compatibility

# Compatibility

Supported and tested versions of every tool ktor-svelte works with.

| Tool | Supported | Tested with |
|---|---|---|
| Ktor | 3.6 and newer 3.x | 3.6.1 |
| Kotlin | 2.3 and newer | 2.4.21 |
| JVM | 17 and newer | 17, 21 |
| Gradle | Latest 8.x and 9.x | 8.14.6, 9.9.0 |
| SvelteKit | 3.x | 3.1.1 |
| Svelte | 5.57.3 and newer | 5.57.3 |
| Package managers | Bun, pnpm, npm, Yarn | All four build and test an example end to end in CI |

On Gradle 8.x, use Shadow 9.2 or older if you use Shadow. Newer versions need a newer Gradle.

# Upgrading

From 1.0 on, ktor-svelte follows semantic versioning: only a major release can break your build, and patch releases only fix bugs. Before 1.0, a minor release such as 0.8.0 to 0.9.0 could change behaviour. Each release that changes what your app does, or what you need to write, has a guide with the steps to adopt it. The [changelog](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/changelog) links each release to its guide.

To upgrade across several releases, follow the guides in order.

| Release | What changes for you |
|---|---|
| [1.0](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/1.0) | Enum constants use one casing, the deprecated `SvelteSecurityHeaders` alias is removed, and configuration classes lose their public constructors |
| [0.11](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/0.11) | Generated Kotlin moves to `io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte`, and apps serve a generated `sitemap.xml` and `robots.txt` |
| [0.10](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/0.10) | `publicConfig` is inlined into pages, API responses carry a build header, and `svelteDevAll` opens the browser |
| [0.9](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/0.9) | Wrong methods on pages answer 405, JSON request bodies have a nesting limit, and every request gets an `X-Request-Id` |
| [0.8](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/0.8) | API responses of 1 KiB or more are compressed |
| [0.7](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/0.7) | API writes are rate limited per client |
| [0.6](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/0.6) | Security headers, a strict Content-Security-Policy, an origin check and a body size limit |

Releases before 0.6 only added features, so they need no steps.

## Bump the version

The Gradle plugin adds the matching runtime library for you, so one version change upgrades both:

```kotlin
plugins {
    id("io.github.nijasc.ktor-svelte") version "<new version>"
}
```

If you set `addRuntimeDependency = false` and declare `ktor-svelte-server` yourself, bump it to the same version. Then run `./gradlew svelteSync` once, because generated files and frontend library setup can change between releases. If your app uses `generateTs`, also run `./gradlew svelteGenerateTs` and commit the result, because the generated client can change too. Until you do, `check` stops at `svelteVerifyTs` and names the files that are out of date.

Afterwards, `./gradlew svelteConfig` shows every setting with its new default and suggests what to turn on, so you notice new options. See [Review your configuration](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/gradle#review-your-configuration).

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/releases/1.0

# ktor-svelte 1.0

1.0 adds no headline feature. It is the release where the API stops moving, and where everything that was already there got tested harder than before.

## What 1.0 promises

From this release on, ktor-svelte follows semantic versioning:

- a patch release such as 1.0.1 only fixes bugs
- a minor release such as 1.1.0 adds features and keeps your build working
- only a major release can remove or rename something, and it comes with an [upgrade guide](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/)

The promise covers the Kotlin API outside packages named `internal`, and the settings and tasks of the Gradle plugin.

## What changed on the way

**The API was cleaned up one last time.** Enum constants use one casing, a deprecated alias is gone, and classes that were public by accident are closed. Most apps compile unchanged. The [upgrade guide for 1.0](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/1.0) lists every step.

**A third example app.** [`examples/showcase`](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/examples#showcase) is a team board with sign in, roles, an admin area, a database with migrations, file uploads, search, paging, themes and two languages. Building it and clicking through it is how most of the bugs below were found.

**Bugs fixed.** Each of these was found by using ktor-svelte the way an app does, not by reading its code:

- A nullable property such as `val assignee: UserRef?` was typed as a second TypeScript type `UserRef2`. It is `UserRef | null` now.
- `call.messages` and `call.theme` failed with "i18n is not configured" while the app ran under `svelteDevAll`.
- With `transport { compression() }`, precompressed pages and assets were compressed a second time on every request.
- Text typed into an input with `use:field` before the page became interactive was wiped.
- The dev proxy answered 502 to clients that offer an HTTP/2 upgrade, such as Java's `HttpClient`.
- A compressed request body could unpack far beyond `maxApiBodySize`. The limit now also covers the unpacked size.
- A path with a broken percent escape, and a `Host` header that cannot be parsed, answered 500. They answer 400 now.

**The setup script is more careful.** It does nothing until it has been downloaded completely, and it refuses a version that does not look like one.

## How it was tested

- **End to end.** Every example is built into a JAR and tested over HTTP. For the showcase that covers sessions, cookie flags, roles, uploads, paging, rate limits and data that survives a hard stop.
- **In real browsers.** The showcase JAR is driven by Playwright in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit: forms, uploads, downloads, both languages, themes and the Content-Security-Policy.
- **Accessibility.** Every page of the showcase passes the axe checks for WCAG 2.1 A and AA, in a light and in a dark theme.
- **Development mode.** A test starts `svelteDevAll`, edits a Svelte file and a Kotlin file, and checks that the open page updates and the app restarts.
- **Every package manager.** Bun, npm, pnpm and Yarn each install, build and test an example in CI.
- **Upgrades.** A project created by release 0.12.0 is switched to the current code and has to build, on every change.
- **A pentest.** About 150 hand-written requests against the showcase JAR: path traversal, redirects, the Host header, the origin check, request bodies, injection, access control, session cookies and sign in. The three weaknesses it found are in the list above. The [security page](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/security) says what ktor-svelte protects and what it leaves to you.
- **Static analysis.** CodeQL scans the Kotlin, the TypeScript and the workflows on every pull request.

## If you skipped 0.12

0.12 made IntelliJ a better place to work:

- Compiler errors and browser stack traces in the `svelteDevAll` console are links to the file and line.
- New run configurations debug the frontend, and start the app with a debugger attached in one click.
- New projects get their run configurations and live templates set up without a second command.

## Upgrading

1. Change the plugin version to `1.0.0`.
2. Run `./gradlew svelteSync`, and `./gradlew svelteGenerateTs` if you use `generateTs`. Commit what changed.
3. If the build does not compile, the [upgrade guide for 1.0](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/1.0) has the step you need.

## Good to know

- The built-in messages for `@JsonSchema` bounds are English. Write your own rule with `check` for other wording.
- SvelteKit 3 does not load TypeScript 7 yet. Stay on TypeScript 6 in your frontend.
- The dev proxy forwards HTTP only. Hot reload still works, because Vite's client connects to Vite directly.
- There is no server-side rendering, by design. The [FAQ](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/faq) explains why and what to use instead.

The full list of changes is in the [changelog](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/changelog).

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/1.0

# Upgrading to 1.0

1.0 is the first release with a stable API. Before the freeze, a few names were made consistent and some classes that were public by accident were closed. Most apps compile without changes. If yours does not, one of the steps below applies.

## Enum constants use one casing

Every enum in ktor-svelte now writes its constants like `SvelteRouting.Automatic`. Two enums still used capitals, so their constants are renamed:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `DevMode.AUTO`, `DevMode.ALWAYS`, `DevMode.NEVER` | `DevMode.Auto`, `DevMode.Always`, `DevMode.Never` |
| `PackageManager.AUTO`, `PackageManager.BUN`, `PackageManager.PNPM`, `PackageManager.NPM`, `PackageManager.YARN` | `PackageManager.Auto`, `PackageManager.Bun`, `PackageManager.Pnpm`, `PackageManager.Npm`, `PackageManager.Yarn` |

In `Application.kt`:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    dev {
        mode = DevMode.Never
    }
}
```

In `build.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.gradle.PackageManager

svelte {
    packageManager = PackageManager.Pnpm
}
```

## SvelteSecurityHeaders is removed

The deprecated alias `SvelteSecurityHeaders` is gone. Use `SvelteSecurityHeadersConfig`, the name it has pointed to since 0.6.1. This only matters if you named the type yourself, for example in a helper function. A `securityHeaders { }` block needs no change.

## Configuration classes cannot be created by hand

`SvelteConfig`, `SvelteCacheConfig`, `SvelteDevConfig`, `SvelteSecurityHeadersConfig`, `SvelteRateLimitConfig`, `SvelteTransportConfig` and `Validator` no longer have a public constructor. ktor-svelte creates them and hands them to your `install(Svelte) { }`, `cache { }` or `validate { }` block, which is the only way they were meant to be used.

The same goes for the Gradle plugin: `DaisyCustomTheme` and `DaisyCustomThemeBuilder` are created by `customTheme(...) { }`, and the `TailwindSpec`, `DaisySpec`, `I18nSpec` and `LibrarySpec` values that tasks carry can be read but not built or copied. `ToolVersionSource` is internal now.

## What 1.0 promises

From 1.0 on, ktor-svelte follows semantic versioning. A patch release only fixes bugs, a minor release adds features without breaking your build, and only a major release can remove or rename something. Anything in a package named `internal` is not part of the API.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/0.11

# Upgrading to 0.11

0.11 renames the package of generated Kotlin and adds two files to production apps. Most apps only need to update imports.

## Generated Kotlin moved to io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte

With frontend libraries on, ktor-svelte generates Kotlin such as `AppTheme`, `LucideIcon`, `Messages` and the `call.theme` and `call.messages` extensions. They now live in `io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte` instead of `ktorsvelte`, so they no longer sit in a top-level package of their own. Update your imports:

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.AppTheme
import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.LucideIcon
import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.messages
```

In IntelliJ, replace `import ktorsvelte.` with `import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.` across the project. To keep the old package instead, set it in `build.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
svelte {
    libraries {
        generatedPackage = "ktorsvelte"
    }
}
```

## sitemap.xml and robots.txt

When your build has no `sitemap.xml` or `robots.txt`, ktor-svelte now serves generated ones: a sitemap of your prerendered pages, and a `robots.txt` that keeps crawlers out of your API. Set `siteUrl` to your public address, put your own files in `frontend/static/`, or turn both off with `sitemap = false`. See [Sitemap and robots.txt](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/endpoints#sitemap-and-robots-txt).

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/0.10

# Upgrading to 0.10

0.10 adds features that change a few responses and the dev loop. Most apps need no changes.

## publicConfig is inlined into pages

When you set `publicConfig`, every page from your build now contains it as `<script type="application/json" id="ktor-svelte-config">`, and pages get their own ETag. The generated `loadPublicConfig()` reads it from there before asking the server.

You are affected only if a test compares page bodies byte for byte, or a cache in front of the app keys on the build hash. Set `inlinePublicConfig = false` to keep pages unchanged. See [Runtime config](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/runtime-config).

## Build header on API responses

API responses now carry `X-Ktor-Svelte-Build` with a short fingerprint of the frontend build, so the generated client can tell when a new version is deployed. Set `buildHeader = false` to leave it out.

## svelteDevAll opens the browser

`svelteDevAll` opens the app in your default browser once, when it is first ready. It never does in CI or without a display. Turn it off in `build.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
svelte {
    dev {
        openBrowser = false
    }
}
```

## Paths under /_ktor-svelte/

Unknown paths under `/_ktor-svelte/` now answer 404 instead of the SPA fallback, because ktor-svelte reserves them for its own endpoints. If your SvelteKit app has a route there, move it.

## Regenerate the client

The generated client gained timeouts, `latest()`, `onNewBuild`, JSDoc from route descriptions and companions for sealed class unions. Start the app once in development, or run `./gradlew svelteGenerateTs`, and commit the updated files under `src/lib/api`.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/0.9

# Upgrading to 0.9

0.9 changes three responses. Most apps need no changes.

## 405 for wrong methods on pages

A POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE to a path that is a page or file of your build, such as `/about`, now answers 405 with `Allow: GET, HEAD, OPTIONS`, instead of 404. OPTIONS answers 204. Paths that resolve to nothing still answer 404.

You are affected if a test or monitor expects 404 for such a request. Update the expected status.

## JSON nesting limit

JSON request bodies on API paths that nest deeper than 64 levels now answer 400. Real payloads rarely nest beyond 10.

If you accept deeply nested documents, raise the limit, or turn it off with `null`:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    maxJsonDepth = 256
}
```

`maxJsonStringLength` can also refuse long strings. It is off by default. See [JSON shape](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/security#api-request-guards).

## Request IDs

Every request now gets an `X-Request-Id` response header, and the generated client sends one with each call. Unhandled errors are logged with the ID, and `ApiError.requestId` carries it in the frontend.

You are affected only if you install Ktor's `CallId` yourself. ktor-svelte then uses your setup and does not install its own. To turn the feature off, set `requestIds = false`.

## Regenerate the client

The generated client now sends request IDs. Start the app once in development, or run `./gradlew svelteGenerateTs`, and commit the updated files under `src/lib/api`.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/0.8

# Upgrading to 0.8

0.8 compresses API responses of 1 KiB or more with gzip or deflate, and with zstd when its Ktor module is on the classpath.

## Apps that install Ktor's Compression themselves

Nothing changes. When `Compression` is already installed, ktor-svelte leaves it alone and uses your configuration. To let ktor-svelte handle API paths instead, remove your installation.

To keep API responses uncompressed, turn it off:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    apiCompression = false
}
```

## Endpoints that return secrets

A response that mixes a secret, such as an API key, with text an attacker can choose can leak the secret through its compressed size. If you have such an endpoint, turn `apiCompression` off, or install `Compression` yourself with a condition that skips that route. See [API compression](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/transport#api-compression).

## Proxies and tests

Clients that send `Accept-Encoding` now get a compressed body with `Content-Encoding`. Browsers and Ktor's client handle this on their own. Tests that read raw bytes, or proxies that rewrite bodies, may need to decompress first or send no `Accept-Encoding`.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/0.7

# Upgrading to 0.7

0.7 rate limits writes to your API by default. Each client may send 120 requests per minute with any method except GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE. More answer 429 with `Retry-After`.

## Behind a reverse proxy

Clients are told apart by `call.request.origin.remoteHost`. Without forwarded headers, every request seems to come from the proxy, so all users share one budget. Install Ktor's `XForwardedHeaders` or `ForwardedHeaders` before upgrading.

## Apps with heavy write traffic

Raise the default, or turn it off for one deployment:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    rateLimit {
        apiWrites = 600
    }
}
```

`rateLimit { enabled = false }` turns it off completely.

## Apps that install Ktor's RateLimit themselves

ktor-svelte now installs Ktor's `RateLimit` plugin, and Ktor allows it only once. Move your limits into `rateLimit { limit(...) }` and keep wrapping routes with `rateLimit(RateLimitName("..."))`:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    rateLimit {
        limit("login", requests = 5, per = 1.minutes)
    }
}

routing {
    rateLimit(RateLimitName("login")) {
        post("/api/login") { /* ... */ }
    }
}
```

Or set `rateLimit { enabled = false }` and keep your own installation.

## Tests

Tests that send many writes in a row can now get 429. Raise `apiWrites` in the test setup, or turn the limit off there. See [Rate limit](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/security#api-request-guards).

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/0.6

# Upgrading to 0.6

0.6 turns on four protections by default. Most apps need no changes. Check each section that applies to you.

## Security headers and CSP

Every response now gets `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and `Referrer-Policy`, and every page from your build gets a strict `Content-Security-Policy` built from its own inline scripts.

You are affected if your pages load scripts, images, fonts or API calls from another origin, such as analytics or a CDN, or if another site embeds your app in a frame. The browser console shows each blocked request.

Allow what you need:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    securityHeaders {
        allowCspSources("script-src", "https://plausible.io")
        allowCspSources("connect-src", "https://plausible.io")
        frameOptions = "SAMEORIGIN"
    }
}
```

`automaticContentSecurityPolicy = false` drops the CSP and keeps the other headers. See [Security headers](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/security#security-headers).

## Origin check

Writes to API paths, meaning every method except GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE, from a browser on another site now answer 403.

You are affected if a frontend on another origin, such as a separate admin app, calls your API. List it:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    allowedOrigins("https://admin.example.com")
}
```

Behind a reverse proxy that changes the `Host` header, install Ktor's `XForwardedHeaders` or `ForwardedHeaders`, so the check compares against the public host. Server-to-server calls and tests without an `Origin` header are not affected.

## Body size limit

Request bodies on API paths larger than 1 MiB now answer 413.

You are affected if you accept uploads or large imports. Raise the limit, or remove it with `null`:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    maxApiBodySize = 50L * 1024 * 1024
}
```

If you installed Ktor's `RequestBodyLimit` yourself, keep it only with `maxApiBodySize = null`, because both cannot be installed together.

## Generated validation

The generated client now has a `validate()` per request type, built from your schema constraints. Nothing changes for existing calls. See [Validation](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/validation) to use it in forms.
